import com.pg85.otg.config.io.SettingsMap;
import com.pg85.otg.config.settingtype.Setting;
import com.pg85.otg.config.settingtype.Settings;
import com.pg85.otg.config.settings.ConfigSection;
import com.pg85.otg.constants.Constants;
import lombok.Builder;
import lombok.Getter;

@Builder
@Getter
public class TerrainSettings extends ConfigSection {
    private final double fractureHorizontal;
    private final double fractureVertical;
    private final int worldHeightCap;
    private final int worldHeightScale;
    private final boolean betterSnowFall;
    private final int waterLevelMax;
    private final int waterLevelMin;
    private final int carverLavaBlockHeight;
    private final boolean useVanillaTerrain;
    private final double continentalScale;
    private final double erosionScale;
    private final double weirdnessScale;
    private final double baseHeightFraction;
    private final double biomeHeightWeight;
    private final double falloffSteepness;
    private final double noiseAmplitude;

    public static final Setting<Boolean> BETTER_SNOW_FALL = Settings.booleanSetting(
            "BetterSnowFall", false,
            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).isBetterSnowFall(),
            "When set to false, 1 layer of snow falls on the highest block only.",
            "When set to true, the number of layers (1-8) is dependent on biome temperature.",
            "Higher altitudes have lower temperatures, so snow becomes deeper higher up.",
            "Also causes snow to fall through leaves, leaves can carry 3 layers while the rest falls through."
    );
    public static final Setting<Integer> WORLD_HEIGHT_SCALE_BITS = Settings.intSetting(
            "WorldHeightScaleBits", 8, 5, 9,
            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).getWorldHeightScale(),
            "The height scale of the world. Increasing this by one doubles the terrain height of the world,",
            "substracting one halves the terrain height. Values must be between 5 and 9, inclusive.",
            "For 1.18+ worlds with 384 height, use 8 (256) or 9 (512)."
    );
    public static final Setting<Integer> WORLD_HEIGHT_CAP_BITS = Settings.intSetting(
            "WorldHeightCapBits", 9, 5, 9,
            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).getWorldHeightCap(),
            "The height cap of the world. A cap of 7 will make sure that there is no terrain above 128 (y=2^7). Near this cap less and less terrain generates with no terrain above this cap.",
            "Values must be between 5 and 9 (inclusive), and may not be lower that WorldHeightScaleBits.",
            "For 1.18+ worlds with 384 height, use 9 (512)."
    );
    public static final Setting<Integer> WATER_LEVEL_MAX = Settings.intSetting(
            "WaterLevelMax", 63, Constants.WORLD_START_MIN_Y, Constants.WORLD_END_MAX_Y,
            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).getWaterLevelMax(),
            "Set water level. Every empty block under this level down to min will be fill water or another block from WaterBlock."
    );
    public static final Setting<Integer> WATER_LEVEL_MIN = Settings.intSetting(
            "WaterLevelMin", 0, Constants.WORLD_START_MIN_Y, Constants.WORLD_END_MAX_Y,
            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).getWaterLevelMin(),
            "Set water level. Every empty block over this level up to max will be fill water or another block from WaterBlock."
    );
    public static final Setting<Integer> CARVER_LAVA_BLOCK_HEIGHT = Settings.intSetting(
            "CarverLavaBlockHeight", 10, Constants.WORLD_START_MIN_Y, Constants.WORLD_END_MAX_Y,
            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).getCarverLavaBlockHeight(),
            "All air blocks are replaced to CarverLavaBlock from world bottom up to CarverLavaBlockHeight.",
            "For example, vanilla replaces air in caves with lava up to Y10.",
            "Defaults to: 10"
    );
    public static final Setting<Boolean> USE_VANILLA_TERRAIN = Settings.booleanSetting(
            "UseVanillaTerrain", false,
            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).isUseVanillaTerrain(),
            "When true, uses configurable terrain constants (ContinentalScale, BaseHeightFraction, etc.)",
            "instead of the hardcoded OTG defaults. Allows tuning terrain shape to behave more like vanilla."
    );
    public static final Setting<Double> CONTINENTAL_SCALE = Settings.doubleSetting(
            "ContinentalScale", 0.2, 0.0, 10.0,
            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).getContinentalScale(),
            "Weight of vanilla continentalness noise in terrain height (UseVanillaTerrain only).",
            "Continentalness controls the land/ocean split at the largest scale.",
            "Higher values = more dramatic continent/ocean height differences."
    );
    public static final Setting<Double> EROSION_SCALE = Settings.doubleSetting(
            "ErosionScale", 0.1, 0.0, 10.0,
            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).getErosionScale(),
            "Weight of vanilla erosion noise in terrain height (UseVanillaTerrain only).",
            "Erosion controls the flatness vs steepness of terrain.",
            "Higher values = more dramatic flat-to-steep transitions."
    );
    public static final Setting<Double> WEIRDNESS_SCALE = Settings.doubleSetting(
            "WeirdnessScale", 0.05, 0.0, 10.0,
            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).getWeirdnessScale(),
            "Weight of vanilla weirdness (ridges) noise in terrain height (UseVanillaTerrain only).",
            "Weirdness adds local variation — hills, bumps, and valleys within a biome region.",
            "Higher values = more local terrain variation."
    );
    public static final Setting<Double> BASE_HEIGHT_FRACTION = Settings.doubleSetting(
            "BaseHeightFraction", 0.46875, 0.0, 1.0,
            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).getBaseHeightFraction(),
            "Where the terrain surface sits as a fraction of world height when all noise values are 0.",
            "0.47 = surface roughly at half world height (default).",
            "0.25 = low surface with lots of sky, 0.75 = high surface with deep underground."
    );
    public static final Setting<Double> BIOME_HEIGHT_WEIGHT = Settings.doubleSetting(
            "BiomeHeightWeight", 0.125, 0.0, 1.0,
            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).getBiomeHeightWeight(),
            "How much OTG biome height config shifts the terrain surface (UseVanillaTerrain only).",
            "0 = all biomes at same baseline, 0.125 = default.",
            "Higher values create more dramatic height differences between biomes."
    );
    public static final Setting<Double> FALLOFF_STEEPNESS = Settings.doubleSetting(
            "FalloffSteepness", 6.0, 0.1, 100.0,
            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).getFalloffSteepness(),
            "Controls how sharply terrain transitions from solid to air.",
            "Higher values = thinner transition zone = sharper terrain edges.",
            "Lower values = thicker transition zone = smoother, more blobby terrain.",
            "Default 6.0 produces ~80 block transition at default biome volatility (0.3)."
    );
    public static final Setting<Double> NOISE_AMPLITUDE = Settings.doubleSetting(
            "NoiseAmplitude", 1.0, 0.0, 1000.0,
            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).getNoiseAmplitude(),
            "Global multiplier for terrain noise contribution.",
            "Scales the effect of Volatility1/Volatility2 from all biomes uniformly.",
            "1.0 = noise at face value, higher = more chaotic terrain, 0 = falloff-only terrain."
    );
    public static final Setting<Double> FRACTURE_HORIZONTAL = Settings.doubleSetting(
            "FractureHorizontal", 0, -500, 500,
            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).getFractureHorizontal(),
            "Can increase (values greater than 0) or decrease (values less than 0) how much the landscape is fractured horizontally.",
            "Values less than 0 will 'relax' the terrain, leading to more gradual and smoother height transitions."
    );
    public static final Setting<Double> FRACTURE_VERTICAL = Settings.doubleSetting(
            "FractureVertical", 0, -500, 500,
            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).getFractureVertical(),
            "Can increase (values greater than 0) or decrease (values less than 0) how much the landscape is fractured vertically.",
            "Values above 0 will lead to large cliffs/overhangs, floating islands, and/or a cavern world depending on other settings.",
            "Values less than 0 will make terrain volatility more 'spiky' but lessen the likelihood of overhangs and floating terrain."
    );

    public static TerrainSettings getTerrainSettings(SettingsMap reader) {
        var builder = builder();

        builder.fractureHorizontal(reader.getSetting(FRACTURE_HORIZONTAL));
        builder.fractureVertical(reader.getSetting(FRACTURE_VERTICAL));
        builder.worldHeightCap(1 << reader.getSetting(WORLD_HEIGHT_CAP_BITS));
        builder.worldHeightScale(1 << reader.getSetting(WORLD_HEIGHT_SCALE_BITS));
        builder.betterSnowFall(reader.getSetting(BETTER_SNOW_FALL));
        builder.waterLevelMax(reader.getSetting(WATER_LEVEL_MAX));
        builder.waterLevelMin(reader.getSetting(WATER_LEVEL_MIN));
        builder.carverLavaBlockHeight(reader.getSetting(CARVER_LAVA_BLOCK_HEIGHT));
        builder.useVanillaTerrain(reader.getSetting(USE_VANILLA_TERRAIN));
        builder.continentalScale(reader.getSetting(CONTINENTAL_SCALE));
        builder.erosionScale(reader.getSetting(EROSION_SCALE));
        builder.weirdnessScale(reader.getSetting(WEIRDNESS_SCALE));
        builder.baseHeightFraction(reader.getSetting(BASE_HEIGHT_FRACTION));
        builder.biomeHeightWeight(reader.getSetting(BIOME_HEIGHT_WEIGHT));
        builder.falloffSteepness(reader.getSetting(FALLOFF_STEEPNESS));
        builder.noiseAmplitude(reader.getSetting(NOISE_AMPLITUDE));

        int configVersion = reader.getVersion();
        if (configVersion < 2) {
            // In older configs, the values were stored as negative values and then converted
            // to positive values in the getter. This is no longer necessary.
            builder.fractureHorizontal(builder.fractureHorizontal < 0.0D
                    ? 1.0D / (Math.abs(builder.fractureHorizontal) + 1.0D)
                    : builder.fractureHorizontal + 1.0D);
            builder.fractureVertical(builder.fractureVertical < 0.0D
                    ? 1.0D / (Math.abs(builder.fractureVertical) + 1.0D)
                    : builder.fractureVertical + 1.0D);
        }

        return builder.fixSettings().build();
    }

    @Override
    public String getSectionName() {
        return "Terrain Settings";
    }

    public static class TerrainSettingsBuilder {
        public TerrainSettingsBuilder fixSettings() {
            checkWaterLevelMax();
            checkFractionHorizontal();
            checkFractionVertical();
            return this;
        }
        private void checkWaterLevelMax() {
            waterLevelMax = Math.max(waterLevelMax, waterLevelMin);
        }
        private void checkFractionHorizontal() {
            if (fractureHorizontal < 0) {
                fractureHorizontal = 1.0D / Math.abs(fractureHorizontal);
            }
        }
        private void checkFractionVertical() {
            if (fractureVertical < 0) {
                fractureVertical = 1.0D / Math.abs(fractureVertical);
            }
        }
    }
}

- Run `carveWithNoise()` (for separate cave control or debugging)
- But wait, this means we'd double-carve (once from finalDensity in terrain generation, once from carveWithNoise)

Looking at the code:
- In `fillFromNoise()`: `randomState.router().finalDensity()` is used for terrain
- In `carveWithNoise()`: `caveRandomState.router().finalDensity()` is used for carving

The `caveRandomState` is created with a different seed in `initCaveComponents()`. So `finalDensity()` from the cave random state will produce different cave patterns than the terrain random state.

So if `UseVanillaCaves: false`, the intent is: use vanilla terrain but re-carve with the cave random state. This could be useful for:
- Different cave patterns from terrain
- OTG-controlled cave settings applied on top of vanilla terrain

### Key method: `populateNoise(...)` (lines 456-688)
This is the method called from `SharedOTGChunkGenerator.fillFromNoise()`:
```java
public void populateNoise(
    OTGWorldInfo worldHeight,
    ChunkBuffer buffer,
    ChunkCoordinate chunkCoord,
    ObjectList<JigsawStructureData> structures,
    Random random
)
```
Phases:
1. **Phase 1**: Biome lookup -- gets biomes for entire chunk, caches `BiomeSettings`.
2. **Phase 2**: Noise column init -- samples terrain noise via `getNoiseColumn()` (uses `NoiseCache` backed by `generateNoiseColumn()`).
3. **Phase 3**: Block placement -- trilinear interpolation of noise columns, density shaping with jigsaw structure influence, stone/water block placement.
4. **Phase 4**: Surface & ground control -- `doSurfaceAndGroundControl()` runs `SurfaceAndGroundControl` per column.

### Other key methods:
- `generateNoiseColumn(...)` (lines 252-452): If `UseVanillaTerrain` is enabled, uses the `vanillaDensityProvider` (wraps vanilla `DensityFunction.finalDensity()`). Otherwise runs the full OTG noise model with biome-weighted height/volatility blending and falloff.
- `carve(ChunkBuffer, long, BitSet, boolean, boolean)` (lines 690-737): Delegates to `CaveCarver` and `RavineCarver` for OTG's own carvers.

## Summary: `fillFromNoise` call chain

```
SharedOTGChunkGenerator.fillFromNoise(blender, randomState, structureManager, chunkAccess)
  |
  +---> createChunkBuffer(chunkAccess)                  [abstract, implemented by platform]
  +---> internalGenerator.populateNoise(otgWorldInfo, buffer, chunkCoord, structures, random)
  |       |
  |       +---> cachedBiomeProvider.getBiomesForChunk(chunkCoord)
  |       +---> generateNoiseColumn(...) for 4x5 noise cells (trilinear interpolation)
  |       |       +---> [if UseVanillaTerrain] vanillaDensityProvider.compute(...)
  |       |       +---> [else] sampleNoise(...) with biome-weighted parameters
  |       +---> setBlock(...) for stone/water placement
  |       +---> doSurfaceAndGroundControl(...) for surface/ground block replacement
  |
  +---> [if modern caves + not (vanilla terrain AND vanilla caves)]
  |       carveWithNoise(blender, randomState, structureManager, chunkAccess, buffer)
  |           +---> caveRandomState.router().finalDensity() computed per block
  |           +---> surface suppression and breakthrough logic
  |
  +---> return CompletableFuture.completedFuture(chunkAccess)
```

**Key architectural insight:** The vanilla `NoiseBasedChunkGenerator` is used only as a **delegate for carver operations** (the `horribleDelegateForCarvers` field). OTG generates all terrain via `OTGChunkGenerator.populateNoise()`, using its own noise model, and only hands off to vanilla for the cave carving pass when `isUseModernCaves()` is enabled.

    private void handleOTGCarvers(long seed, ChunkAccess chunkAccess) {
        IBiome biome = this.internalGenerator.getCachedBiomeProvider().getNoiseBiome(chunkAccess.getPos().x << 2, chunkAccess.getPos().z << 2);
        BiomeGenerationSettings biomegenerationsettings = getBiomeGenerationSettings(biome);
        Iterable<Holder<ConfiguredWorldCarver<?>>> iterable = biomegenerationsettings.getCarvers();

        List<String> defaultCaves = Arrays.asList("minecraft:cave", "minecraft:underwater_cave", "minecraft:nether_cave");
        boolean cavesEnabled = this.preset.getConfig().getCarverSettings().isCavesEnabled();
        if (cavesEnabled) {
            for (Holder<ConfiguredWorldCarver<?>> carver : iterable) {
                if (defaultCaves.stream().noneMatch(
                        b -> b.equalsIgnoreCase(carver.unwrapKey().map(Objects::toString).orElse(""))
                )) {
                    cavesEnabled = false;
                    break;
                }
            }
        }

        List<String> defaultRavines = Arrays.asList("minecraft:canyon", "minecraft:underwater_canyon");
        boolean ravinesEnabled = this.preset.getConfig().getCarverSettings().isRavinesEnabled();
        if (ravinesEnabled) {
            for (Holder<ConfiguredWorldCarver<?>> carver : iterable) {
                if (defaultRavines.stream().noneMatch(
                        b -> b.equalsIgnoreCase(carver.unwrapKey().map(Objects::toString).orElse(""))
                )) {
                    ravinesEnabled = false;
                    break;
                }
            }
        }

        ChunkBuffer chunkBuffer = createChunkBuffer(chunkAccess);
        CarvingMask carvingMask = ((ProtoChunk) chunkAccess).getOrCreateCarvingMask();
        BitSet bitSet = BitSet.valueOf(carvingMask.toArray());
        internalGenerator.carve(
                chunkBuffer,
                seed,
                bitSet,
                cavesEnabled,
                ravinesEnabled
        );
    }

    private NoiseChunk createNoiseChunk(ChunkAccess chunkAccess, StructureManager structureManager, Blender blender, RandomState randomState) {

    }

**Tool Call: Users\dylan\Desktop\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\platforms\shared\src\main\java\com\pg85\otg\shared\registry\OTGRegistryHelper.java**

    public static void loadOTGPresets(
            List<RegistryDataLoader.Loader<?>> loaders,
            ChunkGeneratorFactory chunkGeneratorFactory,
            Function<LocalMaterialData, BlockState> toBlockState
    ) {
        OTGLog.info("Registering the following OTG presets: {}", OTG.getEngine().getDimensionPresetLoader().getAllDimensionPresets());

        // Check if biome registry is available (may not be in world creation flow)
        if (getRegistry(loaders, Registries.BIOME) != null) {
            registerBiomes(loaders);
        } else {
            OTGLog.info("Biome registry not available, skipping biome registration");
        }

        HashMap<DimensionPreset, ResourceKey<DimensionType>> dimensionTypes = null;
        try {
            dimensionTypes = registerDimensionTypes(loaders);
        } catch (Exception e) {
            OTGLog.warn("Could not register dimension types: {}", e.getMessage());
        }

        if (dimensionTypes != null) {
            for (DimensionPreset preset : dimensionTypes.keySet()) {
                try {
                    registerNoiseGenSettings(preset, loaders, toBlockState);
                } catch (Exception e) {
                    OTGLog.warn("Could not register noise gen settings for {}: {}", preset.getRegistryName(), e.getMessage());
                }
            }

            WritableRegistry<WorldPreset> worldPresets = getRegistry(loaders, Registries.WORLD_PRESET);
            if (worldPresets != null) {
                for (DimensionPreset preset : dimensionTypes.keySet()) {
                    if (!preset.getConfig().getPresetInfo().isSelectableInWorldCreation()) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    OTGLog.info("Registering world preset: {}", dimensionTypes.get(preset).location());
                    Map<ResourceKey<LevelStem>, LevelStem> levelStems = createLevelStems(preset, loaders, chunkGeneratorFactory);
                    registerWorldPresets(preset, worldPresets, levelStems);
                }
            }
        }

        // Always try to register YAML WorldPresets if the registry is available
        WritableRegistry<WorldPreset> wpReg = getRegistry(loaders, Registries.WORLD_PRESET);
        if (wpReg != null) {
            List<WorldPresetConfig> worldPresetConfigs = WorldPresetConfigLoader.loadAll(
                OTG.getEngine().getOTGRootFolder());
            if (!worldPresetConfigs.isEmpty()) {
                Map<String, DimensionPreset> presetMap = new HashMap<>();
                for (DimensionPreset p : OTG.getEngine().getDimensionPresetLoader().getAllDimensionPresets()) {
                    presetMap.put(p.getFolderName(), p);
                }
                WorldPresetRegistrar.register(worldPresetConfigs, presetMap, loaders, chunkGeneratorFactory);
            }

            // After all OTG presets are registered, add them to WorldPresetTags.NORMAL and EXTENDED
            // so they appear in the world creation GUI (MC 1.21.5+ filters by these tags).
            addOTGPresetsToWorldPresetTags(wpReg);
        } else {
            OTGLog.warn("World preset registry not available, skipping YAML preset registration");
        }
    }

    private static void addOTGPresetsToWorldPresetTags(WritableRegistry<WorldPreset> registry) {
        // WARNING: Do NOT call registry.get(TagKey) here — MappedRegistry.freeze() hasn't been
        // called yet, so allTags is still TagSet.unbound() and get(TagKey) would throw.
        // Use registry.listElements() + bindTag() instead (bindTag uses frozenTags, not allTags).

        List<Holder<WorldPreset>> allPresets = new ArrayList<>();
        registry.listElements().forEach(ref -> allPresets.add(ref));
        if (allPresets.isEmpty()) return;

        registry.bindTag(WorldPresetTags.NORMAL, allPresets);
        registry.bindTag(WorldPresetTags.EXTENDED, allPresets);
        OTGLog.info("Bound all {} world presets to WorldPresetTags.NORMAL and EXTENDED", allPresets.size());
    }
}

@Getter
public class OTGNeoForgeChunkGenerator extends SharedOTGChunkGenerator {

    public static final MapCodec<OTGNeoForgeChunkGenerator> CODEC =
            RecordCodecBuilder.mapCodec(instance ->
                    instance.group(
                            OTGNeoForgeBiomeProvider.CODEC.forGetter(OTGNeoForgeChunkGenerator::getBiomeSource),
                            NoiseGeneratorSettings.CODEC.fieldOf("settings").forGetter(OTGNeoForgeChunkGenerator::getSettings)
                    ).apply(instance, instance.stable(OTGNeoForgeChunkGenerator::createFromCodec)));

    private final OTGNeoForgeBiomeProvider biomeSource;
    private final SharedShadowChunkGenerator shadowChunkGenerator;

    public static OTGNeoForgeChunkGenerator createFromCodec(
            OTGNeoForgeBiomeProvider biomeSource, Holder<NoiseGeneratorSettings> settings
    ) {
        return new OTGNeoForgeChunkGenerator(biomeSource, settings, null);
    }

    public OTGNeoForgeChunkGenerator(
            OTGNeoForgeBiomeProvider biomeSource, Holder<NoiseGeneratorSettings> settings, Registry<Biome> biomeRegistry
    ) {
        super(biomeSource, settings, biomeRegistry);
        this.biomeSource = biomeSource;
        this.shadowChunkGenerator = new SharedShadowChunkGenerator();
    }

    @Override
    protected MapCodec<? extends ChunkGenerator> codec() {
        return CODEC;
    }

    @Override
    protected SharedWorldGenRegion createWorldGenRegion(
            String presetFolderName, WorldGenLevel worldGenLevel, ChunkAccess chunkAccess) {
        return new NeoForgeWorldGenRegion(
                presetFolderName,
                com.pg85.otg.OTG.getEngine().getPluginConfig(),
                this.getPreset().getConfig(),
                this.getOtgWorldInfo(),
                worldGenLevel,
                chunkAccess,
                this
        );
    }

    @Override
    protected ChunkBuffer createChunkBuffer(ChunkAccess chunkAccess) {
        return new SharedChunkBuffer(chunkAccess);
    }

    @Override
    protected BiomeGenerationSettings getBiomeGenerationSettings(IBiome biome) {
        return ((SharedBiome) biome).getBiome().getGenerationSettings();
    }

    @Override
    public Boolean checkHasVanillaStructureWithoutLoading(ServerLevel level, ChunkCoordinate chunkCoord) {
        return this.shadowChunkGenerator.checkHasVanillaStructureWithoutLoading(
                level, chunkCoord, this.getInternalGenerator().getCachedBiomeProvider(), false);
    }

    @Override
    public int getHighestBlockYInUnloadedChunk(int x, int z, boolean findSolid, boolean findLiquid, boolean ignoreLiquid, boolean ignoreSnow) {
        return this.shadowChunkGenerator.getHighestBlockYInUnloadedChunk(
                this.getServerLevel(), this, this.getOtgWorldInfo(), x, z, findSolid, findLiquid, ignoreLiquid, ignoreSnow);
    }

    @Override
    public LocalMaterialData getMaterialInUnloadedChunk(int x, int y, int z) {
        return this.shadowChunkGenerator.getMaterialInUnloadedChunk(
                this.getServerLevel(), this, this.getOtgWorldInfo(), x, y, z);
    }

## Analysis: The OTG `.bc` (Biome Config) File Format

### Overview

`.bc` files are OTG's biome configuration format. They use a simplified INI/properties style with `#` line comments and `Key: Value` pairs. Some keys use functional-call syntax (e.g. `Ore(...)`, `Registry(...)`) for the resource queue. Files use Windows-style `\r\n` line endings.

### Structural Sections

The files are organized into clearly marked ASCII-box-art sections. Not all biomes define all sections -- **missing sections/keys fall back to template defaults** (inherited from `templates/tag*.bc` files matched by `BiomeDictTags`).

Here is the complete key catalog observed across all files:

---

#### 1. Biome Identity

| Key | Type | Description | Example |
|-----|------|-------------|---------|
| `TemplateForBiome` | bool | If `true`, this file is a template base (not instantiated as a biome). Templates define default values that concrete biomes inherit based on tag matching. | `false` / `true` |
| `BiomeDictTags` | CSV tags | Dictionary tags used for template matching and biome placement logic. `OVERWORLD` is always present for surface biomes. | `PLAINS, OVERWORLD` |
| `BiomeCategory` | string | The biome's terrain category -- determines which `templates/tag*.bc` it inherits from. | `plains`, `ocean`, `forest`, `desert`, `icy`, `mountain`, `swamp`, `jungle`, etc. |

**Template inheritance:** A biome with `BiomeCategory: plains` will automatically inherit all undefined keys from `templates/tagPlains.bc`. If `BiomeCategory: icy` and tags include `SNOWY`, it may also inherit from `templates/Snowy/tagPlainsSnowy.bc` (snowy variant templates exist for each category).

---

#### 2. Biome Placement (Biome Distribution)

| Key | Type | Description | Example |
|-----|------|-------------|---------|
| `BiomeSize` | int | Controls the size of biome regions on the map. Higher = larger regions. Typically 4-5. | `5` |
| `BiomeRarity` | int | Relative rarity in biome selection (0-100). Higher = rarer. 100 = extremely common. | `30` (Plains), `100` (Ocean), `9` (Swamp) |
| `BiomeColor` | hex | Color used for the biome in OTG's minimap/visualizer. | `0x8DB360` |

---

#### 3. Isle Biomes (Sub-biome Embedding)

| Key | Type | Description | Example |
|-----|------|-------------|---------|
| `IsleInBiome` | CSV biome names | List of biomes that can spawn as "islands" inside this biome. Empty = none. | `Plains`, `Snowy Slopes, Grove` |
| `BiomeSizeWhenIsle` | int | Size when this biome spawns as an isle inside another biome. | `6` |
| `BiomeRarityWhenIsle` | int | Rarity when spawning as an isle. | `97` |

---

#### 4. Border Biomes

| Key | Type | Description | Example |
|-----|------|-------------|---------|
| `BiomeIsBorder` | CSV biome names | List of biomes this biome can appear as a border for. | `Mesa` (Desert borders Mesa) |
| `OnlyBorderNear` | CSV biome names | Only spawn as border near these biomes. | (usually empty) |
| `NotBorderNear` | CSV biome names | Never spawn as a border near these biomes. Used for climate separation. | `Cold Ocean, Deep Cold Ocean, ... Snowy Tundra` (Desert) |
| `BiomeSizeWhenBorder` | int | Size when acting as a border biome. | `8` |

---

#### 5. Terrain Height and Volatility

This is the most complex and important section for terrain shape:

| Key | Type | Description | Example |
|-----|------|-------------|---------|
| `BiomeHeight` | float | Base terrain height. 0 = sea level, negative = below sea level, positive = above. | `0.25` (Plains), `-1.0` (Ocean), `1.65` (Jagged Peaks) |
| `BiomeVolatility` | float | Overall terrain roughness/variability. | `0.2` (Plains), `0.05` (Swamp), `1.35` (Jagged Peaks) |
| `SmoothRadius` | int | Radius for terrain smoothing passes. Higher = smoother. | `6` (Plains), `8` (Ocean/Swamp), `3` (Jagged Peaks) |
| `CustomHeightControlSmoothRadius` | int | Smoothing radius for custom height curves. | `2` (all) |
| `MaxAverageHeight` | float | Maximum average height cap. | `14` (Plains), `0.0` (Ocean), `160` (Jagged Peaks) |
| `MaxAverageDepth` | float | Maximum average depth. Usually `0.0`. | `0.0` |
| `Volatility1` | float | Primary volatility layer (larger terrain features). | `0.25` (Plains), `0.0` (Ocean), `1.5` (Jagged Peaks) |
| `Volatility2` | float | Secondary volatility layer (smaller details). | `0.1` (Plains), `0.0` (Ocean), `0.75` (Jagged Peaks) |
| `VolatilityWeight1` | float | Weight for volatility layer 1. **Per CLAUDE.md, values around 48.0 are correct for smooth terrain.** | `48.0` (universal) |
| `VolatilityWeight2` | float | Weight for volatility layer 2. | `46.8` (universal) |
| `Volatility` | float | Additional global volatility multiplier. Usually `0.0`. | `0.0` |
| `DisableBiomeHeight` | bool | If `true`, ignores `BiomeHeight` and uses only noise. | `false` |
| `ContinentalScale` | min:max float | Climate parameter range (MC noise parameters). Controls continentalness. | `0.3594:0.5594` |
| `ErosionScale` | min:max float | Climate parameter range. Controls erosion level. | `-0.0304:0.1696` |
| `WeirdnessScale` | min:max float | Climate parameter range. Controls weirdness/ridges. | `-0.0051:0.1949` |
| `CustomHeightControl` | 33 comma-separated floats | Custom height curve across 33 Y-slices from bottom to top of world. All zeros = use default noise-based height. | `0.0, 0.0, ... 0.0` |

**Key observations:**
- `VolatilityWeight1` and `VolatilityWeight2` are always `48.0` and `46.8` respectively across ALL biome types -- this is the "correct" range per CLAUDE.md (the DefaultPreset's lower values produce jagged terrain).
- The `ContinentalScale`, `ErosionScale`, `WeirdnessScale` ranges are unique per biome and control Minecraft's multi-noise biome selection system. Each biome occupies a specific "climate pocket."
- Ocean biomes have negative `ContinentalScale` ranges; mountains have extreme `ErosionScale` and `WeirdnessScale` ranges.

---

#### 6. Rivers

| Key | Type | Description | Example |
|-----|------|-------------|---------|
| `RiverBiome` | biome name | Which river biome to use. Empty = no rivers. | `River` (tagPlains template), empty (Ocean) |

---

#### 7. Blocks (Surface/Ground Materials)

| Key | Type | Description | Example |
|-----|------|-------------|---------|
| `StoneBlock` | block ID | The base stone block for underground generation. | `minecraft:stone` |
| `SurfaceBlock` | block ID | The top surface block. | `minecraft:dirt` |
| `GroundBlock` | block ID | The block below the surface. | `minecraft:sand` |
| `UnderWaterSurfaceBlock` | block ID | Surface block placed underwater. | `minecraft:sand` |
| `SurfaceAndGroundControl` | CSV or empty | Advanced surface/ground block placement logic. Empty = use defaults. | (empty in all shown) |
| `ReplacedBlocks` | block list or range | Blocks to replace during generation. Can use tuple syntax. | `None`, `(minecraft:dirt,minecraft:sand,62,255)` |

---

#### 8. Water / Lava & Frozen States

| Key | Type | Description | Example |
|-----|------|-------------|---------|
| `UseWorldWaterLevel` | bool | Use the global water level from DimensionPresetConfig.ini. | `true` |
| `WaterLevelMax` | int | Maximum water fill level. | `63` |
| `WaterLevelMin` | int | Minimum water fill level. | `0` |
| `WaterBlock` | block ID | Water block type. | `minecraft:water` |
| `IceBlock` | block ID | Ice block for frozen surfaces. | `minecraft:ice` |
| `PackedIceBlock` | block ID | Packed ice block. | `minecraft:packed_ice` |
| `SnowBlock` | block ID | Snow block. | `minecraft:snow_block` |
| `CooledLavaBlock` | block ID | Cooled lava block. | `minecraft:lava` |

---

#### 9. Visuals and Weather

| Key | Type | Description | Example |
|-----|------|-------------|---------|
| `BiomeTemperature` | float | Biome temperature (affects vanilla biome behavior). | `0.5`, `0.9` |
| `UseFrozenOceanTemperature` | bool | Use frozen ocean temperature logic. | `false` |
| `BiomeWetness` | float | Biome wetness/precipitation level. | `0.5`, `0.9` |
| `SkyColor` | hex | Sky color. | `0x7BA5FF` |
| `WaterColor` | hex | Water color. | `0xFFFFFF`, `0x3F76E4` |
| `WaterColorControl` | CSV or empty | Advanced water color control. | (empty) |
| `GrassColor` | hex | Grass tint color. | `0xFFFFFF` (no tint) |
| `GrassColorControl` | CSV or empty | Advanced grass color control. | (empty) |
| `GrassColorModifier` | string | Grass color modifier name. | `None` |
| `FoliageColor` | hex | Foliage tint color. | `0xFFFFFF` |
| `FoliageColorControl` | CSV or empty | Advanced foliage color control. | (empty) |
| `FogColor` | hex | Fog color. | `0x000000`, `0xC0D8FF` |
| `FogDensity` | float | Fog density. `0.0` = no custom fog. | `0.0` |
| `WaterFogColor` | hex | Underwater fog color. | `0x000000`, `0x050533` |
| `ParticleType` | resource location or empty | Ambient particle effect. | `minecraft:spore_blossom_air` |
| `ParticleProbability` | float | Probability of spawning a particle per tick. | `0.01`, `0.118093334` |
| `Music` | resource location or empty | Custom music track. | `minecraft:music.overworld.lush_caves` |
| `MusicMinDelay` | int | Minimum delay between music tracks (ticks). | `0`, `12000` |
| `MusicMaxDelay` | int | Maximum delay between music tracks (ticks). | `0`, `24000` |
| `ReplaceCurrentMusic` | bool | Replace currently playing music. | `false` |
| `AmbientSound` | resource location or empty | Ambient sound event. | (empty) |
| `MoodSound` | resource location | Sound for the "mood" mechanic (cave sounds). | `minecraft:ambient.cave` |
| `MoodSoundDelay` | int | Ticks between mood sound triggers. | `6000` |
| `MoodSearchRange` | int | Range to search for a player for mood sounds. | `8` |
| `MoodOffset` | float | Y offset for mood sound source. | `2.0` |
| `AdditionsSound` | resource location or empty | Additional ambient sound. | (empty) |
| `AdditionsTickChance` | float | Chance per tick to play additions sound. | `0.0` |

---

#### 10. Resource Queue (Ore/Feature Generation)

This is a free-form list of generation commands. Each line is a functional call:

| Function | Syntax | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `Ore(block, veinSize, veinsPerChunk, rarity, minY, maxY, targetBlock)` | `Ore(minecraft:coal_ore,17,20,100.0,0,127,minecraft:stone)` | Standard ore generation |
| `UnderWaterOre(block, veinSize, veinsPerChunk, rarity, targetBlock, targetBlock2)` | `UnderWaterOre(minecraft:sand,7,3,100.0,minecraft:dirt,minecraft:grass_block)` | Underwater ore generation |
| `Registry(feature_id, step)` | `Registry(minecraft:kelp_cold,VEGETAL_DECORATION)` | Delegate to vanilla worldgen feature registry |
| `UnderGroundLake(size, count, rarity, chance, minY, maxY)` | `UnderGroundLake(25,60,2,5.0,0,49)` | Underground lake placement |
| `Liquid(block, rarity, chance, minY, maxY, targetBlock)` | `Liquid(minecraft:water,20,100.0,8,128,minecraft:stone)` | Liquid pocket placement |
| `SmallLake(block, rarity, chance, minY, maxY)` | `SmallLake(minecraft:water,4,2.0,8,119)` | Small lake placement |
| `Dungeon(size, count, chance)` | `Dungeon(8.0,10,100)` | Dungeon spawner placement |
| `Tree(count, type, rarity, groundBlock, maxY)` | `Tree(1,BigTree,1,Tree,9)` | Tree generation |
| `Grass(type, grouping, rarity, chance, surfaceBlock, groundBlock)` | `Grass(Tallgrass,NotGrouped,10,100.0,minecraft:grass_block,minecraft:dirt)` | Grass decoration |

## Objective
- Cross-reference every OTG `.bc` biome config against vanilla 1.21.11 biome JSONs from mcasset.cloud and fix mob spawning, block palette, feature queues, trees, colors, and other settings to match vanilla.

## Important Details
- The vanilla JSON files are fetched from `https://assets.mcasset.cloud/1.21.11/data/minecraft/worldgen/biome/` (65 biome JS
- Key fields to sync per biome: `temperature`, `downfall`, `has_precipitation`, `water_color`, `foliage_color`, `grass_color`, `grass_color_modifier`, sky/fog color attributes, `spawners` (all categories), and `features` (all 11+ decoration steps).
- `.bc` files store mobs via `InheritMobsBiomeName: minecraft:<id>` (delegates to vanilla) — mapping must be correct.
- `.bc` block palette: `SurfaceBlock`, `GroundBlock`, `StoneBlock` should match vanilla surface rules.
- `.bc` features: `Registry()` entries + OTG `Ore()`/`Grass()`/`Plant()`/`Tree()` entries should mirror vanilla's feature lists.
- Project targets MC **1.21.5** (Yarn mappings), not 1.21.11 — vanilla biome JSONs from 1.21.11 may differ slightly from 1.21.5.
- The user wants every biome checked systematically.

## Work State
### Completed
- `VanillaNoiseProvider` → `VanillaDensityProvider` interface (`compute(int x, int y, int z)`), old interface deprecated.
- `OTGChunkGenerator.generateNoiseColumn()`: early-return samples `finalDensity()` via `VanillaDensityProvider` when `UseVanillaTerrain: true`, bypassing all OTG falloff/noise/CHC logic.
- `SharedOTGChunkGenerator.fillFromNoise()`: wires `randomState.router().finalDensity()` into `VanillaDensityProvider`.
- `UseVanillaCaves` setting added to `TerrainSettings` (default `true`): when `UseVanillaTerrain: true` and `UseVanillaCaves: true`, skips `carveWithNoise()` (caves already baked into `finalDensity()`). When `false`, runs the separate noise cave carver.
- Build succeeds (Fabric + NeoForge).

### Active
- First 4 batches (44 of 65) vanilla biome JSONs fetched and partially analyzed; ~20 more biomes remain.
- `badlands`, `bamboo_jungle`, `beach`, `desert`, `savanna`, `warm_ocean` and others have been extracted but NOT yet cross-referenced against their `.bc` files.
- The vanilla `NoiseBasedChunkGenerator` delegation (suggested as "directly pull the complete vanilla way") was **discussed but not implemented** — current code still uses `VanillaDensityProvider` inside OTG's own `generateNoiseColumn()` / `populateNoise()` pipeline, not a full vanilla chunk generator delegate.

### Blocked
- (none)

## How `.bc` Biome Config Files Are Loaded

### 1. File Discovery & Parsing

- The loader searches a preset's `Biomes/` folder recursively for files with these extensions:
  - `.bc`, `.biome`, `BiomeConfig.ini`, `.bc.ini`, `.biome.ini`
- It uses `FileSettingsReader.read()` to parse each file into a `SimpleSettingsMap` (which implements `SettingsMap`).

**File:** `C:\Users\dylan\Desktop\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\common\common-util\src\main\java\com\pg85\otg\config\io\FileSettingsReader.java`

- Basic line-by-line reader. Lines with `:` are plain settings (`Name: Value`). Lines with `(` are config functions/resources (e.g., `Ore(...)`). Lines starting with `#` or `<` are comments. Empty lines are ignored.

**File:** `C:\Users\dylan\Desktop\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\common\common-util\src\main\java\com\pg85\otg\config\io\SimpleSettingsMap.java`

- The parsed `SettingsMap` stores settings in a `LinkedHashMap` keyed by setting name (lowercased).

### 5. How `InheritMobsBiomeName` Works

**Definition (in `MobSettings`):**
- `C:\Users\dylan\Desktop\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\common\common-util\src\main\java\com\pg85\otg\config\settings\biome\MobSettings.java` (line 81-89)
- Default value: `""` (empty string, meaning no inheritance)

**Runtime Handler:**
- `C:\Users\dylan\Desktop\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\platforms\shared\src\main\java\com\pg85\otg\shared\biome\MobInheritanceHandler.java`

The logic:
1. `handleMobInheritance()` is called for each `BiomeConfig`.
2. If `InheritMobsBiomeName` is blank, the biome's own `mobSettings` are used directly (no inheritance).
3. If it's set:
   - **If the name starts with `otg:` or has no `:` at all** -- it's treated as an OTG biome name. The handler searches through all loaded biome configs for a matching biome name or registry key. Recursively processes that parent biome first, then combines mob lists.
   - **If the name contains `:` (and doesn't start with `otg:`)** -- it's treated as a vanilla biome resource location (e.g., `minecraft:ocean`). The handler looks it up in the Minecraft `Biome` registry and reads the 6 vanilla `MobCategory` spawn lists.
4. **Combination rule:** The child biome's mob settings take priority. `combine()` creates a merged list: `[child entries...] + [parent entries...]`. This means child settings with the same mob type in the same category override the parent (because the child list is added first and vanilla Minecraft uses first-match semantics? Actually, no -- OTG just appends child entries first, then parent entries. The override would need to be deduplicated elsewhere if needed, but the comment says "Any mob type defined in this biome config will override inherited mob settings for the same mob in the same mob category" -- this must happen somewhere in the spawn logic if mobs with the same name appear twice.)
5. **Cycle detection:** An inheritance chain is tracked to detect infinite loops (throws `InvalidConfigException`).

**Example from Hell.bc:** `InheritMobsBiomeName: minecraft:nether_wastes` -- this will pull all mob spawn entries from vanilla's Nether Wastes biome (ghasts, zombified piglins, etc.) but since the Hell.bc has `SpawnMonsters: []` (empty), the vanilla nether monsters are effectively suppressed.

### 6. Resource Queue (Features)

**Registration of resource types:**
- `BiomeConfig.java` (lines 31-69) -- The `RESOURCE_QUEUE_RESOURCES` HashMap maps resource names (strings) to their handler classes. All 32 resource types are registered here: `AboveWaterRes`, `Boulder`, `Cactus`, `Dungeon`, `Grass`, `Fossil`, `IceSpike`, `Liquid`, `Ore`, `Plant`, `UnderWaterPlant`, `Reed`, `SmallLake`, `SurfacePatch`, `UndergroundLake`, `UnderWaterOre`, `Vein`, `Vines`, `Well`, `CustomObject`, `CustomStructure`, `Sapling`, `Tree`, `Bamboo`, `SeaGrass`, `Kelp`, `SeaPickle`, `Registry`, `CoralMushroom`, `CoralTree`, `CoralClaw`, `Iceberg`, `BasaltColumn`, `Group`, `Scatter`.

**How resource queue entries are parsed:**
1. In `FileSettingsReader.readIntoMap()`, lines containing `(` are recognized as functions/resources (vs `:` for plain settings).
2. In `SimpleSettingsMap.getConfigFunctions()` (lines 85-115), each raw function string is split at `(` to get the function name, and the parameters between `(` and `)` are comma-separated.
3. The `BiomeResourcesManager` (in `BiomeResourcesManager.java`) is the `IConfigFunctionProvider` that matches function names to Java classes. It uses reflection to find a 2-param constructor `(BiomeSettings, List<String>)` or a 3-param constructor `(BiomeSettings, List<String>, OTGWorldInfo)` and instantiates the resource handler.
4. These parsed functions are then sorted in `BiomeResourceSettings.readResourceSettings()`:
   - `Sapling` and `CustomSapling` instances go into sapling maps (by type or by material).
   - Everything else goes into `resourceQueue` (an ordered `ArrayList`). `CustomStructure` functions also get cached in `customStructures`.
   - The resource queue is executed **in order** during chunk decoration, making placement order important.

### How Defaults Flow

The `Setting<T>` abstract class defines `getDefaultValue()`. Each concrete setting type (e.g., `FloatSetting`, `ColorSetting`, `IntSetting`, `MaterialSetting`) stores the default value passed to its constructor.

When a `.bc` file is read:
1. `FileSettingsReader` creates a `SimpleSettingsMap` from the file.
2. During `BiomeSettings.readDefaultSettings()`, each settings section's static factory method (e.g., `BiomeVisualSettings.getBiomeVisualSettings()`) calls `reader.getSetting(SOME_SETTING)`.
3. `SimpleSettingsMap.getSetting(setting)` checks if the key exists in its `settingsCache` map. If found, it parses the value via `setting.read(stringValue)`. If **not found**, it returns `setting.getDefaultValue()` (line 182 of SimpleSettingsMap: `return defaultValue` where `defaultValue` was `setting.getDefaultValue()` from line 151).
4. This means **any setting not present in the .bc file simply uses its Java-defined default**. Most DefaultPreset `.bc` files are short because they rely on these code defaults for the many visual/block settings they omit.

# Parse .bc file into settings
function Parse-BCFile {
    param($path)
    $settings = @{}
    $functions = @()
    $currentSection = ""
    Get-Content -Path $path -Encoding utf8 | ForEach-Object {
        $line = $_.Trim()
        if ($line -match "^#") { return }
        if ($line -match "^<") { return }
        if ($line -eq "") { return }
        if ($line -match "^#+$") { $currentSection = ""; return }
        if ($line -match "\+--") { return }
        if ($line -match "\|(.+?)\|") {
            $currentSection = $matches[1].Trim()
            return
        }
        if ($line -match "^(.+?):\s*(.*)$") {
            $key = $matches[1].Trim()
            $val = $matches[2].Trim()
            $settings[$key] = $val
        } elseif ($line -match "^(.+?)\((.+)\)$") {
            $functions += @{Name=$matches[1].Trim(); Args=$matches[2].Trim()}
        }
    }
    return @{Settings=$settings; Functions=$functions}
}

# Compare a .bc file with vanilla JSON
function Compare-BCtoVanilla {
    param($bcSettings, $vanillaJson, $vanillaId)

    $differences = @()

    # temperature
    $bcTemp = [float]($bcSettings["BiomeTemperature"] -replace ",","." -replace "f","")
    $vanTemp = [float]$vanillaJson.temperature
    if ([Math]::Abs($bcTemp - $vanTemp) -gt 0.01) {
        $differences += "BiomeTemperature: $bcTemp vs vanilla $vanTemp"
    }

    # downfall/wetness
    $bcWet = [float]($bcSettings["BiomeWetness"] -replace ",","." -replace "f","")
    $vanWet = [float]$vanillaJson.downfall
    if ([Math]::Abs($bcWet - $vanWet) -gt 0.01) {
        $differences += "BiomeWetness: $bcWet vs vanilla $vanWet"
    }

    # has_precipitation (not directly in .bc, but useful for info)
    $hasPrecip = $vanillaJson.has_precipitation

    # SkyColor
    if ($bcSettings.ContainsKey("SkyColor")) {
        $bcSky = [int]($bcSettings["SkyColor"] -replace "0x","0x", [System.Globalization.NumberStyles]::HexNumber)
        # Check both old and new format for sky color
        $vanSkyStr = ""
        if ($vanillaJson.effects.sky_color) { $vanSkyStr = $vanillaJson.effects.sky_color }
        if (!$vanSkyStr -and $vanillaJson.attributes."minecraft:visual/sky_color") {
            $vanSkyStr = $vanillaJson.attributes."minecraft:visual/sky_color"
        }
        if ($vanSkyStr) {
            $vanSky = [int]($vanSkyStr -replace "#","0x")
            if ($bcSky -ne $vanSky) {
                $differences += "SkyColor: 0x$('{0:X6}' -f $bcSky) vs vanilla $vanSkyStr"
            }
        }
    }

    # WaterColor
    if ($bcSettings.ContainsKey("WaterColor")) {
        $bcWater = [int]($bcSettings["WaterColor"] -replace "0x","0x")
        $vanWaterStr = $vanillaJson.effects.water_color
        if ($vanWaterStr) {
            $vanWater = [int]($vanWaterStr -replace "#","0x")
            if ($bcWater -ne $vanWater) {
                $differences += "WaterColor: 0x$('{0:X6}' -f $bcWater) vs vanilla $vanWaterStr"
            }
        }
    }

    # GrassColor
    if ($bcSettings.ContainsKey("GrassColor")) {
        $bcGrass = [int]($bcSettings["GrassColor"] -replace "0x","0x")
        $vanGrassStr = $vanillaJson.effects.grass_color
        if ($vanGrassStr) {
            $vanGrass = [int]($vanGrassStr -replace "#","0x")
            if ($bcGrass -ne $vanGrass) {
                $differences += "GrassColor: 0x$('{0:X6}' -f $bcGrass) vs vanilla $vanGrassStr"
            }
        }
    }

    # FoliageColor
    if ($bcSettings.ContainsKey("FoliageColor")) {
        $bcFoliage = [int]($bcSettings["FoliageColor"] -replace "0x","0x")
        $vanFoliageStr = $vanillaJson.effects.foliage_color
        if ($vanFoliageStr) {
            $vanFoliage = [int]($vanFoliageStr -replace "#","0x")
            if ($bcFoliage -ne $vanFoliage) {
                $differences += "FoliageColor: 0x$('{0:X6}' -f $bcFoliage) vs vanilla $vanFoliageStr"
            }
        }
    }

    # FogColor
    if ($bcSettings.ContainsKey("FogColor")) {
        $bcFog = [int]($bcSettings["FogColor"] -replace "0x","0x")
        $vanFogStr = $vanillaJson.effects.fog_color
        if (!$vanFogStr -and $vanillaJson.attributes."minecraft:visual/fog_color") {
            $vanFogStr = $vanillaJson.attributes."minecraft:visual/fog_color"
        }
        if ($vanFogStr) {
            $vanFog = [int]($vanFogStr -replace "#","0x")
            if ($bcFog -ne $vanFog) {
                $differences += "FogColor: 0x$('{0:X6}' -f $bcFog) vs vanilla $vanFogStr"
            }
        }
    }

    # WaterFogColor
    if ($bcSettings.ContainsKey("WaterFogColor")) {
        $bcWaterFog = [int]($bcSettings["WaterFogColor"] -replace "0x","0x")
        $vanWaterFogStr = $vanillaJson.effects.water_fog_color
        if ($vanWaterFogStr) {
            $vanWaterFog = [int]($vanWaterFogStr -replace "#","0x")
            if ($bcWaterFog -ne $vanWaterFog) {
                $differences += "WaterFogColor: 0x$('{0:X6}' -f $bcWaterFog) vs vanilla $vanWaterFogStr"
            }
        }
    }

    # GrassColorModifier
    if ($bcSettings.ContainsKey("GrassColorModifier") -and $vanillaJson.effects.grass_color_modifier) {
        $bcMod = $bcSettings["GrassColorModifier"]
        $vanMod = $vanillaJson.effects.grass_color_modifier
        if ($bcMod -ne $vanMod) {
            $differences += "GrassColorModifier: $bcMod vs vanilla $vanMod"
        }
    }

    # InheritMobsBiomeName - check if it matches the expected vanilla biome
    if ($bcSettings.ContainsKey("InheritMobsBiomeName")) {
        $mobsBiome = $bcSettings["InheritMobsBiomeName"]
        $expectedMobsBiome = "minecraft:$vanillaId"
        if ($mobsBiome -ne $expectedMobsBiome) {
            $differences += "InheritMobsBiomeName: $mobsBiome vs expected $expectedMobsBiome"
        }
    } else {
        $differences += "MISSING: InheritMobsBiomeName (expected minecraft:$vanillaId)"
    }

    # Check block palette defaults
    $defaults = @{
        "SurfaceBlock" = "minecraft:grass_block"
        "GroundBlock" = "minecraft:dirt"
        "StoneBlock" = "minecraft:stone"
    }

    # Check features - Registry entries
    $bcRegistries = @()
    $bcFunctions = $bcSettings["_functions"]
    if ($bcFunctions) {
        foreach ($fn in $bcFunctions) {
            if ($fn.Name -eq "Registry") {
                $bcRegistries += $fn.Args
            }
        }
    }

    # SurfaceBlock should match vanilla surface rule's top material

    return $differences
}

    $relPath = $_.FullName.Substring($bcDir.Length + 1)
    $parsed = Parse-BCFile -path $_.FullName

        $templates++

        $diffs = Compare-BCtoVanilla -bcSettings $parsed.Settings -vanillaJson $vanillaJson -vanillaId $mapping.VanillaId

        if ($diffs.Count -gt 0) {
            $totalDifferences += $diffs.Count
            $outputLines += "--- $relPath ---"
            $outputLines += "  Vanilla: $($mapping.VanillaId) (source: $($mapping.Source))"
            $outputLines += "  File size: $((Get-Item $_.FullName).Length) bytes"
            foreach ($d in $diffs) {
                $outputLines += "    $d"
            }
            $outputLines += ""
        }
    } else {
        $unmatched++
        if (!$mapping) {
            # It's an OTG-specific biome, just note it
        }
    }
}

    param($path)
    $settings = @{}
    $functions = @()
    Get-Content -Path $path -Encoding utf8 | ForEach-Object {
        $line = $_.Trim()
        if ($line -match "^[#<]") { return }

        if ($line -match "^[\+=#\-| ]+$") { return }

            $val = $matches[2].Trim()
            $settings[$key] = $val
        } elseif ($line -match "^(.+?)\((.+)\)$") {
            $functions += @{Name=$matches[1].Trim(); Args=$matches[2].Trim()}
        }
    }
    return @{Settings=$settings; Functions=$functions}
}

function Get-BiomeMapping {

        $vanWetF = [float]$vanillaJson.downfall

function Parse-BCFile {
    param($path)
    $settings = @{}
    $functions = @()
    Get-Content -Path $path -Encoding utf8 | ForEach-Object {
        $line = $_.Trim()
        if ($line -match "^[#<]") { return }
        if ($line -eq "") { return }
        if ($line -match "^[\+=#\-| ]+$") { return }
        if ($line -match "^(.+?):\s*(.*)$") {
            $key = $matches[1].Trim()
            $val = $matches[2].Trim()
            $settings[$key] = $val
        } elseif ($line -match "^(.+?)\((.+)\)$") {
            $functions += @{Name=$matches[1].Trim(); Args=$matches[2].Trim()}
        }
    }
    return @{Settings=$settings; Functions=$functions}
}

$matched = 0
$unmatched = 0
$templates = 0

Get-ChildItem -Path $bcDir -Recurse -Filter "*.bc" | ForEach-Object {
    $relPath = $_.FullName.Substring($bcDir.Length + 1)
    $parsed = Parse-BCFile -path $_.FullName

    if ($parsed.Settings.ContainsKey("TemplateForBiome") -and $parsed.Settings["TemplateForBiome"] -eq "true") {
        $templates++
        return
    }

    $mapping = Get-BiomeMapping -relPath $relPath -settings $parsed.Settings

    if ($mapping -and $vanillaBiomes.ContainsKey($mapping.VanillaId)) {
        $matched++
        $v = $vanillaBiomes[$mapping.VanillaId]
        $diffs = @()

        # Temperature
        $bcTemp = $parsed.Settings["BiomeTemperature"]
        if (!$bcTemp) { $bcTemp = "0.5(default)" }
        $bcTempF = [float](($bcTemp -replace "\(default\)","") -replace ",",".")
        $vanTempF = [float]$v.temperature
        if ([Math]::Abs($bcTempF - $vanTempF) -gt 0.01) {
            $diffs += "BiomeTemperature: $bcTempF vs vanilla $vanTempF"
        }

        # Downfall/Wetness
        $bcWet = $parsed.Settings["BiomeWetness"]
        if (!$bcWet) { $bcWet = "0.5(default)" }
        $bcWetF = [float](($bcWet -replace "\(default\)","") -replace ",",".")
        $vanWetF = [float]$v.downfall
        if ([Math]::Abs($bcWetF - $vanWetF) -gt 0.01) {
            $diffs += "BiomeWetness: $bcWetF vs vanilla $vanWetF"
        }

        # Colors
        function Check-Color {
            param($bcVal, $vanVal, $label, $defaultHex)
            if ($vanVal) {
                if (!$bcVal) { $bcVal = "$defaultHex(default)" }
                if ($bcVal -match "^N/A|default") {
                    $expectedDefault = $defaultHex
                    if ($expectedDefault -ne ("0x" + $vanVal.Replace("#",""))) {
                        return "$label: $bcVal vs vanilla $vanVal"
                    }
                } else {
                    $bcHex = $bcVal -replace "0x",""
                    $vanHex = $vanVal -replace "#",""
                    if ($bcHex -ne $vanHex) {
                        return "$label: $bcVal vs vanilla $vanVal"
                    }
                }
            }
            return $null
        }

        # Sky color
        $vanSkyStr = ""
        if ($v.effects.sky_color) { $vanSkyStr = $v.effects.sky_color }
        if (!$vanSkyStr -and $v.attributes."minecraft:visual/sky_color") { $vanSkyStr = $v.attributes."minecraft:visual/sky_color" }
        $d = Check-Color -bcVal $parsed.Settings["SkyColor"] -vanVal $vanSkyStr -label "SkyColor" -defaultHex "0x7BA5FF"
        if ($d) { $diffs += $d }

        # Water color
        $vanWaterStr = $v.effects.water_color
        $d = Check-Color -bcVal $parsed.Settings["WaterColor"] -vanVal $vanWaterStr -label "WaterColor" -defaultHex "0xFFFFFF"
        if ($d) { $diffs += $d }

        # Fog color
        $vanFogStr = $v.effects.fog_color
        if (!$vanFogStr -and $v.attributes."minecraft:visual/fog_color") { $vanFogStr = $v.attributes."minecraft:visual/fog_color" }
        $d = Check-Color -bcVal $parsed.Settings["FogColor"] -vanVal $vanFogStr -label "FogColor" -defaultHex "0x000000"
        if ($d) { $diffs += $d }

        # Water fog color
        $vanWFStr = $v.effects.water_fog_color
        $d = Check-Color -bcVal $parsed.Settings["WaterFogColor"] -vanVal $vanWFStr -label "WaterFogColor" -defaultHex "0x000000"
        if ($d) { $diffs += $d }

        # Grass color
        $vanGrassStr = $v.effects.grass_color
        $d = Check-Color -bcVal $parsed.Settings["GrassColor"] -vanVal $vanGrassStr -label "GrassColor" -defaultHex "0xFFFFFF"
        if ($d) { $diffs += $d }

        # Foliage color
        $vanFoliageStr = $v.effects.foliage_color
        $d = Check-Color -bcVal $parsed.Settings["FoliageColor"] -vanVal $vanFoliageStr -label "FoliageColor" -defaultHex "0xFFFFFF"
        if ($d) { $diffs += $d }

        # GrassColorModifier
        $bcMod = $parsed.Settings["GrassColorModifier"]
        if (!$bcMod) { $bcMod = "None(default)" }
        $vanMod = $v.effects.grass_color_modifier
        if ($vanMod -and $bcMod -ne $vanMod) {
            $diffs += "GrassColorModifier: $bcMod vs vanilla $vanMod"
        }

        # InheritMobsBiomeName check
        $expectedMobs = "minecraft:$($mapping.VanillaId)"
        $actualMobs = $parsed.Settings["InheritMobsBiomeName"]
        if ($actualMobs) {
            if ($actualMobs -ne $expectedMobs) {
                $diffs += "InheritMobsBiomeName: $actualMobs vs expected $expectedMobs"
            }
        } else {
            $diffs += "MISSING: InheritMobsBiomeName (expected $expectedMobs)"
        }

        if ($diffs.Count -gt 0) {
            $allDiffs[$relPath] = @{
                VanillaId = $mapping.VanillaId
                Source = $mapping.Source
                Diffs = $diffs
                Temp = $bcTemp
                Wet = $bcWet
            }
        }
    } else {
        $unmatched++
    }
}

# For replacing a value in text content
function Update-Value {
    param($content, $key, $newValue)
    $pattern = "(?m)^$key:\s*.*$"
    $replacement = "$key: $newValue"
    if ($content -match $pattern) {
        return $content -replace $pattern, $replacement
    }
    return $null
}

Formula: `BiomeHeight = cont_base(continent) + e_height(erosion) * w_mult(weirdness)`. Erosion maps to height (peaks 1.80, slopes 0.70, highland 0.40, rolling 0.25, flat 0.12, windswept 0.20, wetland 0.0). Weirdness multiplies erosion height (valleys 0.85, ridges 1.20).
