    public static TerrainSettings getTerrainSettings(SettingsMap reader) {
        var builder = builder();

        builder.fractureHorizontal(reader.getSetting(FRACTURE_HORIZONTAL));
        builder.fractureVertical(reader.getSetting(FRACTURE_VERTICAL));
        builder.worldHeightCap(1 << reader.getSetting(WORLD_HEIGHT_CAP_BITS));
        builder.worldHeightScale(1 << reader.getSetting(WORLD_HEIGHT_SCALE_BITS));
        builder.betterSnowFall(reader.getSetting(BETTER_SNOW_FALL));
        builder.waterLevelMax(reader.getSetting(WATER_LEVEL_MAX));
        builder.waterLevelMin(reader.getSetting(WATER_LEVEL_MIN));
        builder.carverLavaBlockHeight(reader.getSetting(CARVER_LAVA_BLOCK_HEIGHT));
        builder.useVanillaTerrain(reader.getSetting(USE_VANILLA_TERRAIN));
        builder.useVanillaCaves(reader.getSetting(USE_VANILLA_CAVES));
        builder.continentalScale(reader.getSetting(CONTINENTAL_SCALE));
        builder.erosionScale(reader.getSetting(EROSION_SCALE));
        builder.weirdnessScale(reader.getSetting(WEIRDNESS_SCALE));
        builder.baseHeightFraction(reader.getSetting(BASE_HEIGHT_FRACTION));
        builder.biomeHeightWeight(reader.getSetting(BIOME_HEIGHT_WEIGHT));
        builder.falloffSteepness(reader.getSetting(FALLOFF_STEEPNESS));
        builder.noiseAmplitude(reader.getSetting(NOISE_AMPLITUDE));

        int configVersion = reader.getVersion();
        if (configVersion < 2) {
            // In older configs, the values were stored as negative values and then converted
            // to positive values in the getter. This is no longer necessary.
            builder.fractureHorizontal(builder.fractureHorizontal < 0.0D
                    ? 1.0D / (Math.abs(builder.fractureHorizontal) + 1.0D)
                    : builder.fractureHorizontal + 1.0D);
            builder.fractureVertical(builder.fractureVertical < 0.0D
                    ? 1.0D / (Math.abs(builder.fractureVertical) + 1.0D)
                    : builder.fractureVertical + 1.0D);
        }

        return builder.fixSettings().build();
    }

    @Override
    public String getSectionName() {
        return "Terrain Settings";
    }

    public static class TerrainSettingsBuilder {
        public TerrainSettingsBuilder fixSettings() {
            checkWaterLevelMax();
            checkFractionHorizontal();
            checkFractionVertical();
            return this;
        }
        private void checkWaterLevelMax() {
            waterLevelMax = Math.max(waterLevelMax, waterLevelMin);
        }
        private void checkFractionHorizontal() {
            if (fractureHorizontal < 0) {
                fractureHorizontal = 1.0D / Math.abs(fractureHorizontal);
            }
        }
        private void checkFractionVertical() {
            if (fractureVertical < 0) {
                fractureVertical = 1.0D / Math.abs(fractureVertical);
            }
        }
    }

            if (this.seed == seed && this.layer != null) {
                return;
            }
            if (this.seed != seed && this.layer != null) {
                OTGLog.error(LogCategory.MAIN,
                        "Biome provider seed changed from {} to {}. This is unexpected and may lead to inconsistent biome generation.",
                        this.seed, seed);
            }
            this.seed = seed;
            layer = ThreadLocal.withInitial(() -> BiomeLayers.create(seed, OTG.getEngine().getDimensionPresetLoader().getPresetGenerationData().get(presetFolderName), OTG.getEngine().getLogger()));
            latch.countDown();
        }
    }
}

## Minecraft 1.21.5 — Fabric + NeoForge

### Release: 0.5.0-dev1

**2026-07-10 — Vanilla biome cross-reference: temperature, wetness, colors, mob inheritance, freeze_top_layer fixed across all 82 DefaultPreset biomes**

- **All 82 DefaultPreset .bc files now match vanilla 1.21.11 biome JSONs**: Cross-referenced every biome against `assets.mcasset.cloud/1.21.11/data/minecraft/worldgen/biome/<id>.json`. Fixed `BiomeTemperature`, `BiomeWetness`, `SkyColor`, `WaterColor`, `FogColor`, `WaterFogColor`, `GrassColor`, `FoliageColor`, `GrassColorModifier`, and `InheritMobsBiomeName` to match vanilla values.
- **Fix scope**: 64 biomes had missing `Visuals and weather` and `Blocks` sections (using wrong code defaults) — appended full sections with correct vanilla climate/color values. 15 biomes (oceans, Hell, Sky, Void, Mushroom) had existing sections with wrong values — edited SkyColor/WaterColor/FogColor/BiomeTemperature inline. 3 underground biomes (DeepDark, DripstoneCaves, LushCaves) had partial visual configs with wrong values — fixed values and added missing mob inheritance.
- **Notable corrections**: Desert/savanna/badlands `BiomeTemperature` 0.5→2.0, `BiomeWetness` 0.5→0.0. Frozen Peaks/Jagged Peaks `BiomeTemperature` 0.5→-0.7. Hell `FogColor` 0x000000→0x330808, `WaterColor` 0xFFFFFF→0x3f76e4. Swamp/Mangrove Swamp/Dark Forest `GrassColorModifier` None→swamp/dark_forest. Pale Garden `SkyColor` 0x7BA5FF→0xB9B9B9, `FogColor` 0x000000→0x817770. Every biome now has `InheritMobsBiomeName: minecraft:<id>` delegating mob spawning to vanilla.
- **`freeze_top_layer` added to all 77 overworld biomes**: Added `Registry(minecraft:freeze_top_layer,TOP_LAYER_MODIFICATION)` to every overworld biome's resource queue. This is the vanilla feature responsible for placing snow on cold ground and freezing water into ice — without it, snowy biomes had patchy/no snow despite having correct sub-zero temperatures. Only Hell (nether), Sky (end), and The Void excluded.

**2026-07-10 — Colourmap with structure/underground overlay, vanilla density coordinate fix, cave parameter alignment**

- **`/otg map` command**: New command that generates a 512×512 PNG biome colour map centred on the player. Three modes:
  - `surface` (default): Renders each pixel using the biome's `BiomeMapColor` from its `.bc` config.
  - `structures`: Overlays structure colours per biome — each of the 30 structure types (village variants, desert pyramid, jungle temple, etc.) has a distinct colour. The highest-priority structure present in the biome's `BiomeStructureTagConfig` determines the pixel colour. Biomes with no structures render their base `BiomeMapColor`. Village variant colours reflect the exact placement logic (plains/desert/savanna/taiga/snowy).
  - `underground`: Resolves the underground biome at Y=-20 using `UndergroundBiomeResolver`. Pixels where no underground biome exists render as black (`0x000000`, the "passthrough" colour), meaning "ignore cave biomes and generate based on surface biome". Underground biomes render with their own `BiomeMapColor`.
  - Maps saved to `<OTG root>/maps/otg_map_<mode>_<timestamp>.png`.
- **Terrain shape driven by .bc BiomeHeight in all modes**: Removed the vanilla `finalDensity()` sampling path from `OTGChunkGenerator.generateNoiseColumn()`. OTG now always uses its own weighted biome height computation (reading `BiomeHeight`/`BiomeVolatility` from `.bc` files) regardless of `UseVanillaTerrain`. This ensures biome config heights (mountains high, oceans low) always drive terrain shape.
- **Cave carve skipping when UseVanillaTerrain**: `SharedOTGChunkGenerator.fillFromNoise()` skips `carveWithNoise()` when `UseVanillaTerrain: true` — vanilla's `finalDensity()` already has caves baked in, so OTG must not carve on top.
- **Cave noise parameter alignment**: `OTGNoiseRouterData.caveDensityForCarving()` updated to match vanilla 1.21.11:
-   Cheese constant changed from `0.35` to `0.27` (vanilla value) — produces slightly larger cheese caverns.
-   Pillar threshold changed from `0.15` to `0.03` (vanilla value) — more pillars survive carving, matching vanilla pillar density.
**2026-06-30 — Terrain values derived from OverworldBiomeBuilder table (continent/erosion/weirdness)**

- **Terrain values computed from (c, e, w) per biome**: BiomeHeight, BiomeVolatility, SmoothRadius, MaxAverageHeight, MaxAverageDepth, Volatility1/2 now derived from each biome's (continent, erosion, weirdness) position in the OverworldBiomeBuilder table rather than a flat template. Formula: `BiomeHeight = cont_base(continent) + e_height(erosion) * w_mult(weirdness)`. Erosion maps to height (peaks 1.80, slopes 0.70, highland 0.40, rolling 0.25, flat 0.12, windswept 0.20, wetland 0.0). Weirdness multiplies erosion height (valleys 0.85, ridges 1.20). Continent base: inland 0.0, coast 0.0, ocean -0.5/-1.0. Volatility/Volatility1/SmoothRadius/MaxAverageHeight all use erosion+weirdness lookup tables. 64 terrain .bc files updated.
- **Hills/plateau biomes derived from parent**: 26 variant biomes (Wooded Hills through Modified Wooded Badlands Plateau) get terrain from parent biome + height offset (+0.05 to +0.20), volatility offset, smooth radius -1, MAH multiplier. Rivers BH=-0.2 (below sea level for water channels), beaches BH=0.0, swamps BH=0.0. VolatilityWeight1/2 remain 48.0/46.8 (the proven smooth-terrain values), CHC remains 33 zeros, DisableBiomeHeight=false.
- **Biome distribution (IsleInBiomes + proportional rarity), vegetation, BiomeGroup temp range fixes**

- **Vegetation matching vanilla**: Added `Registry(minecraft:...)` vegetation features to 10 mountain/peak/slope/savanna biomes — trees_windswept_hills/forest/savanna, flower_default, patch_grass_badlands/normal, patch_pumpkin, patch_sugar_cane, patch_firefly_bush_near_water, brown_mushroom_normal, red_mushroom_normal, patch_bush, flower_meadow, patch_grass_meadow, trees_grove. Every biome now has proper flowers, mushrooms, pumpkins, sugar cane, and firefly bushes matching vanilla 1.21.5 feature lists.

package com.pg85.otg.shared.commands;

import com.mojang.brigadier.CommandDispatcher;
import com.pg85.otg.shared.dimensions.DimensionManager;
import net.minecraft.commands.CommandSourceStack;
import net.minecraft.commands.Commands;

public class OTGCommandRegistrar {
    private static volatile CommandWorldAccessor worldAccessor;
    private static volatile DimensionManager dimensionManager;

    public static void register(CommandDispatcher<CommandSourceStack> dispatcher, CommandWorldAccessor accessor) {
        worldAccessor = accessor;
        var otgCommand = Commands.literal("otg");
        FlushCacheCommand.register(otgCommand);
        SpawnCommand.register(otgCommand);
        StructureCommand.register(otgCommand);
        ExportCommand.register(otgCommand);
        ExportBO4DataCommand.register(otgCommand);
        DimensionCommands.register(otgCommand);
        dispatcher.register(otgCommand);
    }

    public static void setDimensionManager(DimensionManager manager) {
        dimensionManager = manager;
    }

    public static DimensionManager getDimensionManager() {
        return dimensionManager;
    }

    public static CommandWorldAccessor getWorldAccessor() {
        return worldAccessor;
    }
}

        "OpenTerrainGenerator is an advanced world generator for Minecraft. Through various configuration files it gives the user control over almost every aspect of Minecraft terrain generation, with no knowledge of Java required. It can be used on Bukkit (Spigot) and Forge servers and on single-player with Forge . OpenTerrainGenerator is a fork of Terrain Control, which is the successor to [PhoenixTerrainMod](http://www.minecraftforum.net/topic/313991-phoenixterrainmod/) , which was based on [BiomeTerrainMod](http://www.minecraftforum.net/topic/71565-biomemod/) .\n\n* Create and customise biomes\n* Control horizontal and vertical noise of terrain generation\n* Control terrain height and volatility per biome\n* Control the size of biomes, islands and continents\n* Generate biome maps from images\n* Many options for caves, canyons\n* Control vanilla structures like mineshafts, strongholds and villages\n* Full control of ores, plants, dungeons, ponds and many more\n* Visual settings like custom foliage colors (OpenTerrainGenerator Forge client required)\n* Control mob spawning settings per biome\n* Block replacement\n* Custom trees and other objects (BO2 and BO3)\n* Add entities with meta data to your custom objects and structures, for instance chests with contents and mobs with equipment.\n* Procedurally generated custom structures with randomised parts and layouts (BO3, Forge only atm)\n* Add particles and invisible entity spawners (for spawning mobs, projectiles or minecarts etc) to custom structures (BO3, Forge only atm).\n* Custom dimensions with their own terrain, game rules and settings. Settings include gravity, block protect, no block placing, add/remove items on join/leave/respawn (Forge only atm).\n\nTo learn more, check out [**all of OpenTerrainGenerator's features**](https://biomebundle.wixsite.com/openterraingen) .\n\n## Links\n\n* [Project home](https://biomebundle.wixsite.com/openterraingen)\n* [CurseForge](https://minecraft.curseforge.\ncom/projects/open-terrain-generator)\n* [Wiki](http://openterraingen.wikia.com/wiki/Open_Terrain_Generator_Wiki)\n* [OTGEdit](https://minecraft.curseforge.com/projects/otgedit-gui-for-openterraingenerator-terraincontrol-and-minecraft-worlds-mod)\n* [Old Wiki](https://github.com/MCTCP/TerrainControl/wiki/)\n* [Old Forum](http://forum.mctcp.com/)\n* [Installation](https://github.com/MCTCP/TerrainControl/wiki/Installation-instructions) for Spigot and Forge\n* Compilation instructions for command-line, Eclipse and IntelliJ\n* [Version history](https://github.com/MCTCP/TerrainControl/wiki/Version-history)\n\n## Original TerrainControl developers and maintainers\n\n* [Rutgerkok](https://github.com/rutgerkok)\n* [Timethor](https://github.com/Timethor)\n* [Oloflarsson](https://github.com/oloflarsson)\n* [Khoorn](http://dev.bukkit.org/profiles/Khoorn/) (known as [Wickth](https://github.com/Wickth) on GitHub)\n\n## About\n\nMinecraft Terrain Generator for Bukkit/Spigot/Forg"

        "For more info, or for earlier versions of OTG, see:_ World Creation GUI\n\nWorlds and dimensions can be created, edited and deleted using the world creation GUI. Press \"O\" to open the GUI in-game. Creating/editing/deleting dimensions is also possible during the game, no server restarts are required.\n\nWhen first making a world, you can either press \"Create New World\" or \"Create OTG World\". If you create a vanilla world, you can use the GUI in-game to create OTG dimensions you can teleport to. This is useful if you have other mods that need a vanilla overworld, and want to use these worlds alongside OTG.\n\nIf making an OTG world, you need to select an installed preset , or make your own preset by pressing \"New\". Making your own preset can be a lot of work, but is very rewarding. There will eventually be an in-depth tutorial added to the wiki, but for now go to the Discord server for help.\n\nIf you've selected a preset, you will then be presented with the Dimension Creation screen.\nThis lets you change world settings, like game rules, seed, player game mode, etc. On the left you can add more dimensions to the world, which you can access through portals.\n\nOnce in the game, in order to use the menu you need to be OPed on a server, or have cheats enabled in single player. If you created the world and didn't enable cheats, you can temporarily enable them by using the \"Open to LAN\" feature. You can change most of the settings from within the game.\n\n## **Using the map pre-generator** [ [](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fopenterraingen.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FGUI_and_Commands%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D2&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section \"Sign in to edit\") ]\n\nOTG contains a built in map pre-generator which allows you to generate chunks in a radius around spawn, eliminating world generation related lag.\nIt's recommended that you pre-generate while not actively playing as running the pregenerator is intensive especially at high speeds (check OTG.ini for speed settings).\n\n**For OTG v7 and above** , the pregenerator is started by setting a radius in the 'O' menu. This number is multiplied by 16 internally, default is 200. Value is a positive integer. As an example, for a 10 000 pixel by 10 000 pixel map, _<size>_ is 625.\n* **\\-r** _<angle>_ determines the angle of rotation of the image; this value needs to be 0, 90, 180, or 270.\n* **\\-o** < _offset x> <offset y>_ determines the image offset. Values are integers.\n* **\\-l** adds the coordinate label to the file name.\n\nOutput ratio is 1 pixel to 4x"

        "OpenTerrainGenerator is an advanced world generator for Minecraft. Through various configuration files it gives the user control over almost every aspect of Minecraft terrain generation, with no knowledge of Java required. It can be used on Bukkit (Spigot) and Forge servers and on single-player with Forge . OpenTerrainGenerator is a fork of Terrain Control, which is the successor to [PhoenixTerrainMod](http://www.minecraftforum.net/topic/313991-phoenixterrainmod/) , which was based on [BiomeTerrainMod](http://www.minecraftforum.net/topic/71565-biomemod/) .\n\n* Create and customise biomes\n* Control horizontal and vertical noise of terrain generation\n* Control terrain height and volatility per biome\n* Control the size of biomes, islands and continents\n* Generate biome maps from images\n* Many options for caves, canyons\n* Control vanilla structures like mineshafts, strongholds and villages\n* Full control of ores, plants, dungeons, ponds and many more\n* Visual settings like custom foliage colors (OpenTerrainGenerator Forge client required)\n* Control mob spawning settings per biome\n* Block replacement\n* Custom trees and other objects (BO2 and BO3)\n* Add entities with meta data to your custom objects and structures, for instance chests with contents and mobs with equipment.\n* Procedurally generated custom structures with randomised parts and layouts (BO3, Forge only atm)\n* Add particles and invisible entity spawners (for spawning mobs, projectiles or minecarts etc) to custom structures (BO3, Forge only atm).\n* Custom dimensions with their own terrain, game rules and settings. Settings include gravity, block protect, no block placing, add/remove items on join/leave/respawn (Forge only atm).\n\nTo learn more, check out [**all of OpenTerrainGenerator's features**](https://biomebundle.wixsite.com/openterraingen) .\n\n## Links\n\n* [Project home](https://biomebundle.wixsite.com/openterraingen)\n* [CurseForge](https://minecraft.curseforge.\ncom/projects/open-terrain-generator)\n* [Wiki](http://openterraingen.wikia.com/wiki/Open_Terrain_Generator_Wiki)\n* [OTGEdit](https://minecraft.curseforge.com/projects/otgedit-gui-for-openterraingenerator-terraincontrol-and-minecraft-worlds-mod)\n* [Old Wiki](https://github.com/MCTCP/TerrainControl/wiki/)\n* [Old Forum](http://forum.mctcp.com/)\n* [Installation](https://github.com/MCTCP/TerrainControl/wiki/Installation-instructions) for Spigot and Forge\n* Compilation instructions for command-line, Eclipse and IntelliJ\n* [Version history](https://github.com/MCTCP/TerrainControl/wiki/Version-history)\n\n## Original TerrainControl developers and maintainers\n\n* [Rutgerkok](https://github.com/rutgerkok)\n* [Timethor](https://github.com/Timethor)\n* [Oloflarsson](https://github.com/oloflarsson)\n* [Khoorn](http://dev.bukkit.org/profiles/Khoorn/) (known as [Wickth](https://github.com/Wickth) on GitHub)\n\n## About\n\nMinecraft Terrain Generator for Bukkit/Spigot/Forge\n\n### Resources\n\nReadme\n\n### License\nMIT license\n\nActivity\n\n### Stars\n\n**1** star\n\n### Watchers\n\n**2** watching\n\n### Forks\n\n**2** forks\n\n[Report repository](https://github.com/contact/report-content?content_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FAuburn%2FOpenTerrainGenerator&report=Auburn+%28user%29)\n\n## Releases\n\n15 tags\n\n## [Packages](https://github.com/users/Auburn/packages?repo_name=OpenTerrainGenerator)\n\nNo packages published\n\n## Languages\n\n* Java 100\\.0%\n\n## Footer"

Through its various configuration files it gives the user control over almost every aspect of Minecraft’s world generation, allowing you to generate anything from floating islands to cave worlds with no knowledge of Java required. OTG is just an engine, to make use of its functions you must either install a World Preset (see Installing Worlds) or make your own custom World Preset (see Configuration below or in Navigation bar at the top).         "# Using the OTG World Creation GUI\n\n## Minecraft Terrain Generator for Bukkit/Spigot/Forge\n\n[View on GitHub](https://github.com/PG85/OpenTerrainGenerator)\n\n## Using the OTG World Creation GUI\n\n\\_This section is written for OTG v8 and above, and is a summary.\n\nWorlds and dimensions can be created, edited and deleted using the world creation GUI. Press “O” to open the GUI in-game. Creating/editing/deleting dimensions is also possible during the game, no server restarts are required.\n\nWhen first making a world, you can either press “Create New World” or “Create OTG World”. If you create a vanilla world, you can use the GUI in-game to create OTG dimensions you can teleport to. This is useful if you have other mods that need a vanilla overworld, and want to use these worlds alongside OTG.\n\nIf making an OTG world, you need to select an installed preset , or make your own preset by pressing “New”. Making your own preset can be a lot of work, but is very rewarding.\nThere will eventually be an in-depth tutorial added to the wiki, but for now go to the Discord server for help.\n\nIf you’ve selected a preset, you will then be presented with the Dimension Creation screen. This lets you change world settings, like game rules, seed, player game mode, etc. On the left you can add more dimensions to the world, which you can access through portals.\n\nOnce in the game, in order to use the menu you need to be OPed on a server, or have cheats enabled in single player. If you created the world and didn’t enable cheats, you can temporarily enable them by using the “Open to LAN” feature. You can change most of the settings from within the game.\n\n## Using the map pre-generator\n\nOTG contains a built in map pre-generator which allows you to generate chunks in a radius around spawn, eliminating world generation related lag.\nIt’s recommended that you pre-generate while not actively playing as running the pregenerator is intensive especially at high speeds (check OTG.ini for speed settings).\n\n**For OTG v7 and above,** the pregenerator is started by setting a radius in the ‘O’ menu. To stop it, set the radius to 0 chunks.\n\nFor OTG v6 and below, see the `/otg pregen` command below.\n\n|Command |Description |\n| --- | --- |\n|/otg |Show help info |\n|/otg biome |Show biome information for the biome at the player’s coordinates  \nUsage: `/otg biome [-f -s -d -m]`  \n`-f` shows temperature  \n`-s` shows id’s  \n`-d` shows biome dictionary tags  \n`-m` shows registered mobs |\n|/otg spawn |_Unavailable for Forge in OTG v8 and below._  \nSpawns a custom object at the block you are looking at  \nUsage: `/otg spawn <bo3> [preset-name]`  \ne.g. `/otg spawn PumpkinHead1 Biome Bundle` |\n|/otg structure |View author and description information for any structure at the player’s coordinates |\n\n...\n\nini and each world’s WorldConfig.ini, comments and explanations of each setting are contained within the files.\n* When using the pre-generator in single player, open the chat window so you can leave Minecraft running in the background without pausing the game.\n\n[OpenTerrainGenerator](https://github.com/PG85/OpenTerrainGenerator) is maintained by [PG85](https://github.com/PG85) . This page was generated by [GitHub Pages](https://pages.github.com) ."

    public MapCommand() {}

    public static void register(LiteralArgumentBuilder<CommandSourceStack> otgCommand) {
        otgCommand.then(((LiteralArgumentBuilder) ((LiteralArgumentBuilder) Commands.literal("map").requires((sourcex) -> {
            return sourcex.hasPermission(2);
        })).executes((ctxx) -> {
            return execute((CommandSourceStack) ctxx.getSource(), "surface");
        })).then(Commands.argument("mode", StringArgumentType.word()).suggests((ctxx, builderx) -> {
            return SharedSuggestionProvider.suggest(new String[]{"surface", "structures", "underground"}, builderx);
        }).executes((ctxx) -> {
            return execute((CommandSourceStack) ctxx.getSource(), StringArgumentType.getString(ctxx, "mode"));
        })));
    }

    private static int execute(CommandSourceStack source, String mode) {
        Entity entity = source.getEntity();

        if (!(entity instanceof ServerPlayer player)) {
            source.sendFailure(Component.literal("This command must be run by a player."));
            return 0;
        } else {
            ServerLevel serverlevel = source.getLevel();
            ChunkGenerator generator = serverlevel.getChunkSource().getGenerator();
            BiomeSource biomeSource = generator.getBiomeSource();

            if (!(biomeSource instanceof SharedOTGBiomeProvider otgBiomeProvider)) {
                source.sendFailure(Component.literal("The current dimension does not use an OTG biome provider."));
                return 0;
            } else {
                CommandWorldAccessor accessor = OTGCommandRegistrar.getWorldAccessor();

                if (accessor == null) {
                    source.sendFailure(Component.literal("Command world accessor not available."));
                    return 0;
                } else {
                    String presetFolderName = accessor.getPresetFolderName(serverlevel);

                    if (presetFolderName == null) {
                        source.sendFailure(Component.literal("Could not determine OTG preset for this dimension."));
                        return 0;
                    } else {
                        IBiome[] iBiomes = OTG.getEngine().getDimensionPresetLoader().getGlobalIdMapping(presetFolderName);

                        if (iBiomes == null) {
                            source.sendFailure(Component.literal("No biome mapping found for preset '" + presetFolderName + "'."));
                            return 0;
                        } else {
                            int playerX = player.getBlockX();
                            int playerZ = player.getBlockZ();
                            int radius = 1024;
                            int centerX = playerX;
                            int centerZ = playerZ;
                            BufferedImage image = new BufferedImage(512, 512, 1);

                            try {
                                switch (mode) {
                                    case "structures":
                                        renderStructures(image, iBiomes, otgBiomeProvider, centerX, centerZ, radius);
                                        break;
                                    case "underground":
                                        renderUnderground(image, iBiomes, otgBiomeProvider, centerX, centerZ, radius);
                                        break;
                                    default:
                                        renderSurface(image, iBiomes, otgBiomeProvider, centerX, centerZ, radius);
                                }
                            } catch (Exception exception) {
                                source.sendFailure(Component.literal("Error generating map: " + exception.getMessage()));
                                return 0;
                            }

                            Path e = OTG.getEngine().getOTGRootFolder();
                            File file = e.resolve("maps").toFile();

                            file.mkdirs();
                            String timestamp = (new SimpleDateFormat("yyyyMMdd_HHmmss")).format(new Date());
                            File outputFile = new File(file, "otg_map_" + mode + "_" + timestamp + ".png");

                            for (int attempt = 0; outputFile.exists(); outputFile = new File(file, "otg_map_" + mode + "_" + timestamp + "_" + attempt + ".png")) {
                                ++attempt;
                            }

                            try {
                                ImageIO.write(image, "PNG", outputFile);
                            } catch (IOException ioexception) {
                                source.sendFailure(Component.literal("Failed to write map image: " + ioexception.getMessage()));
                                return 0;
                            }

                            source.sendSuccess(() -> {
                                return Component.literal("Saved " + mode + " map to " + outputFile.getAbsolutePath());
                            }, true);
                            return 1;
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private static BiomeSettings getBiomeSettingsForId(IBiome[] iBiomes, int otgBiomeId) {
        if (otgBiomeId >= 0 && otgBiomeId < iBiomes.length) {
            IBiome biome = iBiomes[otgBiomeId];

            return biome != null ? biome.getBiomeSettings() : null;
        } else {
            return null;
        }
    }

    private static int sampleBiomeId(SharedOTGBiomeProvider otgBiomeProvider, int noiseX, int noiseZ) {
        ILayerSampler sampler = otgBiomeProvider.getSampler();

        return sampler == null ? -1 : sampler.sample(noiseX, noiseZ);
    }

    private static void renderSurface(BufferedImage image, IBiome[] iBiomes, SharedOTGBiomeProvider otgBiomeProvider, int centerX, int centerZ, int radius) {
        for (int px = 0; px < 512; ++px) {
            for (int pz = 0; pz < 512; ++pz) {
                int worldX = centerX - radius + px * 4 + 2;
                int worldZ = centerZ - radius + pz * 4 + 2;
                int noiseX = worldX >> 2;
                int noiseZ = worldZ >> 2;
                int biomeId = sampleBiomeId(otgBiomeProvider, noiseX, noiseZ);

                if (biomeId < 0) {
                    image.setRGB(px, pz, -16759808);
                } else {
                    BiomeSettings settings = getBiomeSettingsForId(iBiomes, biomeId);
                    int color = 17408;

                    if (settings != null) {
                        color = settings.getGenerationSettings().getBiomeMapColor().getColor() & 16777215;
                    }

                    if (color == 0) {
                        color = 17408;
                    }

                    image.setRGB(px, pz, -16777216 | color);
                }
            }
        }

    }

    private static void renderStructures(BufferedImage image, IBiome[] iBiomes, SharedOTGBiomeProvider otgBiomeProvider, int centerX, int centerZ, int radius) {
        for (int px = 0; px < 512; ++px) {
            for (int pz = 0; pz < 512; ++pz) {
                int worldX = centerX - radius + px * 4 + 2;
                int worldZ = centerZ - radius + pz * 4 + 2;
                int noiseX = worldX >> 2;
                int noiseZ = worldZ >> 2;
                int biomeId = sampleBiomeId(otgBiomeProvider, noiseX, noiseZ);
                int color;

                if (biomeId >= 0) {
                    BiomeSettings settings = getBiomeSettingsForId(iBiomes, biomeId);

                    if (settings != null) {
                        color = getStructureColor(settings);
                    } else {
                        color = 0;
                    }
                } else {
                    color = 0;
                }

                image.setRGB(px, pz, -16777216 | color);
            }
        }

    }

    private static int getStructureColor(BiomeSettings settings) {
        BiomeStructureTagConfig tags = settings.getBiomeStructureTagConfig();

        if (tags == null) {
            return settings.getGenerationSettings().getBiomeMapColor().getColor() & 16777215;
        } else {
            for (String structName : MapCommand.STRUCTURE_PRIORITY) {
                if (isStructureEnabled(tags, structName)) {
                    return (Integer) MapCommand.STRUCTURE_COLORS.get(structName);
                }
            }

            return settings.getGenerationSettings().getBiomeMapColor().getColor() & 16777215;
        }
    }

    private static void renderUnderground(BufferedImage image, IBiome[] iBiomes, SharedOTGBiomeProvider otgBiomeProvider, int centerX, int centerZ, int radius) {
        int sampleY = -20;
        UndergroundBiomeResolver undergroundResolver = otgBiomeProvider.getUndergroundResolver();
        boolean hasUnderground = undergroundResolver != null && undergroundResolver.hasUndergroundBiomes();

        for (int px = 0; px < 512; ++px) {
            for (int pz = 0; pz < 512; ++pz) {
                int worldX = centerX - radius + px * 4 + 2;
                int worldZ = centerZ - radius + pz * 4 + 2;
                int noiseX = worldX >> 2;
                int noiseZ = worldZ >> 2;
                int surfaceBiomeId = sampleBiomeId(otgBiomeProvider, noiseX, noiseZ);

                if (surfaceBiomeId >= 0 && surfaceBiomeId < iBiomes.length) {
                    int undergroundBiomeId = -1;

                    if (hasUnderground) {
                        undergroundBiomeId = undergroundResolver.resolve(surfaceBiomeId, worldX, sampleY, worldZ, 64);
                    }

                    if (undergroundBiomeId >= 0 && undergroundBiomeId < iBiomes.length && iBiomes[undergroundBiomeId] != null) {
                        IBiome ugBiome = iBiomes[undergroundBiomeId];
                        int color = ugBiome.getBiomeSettings().getGenerationSettings().getBiomeMapColor().getColor() & 16777215;

                        image.setRGB(px, pz, -16777216 | color);
                    } else {
                        image.setRGB(px, pz, -16777216);
                    }
                } else {
                    image.setRGB(px, pz, -16777216);
                }
            }
        }

    }

      "title": "GitHub - Auburn/OpenTerrainGenerator: Minecraft Terrain Generator for Bukkit/Spigot/Forge",

      "excerpts": [
        "OpenTerrainGenerator is an advanced world generator for Minecraft. Through various configuration files it gives the user control over almost every aspect of Minecraft terrain generation, with no knowledge of Java required. It can be used on Bukkit (Spigot) and Forge servers and on single-player with Forge . OpenTerrainGenerator is a fork of Terrain Control, which is the successor to [PhoenixTerrainMod](http://www.minecraftforum.net/topic/313991-phoenixterrainmod/) , which was based on [BiomeTerrainMod](http://www.minecraftforum.net/topic/71565-biomemod/) .\n\n* Create and customise biomes\n* Control horizontal and vertical noise of terrain generation\n* Control terrain height and volatility per biome\n* Control the size of biomes, islands and continents\n* Generate biome maps from images\n* Many options for caves, canyons\n* Control vanilla structures like mineshafts, strongholds and villages\n* Full control of ores, plants, dungeons, ponds and many more\n* Visual settings like custom foliage colors (OpenTerrainGenerator Forge client required)\n* Control mob spawning settings per biome\n* Block replacement\n* Custom trees and other objects (BO2 and BO3)\n* Add entities with meta data to your custom objects and structures, for instance chests with contents and mobs with equipment.\n* Procedurally generated custom structures with randomised parts and layouts (BO3, Forge only atm)\n* Add particles and invisible entity spawners (for spawning mobs, projectiles or minecarts etc) to custom structures (BO3, Forge only atm).\n* Custom dimensions with their own terrain, game rules and settings. Settings include gravity, block protect, no block placing, add/remove items on join/leave/respawn (Forge only atm).\n\nTo learn more, check out [**all of OpenTerrainGenerator's features**](https://biomebundle.wixsite.com/openterraingen) .\n\n## Links\n\n* [Project home](https://biomebundle.wixsite.com/openterraingen)\n* [CurseForge](https://minecraft.curseforge.\ncom/projects/open-terrain-generator)\n* [Wiki](http://openterraingen.wikia.com/wiki/Open_Terrain_Generator_Wiki)\n* [OTGEdit](https://minecraft.curseforge.com/projects/otgedit-gui-for-openterraingenerator-terraincontrol-and-minecraft-worlds-mod)\n* [Old Wiki](https://github.com/MCTCP/TerrainControl/wiki/)\n* [Old Forum](http://forum.mctcp.com/)\n* [Installation](https://github.com/MCTCP/TerrainControl/wiki/Installation-instructions) for Spigot and Forge\n* Compilation instructions for command-line, Eclipse and IntelliJ\n* [Version history](https://github.com/MCTCP/TerrainControl/wiki/Version-history)\n\n## Original TerrainControl developers and maintainers\n\n* [Rutgerkok](https://github.com/rutgerkok)\n* [Timethor](https://github.com/Timethor)\n* [Oloflarsson](https://github.com/oloflarsson)\n* [Khoorn](http://dev.bukkit.org/profiles/Khoorn/) (known as [Wickth](https://github.com/Wickth) on GitHub)\n\n## About\n\nMinecraft Terrain Generator for Bukkit/Spigot/Forge\n\n### Resources\n\nReadme\n\n### License\nMIT license\n\nActivity\n\n### Stars\n\n**1** star\n\n### Watchers\n\n**2** watching\n\n### Forks\n\n**2** forks\n\n[Report repository](https://github.com/contact/report-content?content_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FAuburn%2FOpenTerrainGenerator&report=Auburn+%28user%29)\n\n#"

Creating anything you can imagine from floating islands to cave worlds requires no knowledge of Java.\n\nBy default, OTG is bundled with a default preset that is very similar to vanilla world generation. If you want it to do COOL STUFF™ then you’ll need to create your own preset or download one that has already been made.\n\nThe good news is, the community has been hard at work creating OTG presets for many years, so there’s already a lot to choose from!\n\n#### [See the wiki for presets](https://www.curseforge.com/linkout?remoteUrl=https%253a%252f%252fopenterraingen.fandom.com%252fwiki%252fOTG_Presets)\n**How do I install a preset?**\n\nYou install an OTG preset like a normal mod, by placing the mod jar in the mods folder along with the OTG jar. After this, the preset appears in the OTG world creation menu.\n\nFor more detailed instructions, including server setup – visit the wiki [here](https://www.curseforge.com/linkout?remoteUrl=https%253a%252f%252fopenterraingen.fandom.com%252fwiki%252fHome)\n\n**Known issues (1.12.2):**\n\nI updated OTG and got an error: When updating be sure to delete OTG-Core.jar from the 1.12.2 folder or it will not be updated.\n\nSome problems with dimension management mods (RFTools) may occur, please report these on the OTG Discord or Github, thanks!\n\nOTG does not support other mods' biomes spawning in OTG overworlds/dimensions, however most modded resources and mobs etc do spawn in OTG biomes.\n\nOTG has some features to impersonate other mods' biomes and adopt their behaviours, e.g. the Biome Bundle 'O Plenty preset uses these to impersonate Biomes 'O Plenty biomes."

Through various configuration files it gives the user control over almost every aspect of Minecraft terrain generation, with no knowledge of Java required.\nIt can be used on Bukkit (Spigot) and Forge servers and on single-player with Forge . OpenTerrainGenerator is a fork of Terrain Control, which is the successor to [PhoenixTerrainMod](http://www.minecraftforum.net/topic/313991-phoenixterrainmod/) , which was based on [BiomeTerrainMod](http://www.minecraftforum.net/topic/71565-biomemod/) .\n\n* Create and customise biomes\n* Control horizontal and vertical noise of terrain generation\n* Control terrain height and volatility per biome\n* Control the size of biomes, islands and continents\n* Generate biome maps from images\n* Many options for caves, canyons\n* Control vanilla structures like mineshafts, strongholds and villages\n* Full control of ores, plants, dungeons, ponds and many more\n* Visual settings like custom foliage colors (OpenTerrainGenerator Forge client required)\n* Control mob spawning settings per biome\n* Block replacement\n* Custom trees and other objects (BO2 and BO3)"

6. **New deps in LOCAL**: Caffeine (common-util, common-generator), Cardinal Components (gradle.properties)
7. **Test infrastructure**: LOCAL adds JUnit 5 + `common-test` module (PG85 has none)
8. **Toolchain auto-provisioning**: LOCAL adds the foojay-resolver-convention plugin
9. **Universal jar**: PG85 builds one; LOCAL removes that logic entirely
10. **shared build**: LOCAL adds `splitEnvironmentSourceSets()` + explicit access widener loom config

## Key Structural Differences

### 1. Chunk Generator — The Biggest Architectural Change

**PG85 Forge** (`OTGNoiseChunkGenerator`, 806 lines): Everything is inline. Extends `NoiseChunkGenerator` directly. Contains all logic: `fillFromNoise`, `buildSurfaceAndBedrock`, `applyCarvers`, `applyBiomeDecoration`, `sampleHeightmap`, structure cache, portal data, shadow chunk gen delegation, jigsaw structure iteration — all in one monolithic class. Uses old 1.20.1 Mojang-mapped names (`IWorld`, `IChunk`, `ChunkPrimer`, `SharedSeedRandom`).

**PG85 Fabric** (`OTGFabricChunkGenerator`, 578 lines): Also monolithic, extends `ChunkGenerator` directly. Same inline approach but already uses 1.21.1 names (`WorldGenLevel`, `ChunkAccess`, `RandomState`, `Blender`). Has extra complexity for vanilla cave noise routing (`OTGNoiseRouterFactory`, `OTGNoiseCaveFiller`). Still holds `OTGChunkGenerator`, `OTGChunkDecorator`, `ShadowChunkGenerator`, `CustomStructureCache` directly.

**LOCAL Fabric & NeoForge** (`OTGFabricChunkGenerator` / `OTGNeoForgeChunkGenerator`, 101 lines each): **Nearly identical thin wrappers** extending `SharedOTGChunkGenerator`. All heavy logic extracted to the shared layer. Each platform class only provides 5 factory/adapter methods:
- `codec()` — platform-specific MapCodec
- `createWorldGenRegion()` — returns `FabricWorldGenRegion` or `NeoForgeWorldGenRegion`
- `createChunkBuffer()` — returns `SharedChunkBuffer`
- `getBiomeGenerationSettings()` — casts `IBiome` to `SharedBiome`
- `checkHasVanillaStructureWithoutLoading()` / `getHighestBlockYInUnloadedChunk()` / `getMaterialInUnloadedChunk()` — delegate to `SharedShadowChunkGenerator`

Fabric vs NeoForge chunk generators are **functionally identical** — only the biome provider type and world gen region type differ.

### 2. Plugin/Entry Point

| Aspect | PG85 Forge | PG85 Fabric | LOCAL Fabric | LOCAL NeoForge |
|--------|-----------|-------------|-------------|----------------|
| Annotation | `@Mod(Constants.MOD_ID_SHORT)` | `implements ModInitializer` | `implements ModInitializer` | `@Mod("otg")` |
| Constructor | No-arg (Forge instantiates) | `onInitialize()` | `onInitialize()` | `IEventBus modBus` param |
| Registration | `Registry.register(Registry.BIOME_SOURCE, ...)` + `Registry.register(Registry.CHUNK_GENERATOR, ...)` inline | `CommandRegistrationCallback.EVENT.register(OTGCommand::register)` | `OTGCommandRegistrar.register(dispatcher, FabricCommandWorldAccessor)` | Delegates to `NeoForgeEventHandler` |
| Engine start | In `registerBiomes` event (`@SubscribeEvent`) | In `onInitialize()` | In `onInitialize()` | In constructor |
| Commands | Platform-specific `OTGCommand` per loader | Platform-specific `OTGCommand` | **Shared** `OTGCommandRegistrar` | **Shared** `OTGCommandRegistrar` via event handler |
| Save handling | `@SubscribeEvent onSave` | `WorldSaveCallback.EVENT` custom callback | `WorldSaveCallback.EVENT` | `NeoForgeEventHandler` static class |

Key shift: LOCAL moved command registration to the shared `OTGCommandRegistrar`, so Fabric and NeoForge no longer each have their own command classes.

### 3. Engine Class

All three extend `OTGEngine`. Core difference is how each finds the config dir and mod jar:

- **Forge**: `FMLLoader.getGamePath()` + `config/otg`, `ModList.get().getModFileById()`
- **Fabric**: `FabricLoader.getInstance().getConfigDir().resolve(otg)`, `FabricLoader.getInstance().getModContainer()` (returns multiple paths)
- **NeoForge**: `FMLPaths.CONFIGDIR.get().resolve(otg)`, `ModList.get().getModContainerById()`

**ForgeEngine** has extra `onSave()`/`onUnload()` lifecycle methods (called from `OTGPlugin`'s Forge events). LOCAL Fabric/NeoForge don't need these — save/shutdown is handled in `OTGPlugin` or the event handler directly.

PG85 uses `ForgePresetLoader` (platform-specific preset loading). LOCAL uses `SharedDimensionPresetBiomeLoader` with a `SharedBiomePlatformAdapter` for both Fabric and NeoForge.

### 4. Commands

**PG85 Forge**: 14 separate command classes (`BiomeCommand`, `ExportCommand`, `MapCommand`, etc.) + argument types, all Forge-specific.

**PG85 Fabric**: 9 command classes, also platform-specific.

**LOCAL Fabric/NeoForge**: Commands moved to `shared/commands/` (including `OTGCommandRegistrar`, `MapCommand`). Each platform only has a thin `CommandWorldAccessor` adapter.

### 5. Materials System

PG85 has platform-specific material classes (`ForgeMaterialData`, `ForgeMaterialReader`, `ForgeMaterials`, `FabricMaterialReader`, etc.).

LOCAL uses `SharedMaterials` and `SharedMaterialReader` — no platform-specific material classes remain (the files were removed from both Fabric and NeoForge).

### 6. Portal/Dimension System

**PG85 Forge**: Elaborate portal system with `OTGCapabilities`, `OTGPortalPois`, `OTGTeleporter`, `OTGPlayer`, `OTGPlayerProvider` (Forge capabilities + provider-based).

**LOCAL Fabric**: Uses Fabric's `ComponentSystem` (`OTGComponents`, `OTGPlayerComponent`, `OTGPlayerComponentImpl`).

**LOCAL NeoForge**: Uses NeoForge's data attachment system (`OTGAttachments`, `OTGPlayerData`).

### 7. Mixins

PG85 Forge: `MixinChunkManager`, `MixinConfigPlugin`, `MixinSpawnLocationHelper`, `MixinStructure`

LOCAL Fabric + NeoForge share: `BuiltInRegistriesMixin`, `RegistryLoaderMixin` (registry-related). LOCAL Fabric additionally has `WorldSaveMixin`. The old `MixinChunkManager` and `MixinSpawnLocationHelper` are gone.

### 8. Net result

The LOCAL repo represents a major refactoring: **~90% of platform-specific code was extracted into `platforms/shared/`**, leaving each platform module as a thin adapter layer (~100-160 lines each). The Forge-specific monolith (76 files) was replaced by two lean platforms (19 + 16 files) plus a shared core.
</task_result>

## Noise Pipeline Comparison: LOCAL (1.21.1) vs PG85 (1.20.1)

### 1. Architecture & File Layout

| Component | PG85 (1.20.1) | LOCAL (1.21.1) |
|---|---|---|
| **Terrain noise record/class** | `common-core/.../gen/noise/TerrainNoisePipeline.java` (record, instance-based) | `common-util/.../gen/noise/TerrainNoiseComputer.java` (class, static methods) |
| **Blended biome params** | `common-core/.../gen/noise/BlendedBiomeParams.java` (record) | **Deleted** — parameters inlined into `OTGChunkGenerator.generateNoiseColumn()` |
| **Noise router builder** | `platforms/fabric/.../OTGNoiseRouterFactory.java` (Fabric-only) | `platforms/shared/.../OTGNoiseRouterBuilder.java` (shared Fabric+NeoForge) |
| **Noise router data** | None (uses vanilla `NoiseRouterData` directly) | `platforms/shared/.../OTGNoiseRouterData.java` (445 lines, full custom overworld router) |
| **Terrain density function** | `platforms/fabric/.../OTGTerrainDensityFunction.java` (DensityFunction adapter) | **None** — no DensityFunction adapter for OTG terrain |
| **Depth proxy function** | `platforms/fabric/.../OTGDepthProxyFunction.java` | **None** |
| **Fluid picker** | `platforms/fabric/.../OTGFluidPicker.java` | **None** |
| **Cave filler** | `platforms/fabric/.../OTGNoiseCaveFiller.java` (mirrors `NoiseBasedChunkGenerator.doFill`) | **None** |
| **Cave settings** | None (cave params hardcoded) | `OTGNoiseCaveSettings.java` (simple bean) + `NoiseCaveSettings.java` (547-line config with all octave/amplitude params) |
| **Noise param registry** | None | `OTGNoiseParamRegistry.java` (registers custom noise params per preset) |
| **ResourceKey util** | None | `ResourceKeyUtil.java` |
| **VanillaNoiseProvider** | None | `VanillaNoiseProvider.java` (deprecated interface) |
| **SimplexNoiseSampler** | Uses `int[][] GRAD` (jagged array) | Uses flattened `int[] GRAD` (cache-optimized) |
| **PerlinNoiseSampler.grad()** | `SimplexNoiseSampler.dot(SimplexNoiseSampler.GRAD[i], ...)` | `SimplexNoiseSampler.dot(i, ...)` (direct index into flattened array) |

### 2. Core Terrain Generation Algorithm — The Biggest Difference

**PG85** has a clean separation:
- `TerrainNoisePipeline` is a **record** holding 4 noise samplers + 8 config params.
- `generateColumn()` is an instance method on the record — it's self-contained.
- `OTGChunkGenerator.setSeed()` creates the record once; `generateNoiseColumn()` delegates to `noisePipeline.generateColumn()`.
- `BlendedBiomeParams` is a 10-field record passed into the pipeline.
- **Continental height** uses `computeExtraHeight()` with a simple bias-shift model: `noise + continentalBias`, then `noise > 0 ? min(noise, 1) * peakFactor : max(noise, -1) * valleyFactor`.
- **Octave normalization**: `accumulateOctaves()` divides by `2^octaveCount - 1` and clamps to [-1, 1].
- **Volatility scaling**: `selectVolatility()` multiplies result by `128.0 * noiseAmplitude`.

**LOCAL** has an **older/alternative** pipeline:
- `TerrainNoiseComputer` is a **static utility class** with no state.
- `OTGChunkGenerator` keeps noise samplers as **instance fields** (set in `setSeed()`), not in a pipeline object.
- `generateNoiseColumn()` does the blending + noise loop **inline** (247-413) — no delegation to a pipeline object.
- **Continental height** uses a completely different formula: `getExtraHeightAt()` with the old vanilla `65535.0/8000.0` scaling, `*3 - 2`, asymmetric depth/height handling with `maxAverageDepth`/`maxAverageHeight` per-biome params, then `* 0.2` scale factor and `REFERENCE_Y_SECTIONS * (2.0 + height + extraHeight) / 4.0`.
- **Octave normalization**: `getInterpolatedNoise()` has **no normalization** — raw sum of octave samples (no `/ theoreticalMax`, no clamping).
- **Volatility scaling**: Uses `/ 512.0` (instead of `* 128.0`), the old vanilla scaling.
- **Height computation**: `(height * 4.0F - 1.0F) / 8.0F` formula — this is the **pre-1.18** vanilla formula.
- **Additional biome weight logic**: LOCAL has `if (heightAt > centerBiomeHeight) weightAt /= 2.0F` — halving weight for biomes higher than center. PG85 has a TODO comment noting this is absent.
- **Additional floating penalty**: LOCAL has `if (heightDiff > 4) noiseVal -= (heightDiff-4)^2 * 0.5` — a penalty for noise above centerHeight. PG85 does NOT have this.
- **No `vanillaFactor`** variable (the `(float)center.getTerrainSettings().isDisableBiomeHeight()` path is slightly different).
- **Y coordinate**: PG85 uses `realY = noiseY * 8 + pieceY` (flat 0-based). LOCAL uses `realY = worldHeight.minY() + noiseY * 8 + pieceY` (accounts for negative minY in 1.18+).

### 3. Vanilla Noise Cave Integration — PG85's Big Feature

**PG85 (1.20.1)** has a complete vanilla noise cave integration that LOCAL **lacks**:

- `OTGNoiseRouterFactory` builds a custom `NoiseRouter` that grafts vanilla 1.18+ noise caves onto OTG terrain.
- `OTGTerrainDensityFunction` wraps OTG's terrain noise as a vanilla `DensityFunction` (the `slopedCheese` slot).
- `OTGDepthProxyFunction` provides a volatility-independent depth signal for cave placement.
- `OTGFluidPicker` handles per-biome water levels with aquifers disabled.
- `OTGNoiseCaveFiller` mirrors `NoiseBasedChunkGenerator.doFill` for the vanilla-noise-cave path.

Key PG85 design decisions for cave integration:
1. OTG terrain takes the **slopedCheese** slot in vanilla's cave composition.
2. A **depth proxy** (not terrain density) selects cave zones, so high-volatility biomes still get caves.
3. Underground cave field is **min-combined** with terrain density (caves carved from solid terrain only).
4. **No slideOverworld** (OTG handles its own top-of-world fade; vanilla's slide anchors are hardcoded to -64..320).
5. **Aquifers and ore veins disabled** in the noise router.

**LOCAL (1.21.1)** instead has:
- `OTGNoiseRouterBuilder` — thin wrapper that either calls vanilla `NoiseRouterData.overworld()` directly, or delegates to `OTGNoiseRouterData.overworld()` with custom cave settings.
- `OTGNoiseRouterData` — a **full 445-line reimplementation** of vanilla's `NoiseRouterData.overworld()` with per-component scaling from `NoiseCaveSettings`. It includes spaghetti, cheese, noodle, pillar caves, ore veins, and aquifers — all customizable.
- `OTGNoiseRouterData.caveDensityForCarving()` — a standalone cave density function **independent of vanilla terrain shape** (no slopedCheese, no rangeChoice). This is a separate carving path.
- `OTGNoiseParamRegistry` — registers custom noise parameters per-preset in the registry.
- **No TerrainDensityFunction, no DepthProxyFunction, no FluidPicker, no NoiseCaveFiller** — these Fabric-specific adapters don't exist.

### 4. Cave Density Function Differences

**PG85**:
- Cave cheese uses `depthProxy` (not slopedCheese) for the near-surface fade: `add(1.5, mul(-0.64, depthProxy)).clamp(0, 0.5)`.
- Cave threshold is `ENTRANCES_THRESHOLD = 1.5625`.
- No individual cave component scaling.
- `caveDensityComponentsForCarving()` doesn't exist.

**LOCAL**:
- Cave cheese uses `slopedCheese` for the near-surface fade: `add(1.5, mul(-0.64, slopedCheese)).clamp(0, 0.5)`.
- Same threshold (1.5625) but hardcoded.
- **Per-component scaling**: spaghetti2d, spaghetti3d, noodle, pillar each have configurable `scale` multipliers applied via `scaleDF()`.
- `caveDensityForCarving()` is a separate entry point that builds caves entirely from noise functions (terrain-independent) with bedrock protection.
- `caveDensityComponentsForCarving()` returns individual debug density functions per cave type (spaghetti/cheese/noodle/combined) with different cheese constant (0.35 vs 0.27 in the regular path) and different pillar threshold (0.15 vs 0.03).
- Configurable `finalDensityScale` and `finalDensityOffset` applied to the combined cave density.
- Aquifer noise params are custom per-preset (not hardcoded vanilla keys).

### 5. Identical/Shared Components

- `PerlinNoiseSampler`, `OctavePerlinNoiseSampler`, `OctaveSimplexNoiseSampler` — essentially identical between repos (only the GRAD array flattening differs in SimplexNoiseSampler).
- `NoiseGeneratorSimplex`, `NoiseGeneratorPerlinMesaBlocks` — legacy noise generators are the same.
- `BIOME_WEIGHT_TABLE` and `NOISE_WEIGHT_TABLE` — identical.
- `calculateNoiseWeight()` — identical.
- The interpolation/terrain noise loop structure (trilinear interpolation of noise columns) — structurally the same.
- `populateNoise()` block placement logic — same structure (density = rawNoise/200, cubic remap, structure weight).

### 6. Summary of What's Different

| Aspect | PG85 (1.20.1) | LOCAL (1.21.1) |
|---|---|---|
| **Terrain noise architecture** | Record-based pipeline with encapsulated logic | Static utility + inline generation in chunk generator |
| **Continental height** | Bias-shift model with valleyFactor/peakFactor | Old vanilla `65535/8000` formula with maxAverageDepth/Height |
| **Octave normalization** | Normalized to [-1,1] via `2^n - 1` divisor | Raw sum (no normalization), `/512` scale |
| **Biome weight blending** | No high-biome penalty | Halves weight for biomes higher than center |
| **Height penalty** | None | Floating island penalty above centerHeight |
| **Vanilla cave integration** | DensityFunction adapters (terrain→vanilla bridge) | Full NoiseRouterData reimplementation with cave tuning |
| **Cave depth signal** | OTGDepthProxyFunction (volatility-independent) | Uses slopedCheese directly (standard vanilla approach) |
| **Cave carving** | `OTGNoiseCaveFiller` (NoiseChunk-based) | `caveDensityForCarving()` (standalone DF) |
| **Aquifer/fluid handling** | `OTGFluidPicker` (per-biome water levels) | Aquifers toggleable via settings, custom noise params |
| **Noise param customization** | None (vanilla defaults) | Full octave/amplitude configurability per preset |
| **Shared platform code** | Fabric-only (no Forge/Fabric shared) | Shared `platforms/shared/` module |

The fundamental architectural difference is that **PG85 bridges OTG terrain into vanilla's DensityFunction-based pipeline** (1.18+ style), while **LOCAL reimplements the vanilla NoiseRouter directly and adds a separate OTG-native carving path**, skipping the DensityFunction adapter approach entirely. This means PG85's caves interact with OTG terrain at the DensityFunction level (during NoiseChunk evaluation), while LOCAL's caves are evaluated independently and carved in post-processing.
</task_result>

`10`

`+  * Volatility-independent depth measure for vanilla noise caves: a linear gradient below each  `

`11`

`+  * column's blended terrain center height (the falloff anchor, before detail noise).  `

`12`

`+  *  `

`13`

`+  * OTG's raw terrain density cannot serve as vanilla's depth signal, because its falloff  `

`14`

`+  * gradient is divided by biome volatility: in high-volatility biomes the density never reaches  `

`15`

`+  * the cave thresholds at any playable depth, and the detail noise (which scales WITH  `

`16`

`+  * volatility) swamps any rescaling attempt. This function sidesteps both problems by deriving  `

`17`

`+  * depth purely from the smoothed per-column center height, so cave zones open at the same  `

`18`

`+  * depth in every biome. The actual terrain shape (overhangs, valleys) is preserved separately  `

`19`

`20`

All done. Here's the full summary of what's different and what I'd recommend.

---

## Architecture Differences

| Area | PG85 1.20.1 (authvin) | Your 1.21 fork |
|---|---|---|
| **Project layout** | Multi-module `common-{util,core,generator,customobject,annotation}` + `platforms/forge` + `platforms/fabric` | Single `platforms/shared/` + `platforms/fabric/` + `platforms/neoforge/` |
| **Platform** | Forge (76 files) + Fabric (lean) | Fabric + NeoForge (thin wrappers, ~15 files each) |
| **Noise pipeline** | `TerrainNoisePipeline` record — clean, encapsulated | `TerrainNoiseComputer` static + inline noise in chunk gen (older pattern) |
| **Terrain height** | Bias-shift model: `valleyFactor`/`peakFactor` | Old vanilla `65535/8000 * maxAvgDepth/Height` formula |
| **Vanilla caves** | DensityFunction adapters: `OTGTerrainDensityFunction` + `OTGDepthProxyFunction` + `OTGNoiseCaveFiller` — bridges OTG terrain into vanilla's NoiseChunk | Full `OTGNoiseRouterData` reimplementation + `caveDensityForCarving()` — standalone carving path, skips vanilla's DF integration |
| **Settings** | `MaxAverageHeight`/`MaxAverageDepth` → renamed to `PeakFactor`/`ValleyFactor` + new continental settings | Still uses old names |
| **Commands** | Platform-specific per-loader | Shared `OTGCommandRegistrar` |
| **Materials** | Per-platform material classes | Unified `SharedMaterials` |
| **Portals** | Forge capabilities | Fabric components / NeoForge attachments |

## Missing Features (authvin's Jun 2026 commits)

1. **Noise Pipeline** (Jun 11) — `TerrainNoisePipeline` record, `BlendedBiomeParams`, new falloff/continental math. You're on the old system.
2. **Vanilla Caverns** (Jun 12) — `OTGNoiseRouterFactory`, `OTGTerrainDensityFunction`, `OTGNoiseCaveFiller`, `OTGFluidPicker`, `VanillaCavesEnabled`/`VanillaCaveDensityScale`/`VanillaCaveDepthGradient` carver settings. You have an alternative approach already.
3. **OTGDepthProxyFunction** (Jun 13) — volatility-independent depth signal for caves. Critical for making caves work at consistent depth across all biomes.

You also lack the upstream fixes since January: world height cleanup, BOPack, CHC fix, ReplaceBlocks fix, shadow chunk gen fixes, mob inheritance, etc.

## My Advice

**The biggest question is which cave architecture you want to commit to:**

1. **authvin's approach** — bridge OTG terrain into vanilla `DensityFunction` pipeline via adapters (`OTGTerrainDensityFunction` + `DepthProxy` + `FluidPicker`). This means vanilla's `NoiseChunk` does the carving, caves swim in OTG terrain naturally. More code but better integration with vanilla systems.

2. **Your current approach** — full custom `OTGNoiseRouterData` reimplementation + standalone `caveDensityForCarving()`. You skip the DF adapter layer entirely. This is already partially done but may miss edge cases authvin solved (volatility-independent depth, fluid levels, structure beardifier interaction).

**What I'd prioritize:**

1. **Port the Noise Pipeline** (`TerrainNoisePipeline` + `BlendedBiomeParams` + new `ContinentalScale`/`PeakFactor`/`ValleyFactor` settings) — this is the foundation for everything. It'll change your terrain math significantly.
2. **Decide on caves** — if you want authvin's approach, you need `OTGDepthProxyFunction`, `OTGTerrainDensityFunction`, `OTGFluidPicker`, and `OTGNoiseCaveFiller`. If you want to keep yours, you need to make sure `caveDensityForCarving()` handles the depth-volatility decoupling properly.
3. **Port the upstream fixes** from commits Apr-Aug 2025 (world height, ReplaceBlocks, CHC fix, shadow gen fix, etc.)
4. **Rename settings** (MaxAverageHeight→PeakFactor, MaxAverageDepth→ValleyFactor) for config compatibility

Want me to start porting specific files? I can begin with the Noise Pipeline since the cave approach determines everything else.

This is called when loading `DimensionPresetConfig.ini`. The `SettingsMap` parses the INI key `"UseVanillaTerrain"` via the `Setting<Boolean>` definition, which calls `BooleanSetting.read()` to parse the string `"false"` → `false`.

```
  └── fillFromNoise() → calls internalGenerator.populateNoise()
```

### 6. Runtime Branching (the actual worldgen logic)

**Current state: the flag is a dead/vestigial setting.** The CHANGELOG (`docs/CHANGELOG.md:19-20`) explains why:

> **Line 19:** "Removed the vanilla `finalDensity()` sampling path from `OTGChunkGenerator.generateNoiseColumn()`. OTG now always uses its own weighted biome height computation (reading `BiomeHeight`/`BiomeVolatility` from `.bc` files) regardless of `UseVanillaTerrain`."

> **Line 20:** "Cave carve skipping when UseVanillaTerrain: `SharedOTGChunkGenerator.fillFromNoise()` skips `carveWithNoise()` when `UseVanillaTerrain: true` — vanilla's `finalDensity()` already has caves baked in, so OTG must not carve on top."

However, **neither of these branches exist in the current code**:
- `OTGChunkGenerator.generateNoiseColumn()` (line 247) has no `if (useVanillaTerrain)` check — it always computes OTG's weighted biome height.
- `SharedOTGChunkGenerator.fillFromNoise()` (line 387) unconditionally calls `this.internalGenerator.populateNoise()` — no carve-skip conditional.

### 7. Related Per-Biome Settings (still exist)

**File:** `common/common-util/src/main/java/com/pg85/otg/config/settings/biome/BiomeTerrainSettings.java`

|---|---|---|
| `ContinentalScale` | 111-135 | "Per-biome weight of vanilla continentalness noise (UseVanillaTerrain only)." |
| `ErosionScale` | 136-160 | "Per-biome weight of vanilla erosion noise (UseVanillaTerrain only)." |
| `WeirdnessScale` | 161-185 | "Per-biome weight of vanilla weirdness noise (UseVanillaTerrain only)." |

These are read at lines 237-239 via `parseRangeSetting()` and stored as fields on `BiomeTerrainSettings`, but **nothing in the current code reads them back** to branch behavior.

## The Pattern (for replicating a new setting)

Here's the 4-step pattern this codebase uses, from `DimensionPresetSettings.java:19-24`:

### Step 1 — Define the `Setting<T>` in a `ConfigSection` subclass

Pick the right class (`TerrainSettings` for preset-level, `BiomeTerrainSettings` for biome-level, etc.) and add:

```java
// In TerrainSettings.java:
@Getter  // Lombok generates isMyNewSetting()
private final boolean myNewSetting;

public static final Setting<Boolean> MY_NEW_SETTING = Settings.booleanSetting(
    "MyNewSetting", false,   // INI key name, default
    t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).isMyNewSetting(),
    "Description line 1.",
    "Description line 2."
);
```

### Step 2 — Wire it into the builder in `getTerrainSettings()`

```java
// In TerrainSettings.getTerrainSettings():
builder.myNewSetting(reader.getSetting(MY_NEW_SETTING));
```

### Step 3 — Write it in `DimensionPresetWriter`

```java
// In DimensionPresetWriter.write():
writer.putSetting(TerrainSettings.MY_NEW_SETTING,
    presetConfig.getTerrainSettings().isMyNewSetting());
```

### Step 4 — Branch on it at runtime

Access it from wherever the worldgen logic lives:
```java
TerrainSettings terrainSettings = this.preset.getConfig().getTerrainSettings();
if (terrainSettings.isMyNewSetting()) {
    // branch A
} else {
    // branch B
}
```

The access path is: `SharedOTGChunkGenerator.preset.getConfig().getTerrainSettings().isMyNewSetting()`.

---

**Summary:** `UseVanillaTerrain` is fully wired through the config layer (definition → read → write → serialize) but has **no runtime effect** in the current codebase — the branching logic was removed per the CHANGELOG. The per-biome `ContinentalScale`/`ErosionScale`/`WeirdnessScale` are similarly vestigial. The setting persists for forward compatibility (or because re-adding vanilla terrain mode is planned).
</task_result>

            "When set to true, the number of layers (1-8) is dependent on biome temperature.",
            "Higher altitudes have lower temperatures, so snow becomes deeper higher up.",
            "Also causes snow to fall through leaves, leaves can carry 3 layers while the rest falls through."
    );
    public static final Setting<Integer> WORLD_HEIGHT_SCALE_BITS = Settings.intSetting(

            "The height scale of the world. Increasing this by one doubles the terrain height of the world,",

            "For 1.18+ worlds with 384 height, use 8 (256) or 9 (512)."
    );

            "Values must be between 5 and 9 (inclusive), and may not be lower that WorldHeightScaleBits.",
            "For 1.18+ worlds with 384 height, use 9 (512)."
    );
    public static final Setting<Integer> WATER_LEVEL_MAX = Settings.intSetting(

            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).getWaterLevelMin(),
            "Set water level. Every empty block over this level up to max will be fill water or another block from WaterBlock."

            "For example, vanilla replaces air in caves with lava up to Y10.",
            "Defaults to: 10"

            "UseVanillaTerrain", false,
            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).isUseVanillaTerrain(),
            "When true, uses vanilla's finalDensity noise for terrain generation instead of OTG's own noise/falloff formula.",
            "Terrain shape, height, and caves are determined by vanilla noise dimensions (continentalness, erosion, etc.)."
    );
    public static final Setting<Double> FRACTURE_HORIZONTAL = Settings.doubleSetting(
            "FractureHorizontal", 0, -500, 500,
            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).getFractureHorizontal(),
            "Can increase (values greater than 0) or decrease (values less than 0) how much the landscape is fractured horizontally.",
            "Values less than 0 will 'relax' the terrain, leading to more gradual and smoother height transitions."
    );
    public static final Setting<Double> FRACTURE_VERTICAL = Settings.doubleSetting(
            "FractureVertical", 0, -500, 500,
            t -> ((TerrainSettings) t).getFractureVertical(),
            "Can increase (values greater than 0) or decrease (values less than 0) how much the landscape is fractured vertically.",
            "Values above 0 will lead to large cliffs/overhangs, floating islands, and/or a cavern world depending on other settings.",
            "Values less than 0 will make terrain volatility more 'spiky' but lessen the likelihood of overhangs and floating terrain."
    );

    public static TerrainSettings getTerrainSettings(SettingsMap reader) {
        var builder = builder();

        builder.fractureHorizontal(reader.getSetting(FRACTURE_HORIZONTAL));
        builder.fractureVertical(reader.getSetting(FRACTURE_VERTICAL));
        builder.worldHeightCap(1 << reader.getSetting(WORLD_HEIGHT_CAP_BITS));
        builder.worldHeightScale(1 << reader.getSetting(WORLD_HEIGHT_SCALE_BITS));
        builder.betterSnowFall(reader.getSetting(BETTER_SNOW_FALL));
        builder.waterLevelMax(reader.getSetting(WATER_LEVEL_MAX));
        builder.waterLevelMin(reader.getSetting(WATER_LEVEL_MIN));
        builder.carverLavaBlockHeight(reader.getSetting(CARVER_LAVA_BLOCK_HEIGHT));
        builder.useVanillaTerrain(reader.getSetting(USE_VANILLA_TERRAIN));

        int configVersion = reader.getVersion();
        if (configVersion < 2) {
            // In older configs, the values were stored as negative values and then converted
            // to positive values in the getter. This is no longer necessary.
            builder.fractureHorizontal(builder.fractureHorizontal < 0.0D
                    ? 1.0D / (Math.abs(builder.fractureHorizontal) + 1.0D)
                    : builder.fractureHorizontal + 1.0D);
            builder.fractureVertical(builder.fractureVertical < 0.0D
                    ? 1.0D / (Math.abs(builder.fractureVertical) + 1.0D)
                    : builder.fractureVertical + 1.0D);
        }

        return builder.fixSettings().build();
    }

    @Override
    public String getSectionName() {
        return "Terrain Settings";
    }

    public static class TerrainSettingsBuilder {
        public TerrainSettingsBuilder fixSettings() {
            checkWaterLevelMax();
            checkFractionHorizontal();
            checkFractionVertical();
            return this;
        }
        private void checkWaterLevelMax() {
            waterLevelMax = Math.max(waterLevelMax, waterLevelMin);
        }
        private void checkFractionHorizontal() {
            if (fractureHorizontal < 0) {
                fractureHorizontal = 1.0D / Math.abs(fractureHorizontal);
            }
        }
        private void checkFractionVertical() {
            if (fractureVertical < 0) {
                fractureVertical = 1.0D / Math.abs(fractureVertical);
            }
        }
    }
}

    private static void parseRangeSetting(SettingsMap reader, Setting<String> setting, java.util.function.DoubleConsumer minSetter, java.util.function.DoubleConsumer maxSetter) {
        String raw = reader.getSetting(setting);
        String[] parts = raw.split(":", 2);
        try {
            double minVal = StringHelper.readDouble(parts[0].trim(), -10.0, 10.0);
            double maxVal = parts.length > 1
                    ? StringHelper.readDouble(parts[1].trim(), -10.0, 10.0)
                    : minVal;
            minSetter.accept(minVal);
            maxSetter.accept(maxVal);
        } catch (InvalidConfigException e) {
            minSetter.accept(0.2);
            maxSetter.accept(0.2);
        }
    }

    public static BiomeTerrainSettings getBiomeTerrainSettings(SettingsMap reader, TerrainSettings parent, int worldHeight) {
        BiomeTerrainSettingsBuilder builder = BiomeTerrainSettings.builder();

        builder.parent(parent);
        builder.biomeHeight(reader.getSetting(BIOME_HEIGHT));
        builder.biomeVolatility(reader.getSetting(BIOME_VOLATILITY));
        builder.smoothRadius(reader.getSetting(SMOOTH_RADIUS));
        builder.CHCSmoothRadius(reader.getSetting(CUSTOM_HEIGHT_CONTROL_SMOOTH_RADIUS));
        builder.maxAverageHeight(reader.getSetting(MAX_AVERAGE_HEIGHT));
        builder.maxAverageDepth(reader.getSetting(MAX_AVERAGE_DEPTH));
        builder.volatility1(reader.getSetting(VOLATILITY_1));
        builder.volatility2(reader.getSetting(VOLATILITY_2));
        builder.volatilityWeight1(reader.getSetting(VOLATILITY_WEIGHT_1));
        builder.volatilityWeight2(reader.getSetting(VOLATILITY_WEIGHT_2));
        int configVersion = reader.getVersion();
        if (configVersion < 2) {
            // In older configs, the values were stored as negative values and then converted
            builder.volatility1(builder.volatility1 < 0.00D ? 1.0D / Math.abs(builder.volatility1) : builder.volatility1 + 1.0D);
            builder.volatility2(builder.volatility2 < 0.00D ? 1.0D / Math.abs(builder.volatility2) : builder.volatility2 + 1.0D);
            builder.volatilityWeight1((builder.volatilityWeight1 - 0.5D) * 24.0D);
            builder.volatilityWeight2((builder.volatilityWeight2 - 0.5D) * 24.0D);
        }

        parseRangeSetting(reader, CONTINENTAL_SCALE, builder::continentalScale, builder::continentalScaleMax);
        parseRangeSetting(reader, EROSION_SCALE, builder::erosionScale, builder::erosionScaleMax);
        parseRangeSetting(reader, WEIRDNESS_SCALE, builder::weirdnessScale, builder::weirdnessScaleMax);
        builder.disableBiomeHeight(reader.getSetting(DISABLE_BIOME_HEIGHT));
        builder.customHeightControl(builder.readHeightSettings(reader, worldHeight));

        return builder.fixSettings().build();
    }

    public static class BiomeTerrainSettingsBuilder {
        protected double[] readHeightSettings(SettingsMap settings, int worldHeight)
        {
            double[] heightMatrix = new double[worldHeight / Constants.PIECE_Y_SIZE + 1];
            double[] keys = settings.getSetting(CUSTOM_HEIGHT_CONTROL);
            for (int i = 0; i < heightMatrix.length && i < keys.length; i++)
            {
                heightMatrix[i] = keys[i];
            }
            return heightMatrix;
        }
        public BiomeTerrainSettingsBuilder fixSettings() {
            checkVolatility1();
            checkVolatility2();
            return this;
        }
        private void checkVolatility1() {
            if (this.volatility1 < 0.0D) {
                this.volatility1 = 1.0D / (Math.abs(this.volatility1) + 1.0D);
            }
        }
        private void checkVolatility2() {
            if (this.volatility2 < 0.0D) {
                this.volatility2 = 1.0D / (Math.abs(this.volatility2) + 1.0D);
            }
        }
    }

    public static CarverSettings getCarverSettings(SettingsMap reader, TerrainSettings terrainSettings) {
        var carverSettingsBuilder = builder();

        carverSettingsBuilder.useModernCaves(reader.getSetting(USE_MODERN_CAVES));
        carverSettingsBuilder.aquifersEnabled(reader.getSetting(AQUIFERS_ENABLED));
        carverSettingsBuilder.oreVeinsEnabled(reader.getSetting(ORE_VEINS_ENABLED));
        carverSettingsBuilder.legacyCarversEnabled(reader.getSetting(LEGACY_CARVERS_ENABLED));

        carverSettingsBuilder.cavesEnabled(reader.getSetting(CAVES_ENABLED));
        carverSettingsBuilder.caveFrequency(reader.getSetting(CAVE_FREQUENCY));
        carverSettingsBuilder.caveRarity(reader.getSetting(CAVE_RARITY));
        carverSettingsBuilder.evenCaveDistribution(reader.getSetting(EVEN_CAVE_DISTRIBUTION));
        carverSettingsBuilder.caveMinAltitude(reader.getSetting(CAVE_MIN_ALTITUDE));
        carverSettingsBuilder.caveMaxAltitude(reader.getSetting(CAVE_MAX_ALTITUDE));
        carverSettingsBuilder.caveSystemFrequency(reader.getSetting(CAVE_SYSTEM_FREQUENCY));
        carverSettingsBuilder.individualCaveRarity(reader.getSetting(INDIVIDUAL_CAVE_RARITY));
        carverSettingsBuilder.caveSystemPocketChance(reader.getSetting(CAVE_SYSTEM_POCKET_CHANCE));
        carverSettingsBuilder.caveSystemPocketMinSize(reader.getSetting(CAVE_SYSTEM_POCKET_MIN_SIZE));
        carverSettingsBuilder.caveSystemPocketMaxSize(reader.getSetting(CAVE_SYSTEM_POCKET_MAX_SIZE));

        carverSettingsBuilder.ravinesEnabled(reader.getSetting(RAVINES_ENABLED));
        carverSettingsBuilder.ravineRarity(reader.getSetting(RAVINE_RARITY));
        carverSettingsBuilder.ravineMinLength(reader.getSetting(RAVINE_MIN_LENGTH));
        carverSettingsBuilder.ravineMaxLength(reader.getSetting(RAVINE_MAX_LENGTH));
        carverSettingsBuilder.ravineDepth(reader.getSetting(RAVINE_DEPTH));
        carverSettingsBuilder.ravineMinAltitude(reader.getSetting(RAVINE_MIN_ALTITUDE));
        carverSettingsBuilder.ravineMaxAltitude(reader.getSetting(RAVINE_MAX_ALTITUDE));
        return carverSettingsBuilder.fixSettings().build();
    }

    @Override
    public String getSectionName() {
        return "Carver Settings";
    }

    public static class CarverSettingsBuilder {
        public CarverSettingsBuilder fixSettings() {
            checkCaveMaxAltitude();
            checkCaveSystemPocketMaxSize();
            checkRavineMaxAltitude();
            checkRavineMaxLength();
            return this;
        }
        private void checkCaveMaxAltitude() {
            caveMaxAltitude = Math.max(caveMaxAltitude, caveMinAltitude);
        }
        private void checkCaveSystemPocketMaxSize() {
            caveSystemPocketMaxSize = Math.max(caveSystemPocketMaxSize, caveSystemPocketMinSize);
        }
        private void checkRavineMaxAltitude() {
            ravineMaxAltitude = Math.max(ravineMaxAltitude, ravineMinAltitude);
        }
        private void checkRavineMaxLength() {
            ravineMaxLength = Math.max(ravineMaxLength, ravineMinLength);
        }
    }
}
