**File:** `C:\Users\dylan\Desktop\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\common\common-customobject\src\main\java\com\pg85\otg\customobject\TreeObject.java`

#### `spawnAsTree` (lines 111-177) — **FIX IS PRESENT**

This method has full water/ice validation:

- **Line 122:** Gets the highest block Y via `getHighestBlockAboveYAt(x, z)`
- **Lines 126-128:** World bounds check
- **Lines 131-135:** Min/max height restriction check
- **Lines 138-141:** Checks the spawn position block is air (prevents underwater trees)
- **Lines 144-147:** Checks that the block below is not null
- **Lines 150-153:** **Key fix** — Validates the block below is not liquid, ice, packed ice, or blue ice:
  ```java
  if (blockBelow.isLiquid() || blockBelow.isMaterial(LocalMaterials.ICE) ||
      blockBelow.isMaterial(LocalMaterials.PACKED_ICE) || blockBelow.isMaterial(LocalMaterials.BLUE_ICE)) {
      return false;
  }
  ```
- **Lines 156-165:** Validates the block below matches `sourceBlocks` or falls back to `isValidTreeSoil` (grass, dirt, podzol, mycelium)

#### `process` (lines 57-82) — **FIX IS MISSING**

This method has **no water/ice validation** at all:

```java
int x = world.getDecorationArea().getChunkBeingDecoratedMinX()
        + random.nextInt(Constants.CHUNK_SIZE);
int z = world.getDecorationArea().getChunkBeingDecoratedMinZ()
        + random.nextInt(Constants.CHUNK_SIZE);
int y = world.getHighestBlockAboveYAt(x, z);
if (y < world.getWorldInfo().minY() || y > world.getWorldInfo().maxY()) {
    return false;
}

        structureCache,
        world,

        Rotation.NORTH,

        y,
        z,

```

It calls `getHighestBlockAboveYAt`, checks world bounds, then directly calls `spawnForced` — which calls `world.placeTree(type, random, x, y, z)`. There is **no check for water, ice, or liquid blocks at the spawn position or below it**. This means trees placed via the decoration path (the `process` method) can still spawn on water and ice surfaces.

**Note:** `spawnForced` (lines 97-108) is also a bare pass-through with no validation:
```java
public boolean spawnForced(...) {
    return world.placeTree(type, random, x, y, z);
}
```

The `process` method should be updated to include the same water/ice/soil validation that `spawnAsTree` has before calling `spawnForced`.

### 2. Carver Crash Below y=0 — **FIX IS ALREADY PRESENT**

#### Primary carving mask index computation

**File:** `C:\Users\dylan\Desktop\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\common\common-generator\src\main\java\com\pg85\otg\gen\carver\Carver.java`

**Lines 161-167:**
```java
// Offset Y by minY to ensure non-negative index for BitSet (1.18+ worlds can have negative Y)
int offsetY = y - otgWorldInfo.minY();
int i = relativeX | relativeZ << 4 | offsetY << 8;
if (carvingMask.get(i)) {
    return false;
}
carvingMask.set(i);
```

The `minY` offset is already applied. Without it, the formula `relativeX | relativeZ << 4 | y << 8` would produce a negative integer when `y` is below zero (e.g., y=-64 in a default 1.18+ world), causing `BitSet.get()` and `BitSet.set()` to throw `IndexOutOfBoundsException`.

#### RavineCarver Y-cache index computation

**File:** `C:\Users\dylan\Desktop\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\common\common-generator\src\main\java\com\pg85\otg\gen\carver\RavineCarver.java`

**Lines 116-122** (`isPositionExcluded` method):
```java
// Offset Y by minY for 1.18+ worlds with negative Y coordinates
int cacheIndex = y - otgWorldInfo.minY();
// Bounds check to prevent ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
if (cacheIndex < 0 || cacheIndex >= cache.length) {
    return true;
}
return (scaledRelativeX * scaledRelativeX + scaledRelativeZ * scaledRelativeZ)
    * (double) cache[cacheIndex] + scaledRelativeY * scaledRelativeY / 6.0D >= 1.0D;
```

This also has the `minY` offset and a bounds check. The cache array is sized to `otgWorldInfo.maxY() - otgWorldInfo.minY() + 1` (line 64), so the offset correctly maps world Y to array index.

#### Y-bounds clamping in carveRegion

**File:** `Carver.java`, **lines 70-74:**
```java
int minY = Math.max(MathHelper.floor(localY - pitch) - 1, otgWorldInfo.minY() + 8);
int maxY = Math.min(MathHelper.floor(localY + pitch) + 1, otgWorldInfo.maxY() - 8);
```

The `minY` and `maxY` loop bounds in `carveRegion` are clamped to `otgWorldInfo.minY() + 8` and `otgWorldInfo.maxY() - 8`, which prevents carving at extreme world boundaries.

package com.pg85.otg.customobject;

import com.pg85.otg.constants.Constants;
import com.pg85.otg.customobject.config.CustomObjectResourcesManager;
import com.pg85.otg.customobject.structures.CustomStructureCache;
import com.pg85.otg.interfaces.IMaterialReader;
import com.pg85.otg.interfaces.IModLoadedChecker;
import com.pg85.otg.interfaces.IWorldGenRegion;
import com.pg85.otg.util.bo3.Rotation;
import com.pg85.otg.util.materials.LocalMaterialData;
import com.pg85.otg.util.materials.LocalMaterials;
import com.pg85.otg.util.materials.MaterialSet;
import com.pg85.otg.util.minecraft.TreeType;

import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.Random;

/**
 * A Minecraft tree, viewed as a custom object.
 *
 * <p>For historical reasons, TreeObject implements {@link CustomObject} instead
 * of just {@link SpawnableObject}. We can probably refactor the Tree resource
 * to accept {@link SpawnableObject}s instead of {@link CustomObject}s, so that
 * all the extra methods are no longer needed.
 */
class TreeObject implements CustomObject {
    private final TreeType type;

    TreeObject(TreeType type) {
        this.type = type;
    }

    @Override
    public boolean onEnable(
            String presetFolderName,
            Path otgRootFolder,
            CustomObjectManager customObjectManager,
            IMaterialReader materialReader,
            CustomObjectResourcesManager manager,
            IModLoadedChecker modLoadedChecker
    ) {
        return true;
    }

    @Override
    public String getName() {
        return type.name();
    }

    @Override
    public boolean canSpawnAsTree() {
        return true;
    }

    // Called during decoration.
    @Override
    public boolean process(
            CustomStructureCache structureCache,
            IWorldGenRegion world,
            Random random
    ) {
        // A tree has no frequency or rarity, so spawn it once in the chunk
        // Make sure we stay within decoration bounds.
        int x = world.getDecorationArea().getChunkBeingDecoratedMinX()
                + random.nextInt(Constants.CHUNK_SIZE);
        int z = world.getDecorationArea().getChunkBeingDecoratedMinZ()
                + random.nextInt(Constants.CHUNK_SIZE);
        int y = world.getHighestBlockAboveYAt(x, z);
        if (y < world.getWorldInfo().minY() || y > world.getWorldInfo().maxY()) {
            return false;
        }
        return spawnForced(
                structureCache,
                world,
                random,
                Rotation.NORTH,
                x,
                y,
                z,
                false
        );
    }

    @Override
    public boolean spawnFromSapling(
            IWorldGenRegion worldGenRegion,
            Random random,
            Rotation rotation,
            int x,
            int y,
            int z
    ) {
        return worldGenRegion.placeTree(type, random, x, y, z);
    }

    @Override
    public boolean spawnForced(
            CustomStructureCache structureCache,
            IWorldGenRegion world,
            Random random,
            Rotation rotation,
            int x,
            int y,
            int z,
            boolean allowReplaceBlocks
    ) {
        return world.placeTree(type, random, x, y, z);
    }

    @Override
    public boolean spawnAsTree(
            CustomStructureCache structureCache,
            IWorldGenRegion world,
            Random random,
            int x,
            int z,
            int minY,
            int maxY,
            MaterialSet sourceBlocks
    ) {
        // Get highest block position (including liquids)
        int y = world.getHighestBlockAboveYAt(x, z);
        Rotation rotation = Rotation.getRandomRotation(random);

        // Check world bounds
        if (y < world.getWorldInfo().minY() || y > world.getWorldInfo().maxY()) {
            return false;
        }

        // Check min/max height restrictions
        if (!(minY == -1 && maxY == -1)) {
            if (y < minY || y > maxY) {
                return false;
            }
        }

        // Check that spawn position is air (not underwater!)
        LocalMaterialData blockAtY = world.getMaterial(x, y, z);
        if (blockAtY == null || !blockAtY.isAir()) {
            return false;
        }

        // Validate the block underneath - tree needs appropriate soil
        LocalMaterialData blockBelow = world.getMaterial(x, y - 1, z);
        if (blockBelow == null) {
            return false;
        }

        // Don't spawn on water, ice, or other liquids
        if (blockBelow.isLiquid() || blockBelow.isMaterial(LocalMaterials.ICE) ||
            blockBelow.isMaterial(LocalMaterials.PACKED_ICE) || blockBelow.isMaterial(LocalMaterials.BLUE_ICE)) {
            return false;
        }

        // Use provided sourceBlocks or fall back to default dirt-like blocks
        if (sourceBlocks != null) {
            if (!sourceBlocks.contains(blockBelow)) {
                return false;
            }
        } else {
            // Default: only spawn on grass, dirt, podzol, mycelium
            if (!isValidTreeSoil(blockBelow)) {
                return false;
            }
        }

        return spawnForced(
                structureCache,
                world,
                random,
                rotation,
                x,
                y,
                z,
                true
        );
    }

    /**
     * Checks if the given material is valid soil for tree growth.
     * This matches vanilla Minecraft's tree placement rules.
     */
    private boolean isValidTreeSoil(LocalMaterialData material) {
        return material.isMaterial(LocalMaterials.GRASS) ||
               material.isMaterial(LocalMaterials.DIRT) ||
               material.isMaterial(LocalMaterials.PODZOL) ||
               material.isMaterial(LocalMaterials.MYCELIUM);
    }

    @Override
    public boolean canRotateRandomly() {
        // Trees cannot be rotated
        return false;
    }

    @Override
    public boolean loadChecks(IModLoadedChecker modLoadedChecker) {
        return true;
    }

    @Override
    public boolean doReplaceBlocks() {
        return false;
    }
}

Diff: C:\Users\dylan\Desktop\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\common\common-customobject\src\main\java\com\pg85\otg\customobject\TreeObject.java
```
    // Called during decoration.
    @Override
    public boolean process(
            CustomStructureCache structureCache,
            IWorldGenRegion world,
            Random random
    ) {
        // A tree has no frequency or rarity, so spawn it once in the chunk
        // Make sure we stay within decoration bounds.
        int x = world.getDecorationArea().getChunkBeingDecoratedMinX()
                + random.nextInt(Constants.CHUNK_SIZE);
        int z = world.getDecorationArea().getChunkBeingDecoratedMinZ()
                + random.nextInt(Constants.CHUNK_SIZE);
        int y = world.getHighestBlockAboveYAt(x, z);
        if (y < world.getWorldInfo().minY() || y > world.getWorldInfo().maxY()) {
            return false;
        }

        // Don't spawn on water, ice, or other liquids
        LocalMaterialData blockAtY = world.getMaterial(x, y, z);
        if (blockAtY == null || !blockAtY.isAir()) {
            return false;
        }
        LocalMaterialData blockBelow = world.getMaterial(x, y - 1, z);
        if (blockBelow == null || blockBelow.isLiquid() ||
            blockBelow.isMaterial(LocalMaterials.ICE) ||
            blockBelow.isMaterial(LocalMaterials.PACKED_ICE) ||
            blockBelow.isMaterial(LocalMaterials.BLUE_ICE)) {
            return false;
        }

        return spawnForced(
                structureCache,
                world,
                random,
                Rotation.NORTH,
                x,
                y,
                z,
                false
        );
    }
```

    private static DensityFunction underground(
            DensityFunction depthProxy,
            DensityFunction entrances,
            HolderGetter<DensityFunction> functions,
            HolderGetter<NormalNoise.NoiseParameters> noises
    ) {
        DensityFunction spaghetti2d = getFunction(functions, "overworld/caves/spaghetti_2d");
        DensityFunction spaghettiRoughness = getFunction(functions, "overworld/caves/spaghetti_roughness_function");
        DensityFunction caveLayer = DensityFunctions.noise(noises.getOrThrow(Noises.CAVE_LAYER), 8.0);
        DensityFunction layerBulge = DensityFunctions.mul(DensityFunctions.constant(4.0), caveLayer.square());
        DensityFunction caveCheese = DensityFunctions.noise(noises.getOrThrow(Noises.CAVE_CHEESE), 0.6666666666666666);
        DensityFunction cheese = DensityFunctions.add(
                DensityFunctions.add(DensityFunctions.constant(0.27), caveCheese).clamp(-1.0, 1.0),
                DensityFunctions.add(
                        DensityFunctions.constant(1.5),
                        DensityFunctions.mul(DensityFunctions.constant(-0.64), depthProxy)
                ).clamp(0.0, 0.5)
        );
        DensityFunction caves = DensityFunctions.min(
                DensityFunctions.min(DensityFunctions.add(layerBulge, cheese), entrances),
                DensityFunctions.add(spaghetti2d, spaghettiRoughness)
        );
        DensityFunction pillars = getFunction(functions, "overworld/caves/pillars");
        DensityFunction activePillars = DensityFunctions.rangeChoice(
                pillars, -1000000.0, 0.03, DensityFunctions.constant(-1000000.0), pillars
        );
        return DensityFunctions.max(caves, activePillars);
    }

    private static DensityFunction postProcess(DensityFunction density) {
        DensityFunction blended = DensityFunctions.blendDensity(density);
        return DensityFunctions.mul(DensityFunctions.interpolated(blended), DensityFunctions.constant(0.64)).squeeze();
    }

    private static DensityFunction getFunction(HolderGetter<DensityFunction> functions, String name) {
        Holder<DensityFunction> holder = functions.getOrThrow(
                ResourceKey.create(Registries.DENSITY_FUNCTION, ResourceLocation.parse(name))
        );
        return new DensityFunctions.HolderHolder(holder);
    }
}

    // Height / volatility
    public double getCHCData(int controlLayer) {
        double[] chc = this.getTerrainSettings().getCustomHeightControl();

package com.pg85.otg.gen.resource;

import com.pg85.otg.config.settings.biome.BiomeSettings;
import com.pg85.otg.exceptions.InvalidConfigException;
import com.pg85.otg.interfaces.IWorldGenRegion;
import com.pg85.otg.util.helpers.RandomHelper;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Random;

public class DungeonResource extends FrequencyResourceBase
{
    private final int maxAltitude;
    private final int minAltitude;

    public DungeonResource(BiomeSettings biomeConfig, List<String> args) throws InvalidConfigException
    {
        super(biomeConfig, args);
        assureSize(3, args);

        // Support legacy format with 4 args: Dungeon(Frequency, Rarity, MinAltitude, MaxAltitude)
        // New format has 3 args: Dungeon(Rarity, MinAltitude, MaxAltitude) with frequency=1
        if (args.size() >= 4) {
            // Legacy format - first arg is frequency (ignored, we use 1)
            this.frequency = 1;
            this.rarity = readRarity(args.get(1));
            this.minAltitude = readElevation(args.get(2));
            this.maxAltitude = readElevation(args.get(3));
        } else {
            // New format
            this.frequency = 1;
            this.rarity = readRarity(args.get(0));
            this.minAltitude = readElevation(args.get(1));
            this.maxAltitude = readElevation(args.get(2));
        }
    }

    @Override
    public String toString()
    {
        return "Dungeon(" + this.rarity + "," + this.minAltitude + "," + this.maxAltitude + ")";
    }

    @Override
    public void spawn(IWorldGenRegion world, Random random, int x, int z)
    {
        int y = RandomHelper.numberInRange(random, this.minAltitude, this.maxAltitude);
        world.placeDungeon(random, x, y, z);
    }
}

## World Height Implementation Comparison: PG85 (1.20.1) vs Our Fork (1.21.1)

### 1. CORE DATA STRUCTURE: `OTGWorldInfo` (IDENTICAL)

Both repos have identical `OTGWorldInfo` records:

- **Fork**: `C:\Users\dylan\Desktop\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\common\common-util\src\main\java\com\pg85\otg\util\gen\OTGWorldInfo.java`

No differences. Both store `(int minY, int maxY)` with inclusive maxY and provide the same helper methods.

### 2. WHERE MIN_Y / HEIGHT ARE DEFINED (KEY DIFFERENCE)

#### PG85: `TerrainSettings.java` (line 20-21, 50-61)
**File**: `common\common-util\src\main\java\com\pg85\otg\config\settings\preset\TerrainSettings.java`

PG85 has `minY` and `height` as **direct settings** in TerrainSettings:
```java
private final int worldHeightCap;
private final int worldHeightScale;
private final int minY;        // <-- PRESENT
private final int height;      // <-- PRESENT
```
- `MIN_Y` Setting: default `0`, range `WORLD_START_MIN_Y` to `WORLD_END_MAX_Y-15`
- `HEIGHT` Setting: default `256`, range `16` to `WORLD_MAX_HEIGHT`
- Reading logic (lines 160-177): reads `MinY` from config. If `Height` exists in config, uses it directly; otherwise computes `height = worldHeightCap - minY`.

**PG85 also has `OutdatedSettings.java`** with backward-compatible settings:
- `WorldHeightCapBits` (default 7, range 5-8)
- `WorldHeightCap` (default 256, range 16-2032)
- `WorldHeightScaleBits` (default 7, range 5-8)

The reader checks for the bits-based settings first, then falls back to the direct `WorldHeightCap` value.

#### Our Fork: `TerrainSettings.java` (lines 16-17)
**File**: `common\common-util\src\main\java\com\pg85\otg\config\settings\preset\TerrainSettings.java`

Our fork does **NOT** have `minY` or `height` fields in `TerrainSettings`:
```java

private final int worldHeightScale;
// NO minY field
// NO height field
```
- Only has bits-based settings: `WORLD_HEIGHT_SCALE_BITS` (default 8, range 5-9) and `WORLD_HEIGHT_CAP_BITS` (default 9, range 5-9)
- Reading logic (lines 96-97): simply does `1 << bits` to compute worldHeightCap and worldHeightScale.
- **No direct MinY or Height setting** is read from TerrainSettings.

**Instead**, our fork moved `MIN_Y` and `HEIGHT` to `DimensionSettings.java` (lines 70-81):


And in `DimensionSettings.getDimensionSettings()` (lines 195-196), these are read independently from the DimensionPresetConfig file.

### 3. WHERE `getWorldInfo()` IS COMPUTED (CRITICAL DIFFERENCE)

#### PG85: `PresetSettings.java` (lines 51-63)
**File**: `common\common-util\src\main\java\com\pg85\otg\config\settings\preset\PresetSettings.java`
```java
case OVERWORLD -> otgWorldInfo = new OTGWorldInfo(0, 255);  // <-- 1.20.1 defaults
```

PG85 defaults OVERWORLD to `(0, 255)` -- correct for 1.20.1 (pre-1.18-style).
For OTG type, it falls through to `dimensionSettings.getMinY() + dimensionSettings.getHeight() - 1`.

#### Our Fork: `DimensionPresetSettings.java` (lines 52-64)
**File**: `common\common-util\src\main\java\com\pg85\otg\config\settings\preset\DimensionPresetSettings.java`
```java
case OVERWORLD, OTG -> otgWorldInfo = new OTGWorldInfo(-64, 319);  // <-- 1.18+ defaults
```

Our fork defaults both OVERWORLD and OTG to `(-64, 319)` -- correct for 1.18+.
For other types (like NETHER, END), it still uses hardcoded `(0, 127)`.

For custom types, it computes from `dimensionSettings.getMinY()` + `dimensionSettings.getHeight() - 1`.

**Key point**: In our fork, the `getWorldInfo()` override for OVERWORLD/OTG ignores whatever `dimensionSettings.getMinY()` and `dimensionSettings.getHeight()` actually say. The DimensionSettings file may say `MinY=-64, Height=384`, but `getWorldInfo()` hardcodes the defaults. However, since the DimensionPresetConfig.ini does write these values and the `OTGRegistryHelper` uses them for NoiseSettings, the config values ARE used for the NoiseGeneratorSettings registry. The `getWorldInfo()` override is just a fallback/safety net.

### 4. HOW WORLD HEIGHT REACHES THE CHUNK GENERATOR

#### PG85 Fabric: `OTGFabricChunkGenerator.java` (lines 95-97)

**Source of height**: `NoiseGeneratorSettings.noiseSettings()` -> `NoiseSettings.minY()` / `NoiseSettings.height()`.

#### Our Fork: `SharedOTGChunkGenerator.java` (lines 115-117)

```java
int maxY = settings.value().noiseSettings().height() + minY - 1;
```

**Identical approach**. Both derive `otgWorldInfo` from the vanilla `NoiseGeneratorSettings` -> `NoiseSettings`.

This uses the `DimensionSettings.getMinY()` and `DimensionSettings.getHeight()` values from the config file. So the chain is:

### 5. HOW WORLD HEIGHT IS USED IN `populateNoise` (KEY DIFFERENCE)

#### PG85: `OTGChunkGenerator.java` (line 427)
```java
realY = noiseY * 8 + pieceY;  // No minY offset!
```
The `populateNoise` method receives `OTGWorldInfo worldHeight` as a parameter, but the `realY` calculation starts from **0** (no minY offset). This means PG85 assumes minY=0 for the core terrain noise.

#### Our Fork: `OTGChunkGenerator.java` (line 540)
```java
realY = worldHeight.minY() + noiseY * 8 + pieceY;  // Has minY offset!
```
Our fork correctly offsets `realY` by `worldHeight.minY()`, so terrain generated at negative Y values (like -64) is placed correctly.

**This is a critical improvement in our fork.** PG85 1.20.1 always generates terrain starting from Y=0 (because 1.20.1 overworld minY IS 0). Our fork correctly handles minY=-64 for 1.18+ worlds.

Uses `TerrainSettings.getHeight()` which is the **config-level** height (e.g., 256 from config).

#### Our Fork: `OTGChunkGenerator.java` (line 281)

Uses `otgWorldInfo.getHeight()` which is the **runtime** height computed from `NoiseSettings` (e.g., 384 from -64 to 319).

This is another important difference -- our fork correctly uses the runtime-computed height rather than the config-level one, ensuring consistency between what the NoiseSettings define and what the terrain generator uses.

### 7. CHC (Custom Height Control) ARRAY SIZING

#### PG85: `BiomeTerrainSettings.java` (lines 170-184)
Uses an `Int2DoubleAVLTreeMap` (sparse) for CHC data, with an offset from `parent.getChcStart()`:

#### Our Fork: `BiomeTerrainSettings.java` (lines 247-256)

The worldHeight is passed as a parameter from `presetSettings.getWorldInfo().getHeight()`.

Our fork uses a denser representation but correctly sizes it based on world height.

#### PG85: `TerrainNoisePipeline.java`
A record that stores noise samplers and terrain parameters. The noise column generation is done inside `OTGChunkGenerator.generateNoiseColumn()` which uses `this.noisePipeline`.

#### Our Fork: `TerrainNoiseComputer.java`
A static utility class with static methods. The noise column generation is inlined in `OTGChunkGenerator.generateNoiseColumn()`. The core noise math is the same but refactored for clarity and thread safety.

### 12. KEY FINDINGS AND POTENTIAL ISSUES

1. **Our fork correctly handles minY=-64 in `populateNoise`**. This is an improvement over PG85 which would break with negative minY values. No missing functionality here.

2. **The `getWorldInfo()` hardcodes defaults for OVERWORLD/OTG**. If a user configures `MinY` and `Height` in `DimensionSettings` to something different from -64/384, `getWorldInfo()` would still return `(-64, 319)`. However, the `OTGRegistryHelper` and `SharedOTGChunkGenerator` both use `dimensionSettings.getMinY()/getHeight()` directly from the NoiseSettings, so the actual generation would use the correct values. The `getWorldInfo()` is primarily used for bounds checking in decorations, resources, custom objects, etc. **This could be a subtle bug**: if someone sets custom MinY/Height in DimensionSettings, the getWorldInfo() override would still return the hardcoded defaults.

3. **PG85's TerrainSettings has direct MinY and Height settings** (defaults 0 and 256) that are written to and read from the config. Our fork removed these from TerrainSettings and placed them in DimensionSettings with different defaults (-64 and 384). This is the correct architectural change for 1.18+ Minecraft.

4. **The `worldHeightCap` usage differs**: PG85 uses `terrainSettings.getHeight()` (config-level), our fork uses `otgWorldInfo.getHeight()` (runtime-computed). Our approach is more correct since it stays synchronized with the NoiseSettings.

5. **No critical missing PG85 functionality** was found in our fork's world height handling. The main differences are architectural (where settings live) and correctness improvements (handling negative minY).

```java
public Holder<Biome> getNoiseBiome(int i, int j, int k, Climate.Sampler sampler) {
    return resolveNoiseBiome(i, j, k);  // j (Y) IS used!

private Holder<Biome> resolveNoiseBiome(int noiseX, int noiseY, int noiseZ) {
    int surfaceBiomeId = this.getLayer().get().sample(noiseX, noiseZ);
    if (undergroundResolver != null && undergroundResolver.hasUndergroundBiomes()) {
        int worldY = noiseY << 2;  // Y coordinate IS used
        int estimatedSurfaceY = surfaceHeightEstimator != null
                ? surfaceHeightEstimator.applyAsInt(worldX, worldZ) : 64;
        int undergroundBiomeId = undergroundResolver.resolve(
            surfaceBiomeId, worldX, worldY, worldZ, estimatedSurfaceY);
        if (undergroundBiomeId >= 0) {
            // cheese cave density gating...
            Holder<Biome> underground = keyLookup.get(undergroundBiomeId);
            if (underground != null) return underground;
        }
    }
    return keyLookup.get(surfaceBiomeId);
}
```

### 4. How Underground Biomes Work in Our Fork (Not in PG85)

The pipeline works as follows:

1. **Config:** Biome configs can set `IsUndergroundBiome: true` with Y-range, priority, rarity, and surface conditions in `UndergroundBiomeSettings`.

2. **Planning:** `BiomePlanResolver` (line 85-96) excludes underground biomes from surface layer generation (isle/border/fromImage) but still assigns them OTG biome IDs.

3. **Initialization:** `SharedOTGBiomeProvider.collectPossibleBiomes()` (line 63) creates the `UndergroundBiomeResolver` from all biome data.

4. **Runtime:** `resolveNoiseBiome()` (line 93-124) in `SharedOTGBiomeProvider`:
   - Gets surface biome from 2D layer
   - Converts noise Y to world Y (`noiseY << 2`)
   - Uses `surfaceHeightEstimator` (wired up at `SharedOTGChunkGenerator.setServerLevel()` line 162-163) to estimate surface height
   - Calls `undergroundResolver.resolve()` which checks: Y range, start offset, temperature/wetness conditions, allowed/disallowed lists, priority, rarity
   - Gates through cheese cave density (if wired)

5. **Cheese Cave Density Gating:** The config setting `UndergroundBiomeCheeseDensityThreshold` exists in `NoiseCaveSettings` (line 188-195), and the biome provider has `setCheeseCaveDensity()` (line 130-132), but **`setCheeseCaveDensity` is never actually called from any chunk generator**. This means the cheese cave density gate is defined but **not yet wired up** -- underground biomes currently appear regardless of cheese cave density.

6. **Map Rendering:** `MapCommand.renderUnderground()` (lines 329-363) renders underground biomes at Y=-20 on the `/otg map` command.

---

### 5. Missing Wiring (Potential Issues in Our Fork)

**`setCheeseCaveDensity` is never called.** The method exists at:
- `C:\Users\dylan\Desktop\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\platforms\shared\src\main\java\com\pg85\otg\shared\biome\SharedOTGBiomeProvider.java` line 130

But no code calls it. The cheese cave density threshold from `NoiseCaveSettings.undergroundBiomeCheeseDensityThreshold` is parsed but never passed to the biome provider. This means:
- The cheese cave check in `resolveNoiseBiome()` (line 108-114) always gets `cheese == null`
- The `if (cheese != null)` block is skipped
- Underground biomes appear unconditionally in qualifying Y ranges, without checking if they're inside a cheese cave

---

### 6. What PG85 Has That Our Fork Also Has (Parity)

- The `BiomeInterpolator` inner class in `CachedBiomeProvider` is **identical** -- same 3D nearest-neighbor logic with Y commented out
- The biome layer system (`BiomeLayers.java`) is functionally identical
- The `ICachedBiomeProvider` interface is identical (2D: x, z only)
- The `OTGChunkGenerator` biome blending (via `blendColumnParams`) is identical -- 2D noise-biome weight blending using `BIOME_WEIGHT_TABLE` and `NOISE_WEIGHT_TABLE`
- The `getNoiseBiome(int, int, int)` signature exists in both for MC API compliance but ignores Y in PG85 while using it in ours

## 9. Aquifer Handling -- The Major Architectural Difference

### PG85 (1.20.1)
- **Aquifers are completely disabled** in the noise router (all 4 aquifer slots zeroed)

### Our Fork (1.21.1)

  2. **`OTGNoiseRouterData`** -- full vanilla noise router with **tunable aquifer noises**, used by `OTGNoiseRouterBuilder`

**However**, the `fillFromNoiseModern()` path in `SharedOTGChunkGenerator` (line 446-478) uses `OTGNoiseRouterFactory` (the zeroed-aquifer version), NOT `OTGNoiseRouterData`. So the full aquifer infrastructure in `OTGNoiseRouterData` + `NoiseCaveSettings` appears to be **a second, more advanced cave system that may not yet be fully wired in**.

## 10. The Hardcoded Parameters Issue

In `SharedOTGChunkGenerator.ensureNoiseCaveContext()` (line 480-499):
```java
ctx = OTGNoiseRouterFactory.create(
    this.internalGenerator,
    200.0,   // <-- hardcoded densityScale
    0.1,     // <-- hardcoded depthGradient
    this.settings.value(),
    registryAccess,
    this.seed
);
```

In PG85's `OTGFabricChunkGenerator.ensureNoiseCaveContext()` (line 330-349):
```java
ctx = OTGNoiseRouterFactory.create(
    this.internalGenerator,
    this.preset.getPresetConfig().getCarverSettings().getVanillaCaveDensityScale(),   // default 128.0
    this.preset.getPresetConfig().getCarverSettings().getVanillaCaveDepthGradient(),  // default 0.05
    this.settings.value(),
    registryAccess,
    this.seed
);
```

**Our fork's hardcoded values (200.0, 0.1) differ significantly from PG85's defaults (128.0, 0.05).** This means:
- densityScale 200.0 vs 128.0: terrain density resists carving more strongly near surface
- depthGradient 0.1 vs 0.05: caves open up ~2x closer to the surface (full-size caves at ~16 blocks vs ~31 blocks below terrain center)

Additionally, PG85's `VanillaCavesEnabled`, `VanillaCaveDensityScale`, and `VanillaCaveDepthGradient` config options were removed from our fork's `CarverSettings`, so users have no way to configure these values.

**Our fork adds the `UseModernCaves` flag which completely replaces OTG's carver pipeline with vanilla's, whereas PG85's `VanillaCavesEnabled` only adds noise caves on top of OTG's carvers.**

## 2. Key Differences in Resource Registration and Execution

### 2A. `readElevations()` Removed in Fork

**PG85** (`ConfigFunction.java` line 142):
```java
protected final Pair<Integer, Integer> readElevations(String minString, String maxString)
```
Returns a `Pair<Integer, Integer>` and auto-swaps min/max if inverted.

**Fork** (`ConfigFunction.java` line 136): The `readElevations()` method has been **completely removed**. All 20+ call sites were rewritten to use individual `readElevation()` calls:
```java
// PG85 pattern:
Pair<Integer, Integer> elevations = readElevations(args.get(3), args.get(4));
this.minAltitude = elevations.getFirst();
this.maxAltitude = elevations.getSecond();

// Fork pattern:
this.minAltitude = readElevation(args.get(3));
this.maxAltitude = readElevation(args.get(4));
```

Affected resources: `BasaltColumnResource`, `BoulderResource`, `CactusResource`, `DungeonResource`, `FossilResource`, `IceSpikeResource`, `LiquidResource`, `OreResource`, `PlantResource`, `ReedResource`, `SmallLakeResource`, `SurfacePatchResource`, `UnderWaterPlantResource`, `UndergroundLakeResource`, `VegetationResource`, `VeinResource`, `WellResource`.

**Impact**: The fork loses the auto-swap behavior. If min > max is provided, the fork will not correct it. This is a behavioral change.

### 2B. `BiomeResourcesManager` - Constructor Resolution

**PG85** (`BiomeResourcesManager.java` line 97-108): Only tries a single 2-parameter constructor:
```java
constructor = clazz.getConstructor(BiomeSettings.class, List.class);
```

**Fork** (`BiomeResourcesManager.java` line 75-121): Has a **fallback mechanism** that tries a 3-parameter constructor first, then falls back to 2-parameter:
```java
// Try 2-parameter first
Constructor<...> constructor = clazz.getConstructor(BiomeSettings.class, List.class);
// ... catch NoSuchMethodException -> try 3-parameter:
Constructor<...> constructor = clazz.getConstructor(BiomeSettings.class, List.class, OTGWorldInfo.class);
```

**Impact**: Fork allows resource classes to optionally accept `OTGWorldInfo` in their constructor. This infrastructure exists but is not currently used by any resource type.

### 2C. `DungeonResource` - Legacy Format Support

**PG85** (`DungeonResource.java` line 17-28): 3 args only: `Dungeon(Rarity,MinAlt,MaxAlt)`

**Fork** (`DungeonResource.java` line 16-36): Adds **4-arg legacy format** support:
```java
if (args.size() >= 4) {
    // Legacy format: Dungeon(Frequency, Rarity, MinAltitude, MaxAltitude)
    this.rarity = readRarity(args.get(1));
    this.minAltitude = readElevation(args.get(2));
    this.maxAltitude = readElevation(args.get(3));
} else {
    // New format: Dungeon(Rarity, MinAltitude, MaxAltitude)
    this.rarity = readRarity(args.get(0));
    this.minAltitude = readElevation(args.get(1));
    this.maxAltitude = readElevation(args.get(2));
}
```

### 2D. `OreResource` - API Call Difference

**PG85** (`OreResource.java` line 112):
```java
worldGenRegion.getPresetConfig().getResourceSettings().isDisableOreGen()
```

**Fork** (`OreResource.java` line 109):
```java
worldGenRegion.getConfig().getResourceSettings().isDisableOreGen()
```

This reflects a broader rename from `getPresetConfig()` to `getConfig()` throughout the codebase.

### 2E. `CustomObjectResource` - Thread Safety

**PG85** (`CustomObjectResource.java` line 21):
```java
private final List<CustomObject> objects = new ArrayList<>();
```

**Fork** (`CustomObjectResource.java` line 21):
```java
private volatile List<CustomObject> objects;
```

The fork uses **double-checked locking** with `synchronized` and `volatile` for thread-safe lazy initialization of the objects list. Objects are also stored as an **immutable copy** via `List.copyOf()`.

### 2F. `TreeResource` - Source Blocks Support (Major Feature Addition)

**PG85** (`TreeResource.java`): No sourceBlocks support. Trees can spawn anywhere.

**Fork** (`TreeResource.java` line 34, 62-77, 85-106, 129-130): Adds `sourceBlocks` field and `findTreeDefinitionEnd()` method:
```java
private final MaterialSet sourceBlocks;
// ...
// Parse optional sourceBlocks from remaining arguments
if (treeDefEnd < args.size()) {
    this.sourceBlocks = readMaterials(args, treeDefEnd);
} else {
    this.sourceBlocks = null;
}
```
The `sourceBlocks` is passed to `tree.spawnAsTree()` on line 130.

### 2G. Custom Object Resources - API Signature Changes

All custom object resource classes have **additional parameters** in the fork for `getObjectByName()` and related methods:

**PG85**: `getObjectByName(objectName, presetFolderName, otgRootFolder)`
**Fork**: `getObjectByName(objectName, presetFolderName, otgRootFolder, customObjectManager, materialReader, manager, modLoadedChecker)`

Affected classes:
- `CustomObjectResource.java` (line 38, 47-56)
- `CustomStructureResource.java` (line 70-88)
- `SaplingResource.java` (line 111-113, 136-138, 173)
- `TreeResource.java` (line 111, 146, 176, 195)

### 2H. `CustomObjectResourcesManager` - Singleton Removed, API Extended

**PG85** (`CustomObjectResourcesManager.java` line 14-20): Has static `INSTANCE` singleton pattern.

**Fork** (`CustomObjectResourcesManager.java`): Singleton removed. `getConfigFunction()` takes an additional `IMaterialReader materialReader` parameter (line 42), and `configFunction.init()` also receives it (line 80).

# Structure Generation Comparison: PG85 1.20.1 vs Our 1.21.1 Fork

## 1. ARCHITECTURE OVERVIEW

### PG85 1.20.1 Approach
- Structure generation is handled **per-platform** with platform-specific biome creation classes
- The `ForgeBiome` class (Forge-only) contains the `addVanillaStructures()` method that manually constructs and registers vanilla structures per-biome using `StructureFeatures.*` constants and `WorldGenRegistries.register()`
- Fabric has a completely separate `FabricBiome` with **no structure registration at all** -- Fabric relies entirely on tags/datapacks for structure assignment
- The Forge `MixinStructure` (108 lines) optimizes structure searches by checking biome validity before chunk loading
- Shadow chunk gen iterates over **biome structure suppliers** from `getGenerationSettings().structures()` using a hardcoded name-to-radius map

### Our Fork (1.21.1) Approach
- Structure generation is handled through a **shared module** (`platforms/shared`) with `BiomeFactory`, `SharedBiome`, `SharedShadowChunkGenerator`, and `SharedOTGChunkGenerator`
- **No per-biome structure registration exists in our fork** -- the `BiomeFactory.createOTGBiome()` method builds biomes with features/carvers but **does not add any vanilla structure starts**
- Instead, structures are handled through **Minecraft tags** via `BiomeStructureTagConfig` and `StructureTagMapper`
- The `MixinStructure` optimization from Forge (1.20.1) has been **completely removed** in our fork
- Shadow chunk gen uses a pre-built `Map<Holder<Biome>, List<Structure>>` lookup with `structure.biomes().contains()` instead of string-based name matching

## 2. KEY FILES AND DIFFERENCES

### 2A. Biome Creation -- WHERE STRUCTURES ARE ASSIGNED

**PG85 1.20.1 -- `ForgeBiome.java` (Forge-specific, 525 lines):**

- Lines 282-517: `addVanillaStructures()` method that manually creates and registers structures per-biome
- Line 133: Called from `createOTGBiome()`: `addVanillaStructures(biomeGenerationSettingsBuilder, presetConfig, biomeConfig)`

## 4. CRITICAL GAP: NO STRUCTURE REGISTRATION IN OUR FORK

The most significant difference is that **our fork has no code that actually assigns vanilla structures to biomes**. Here is the flow:

**PG85 1.20.1 (Forge)**:
1. `BiomeStructureSettings` parsed from biome config
2. `StructureSettings` parsed from preset config
3. `ForgeBiome.createOTGBiome()` -> `addVanillaStructures()` checks both configs
4. Structures are manually created and registered via `WorldGenRegistries.register()`
5. Structures added to `BiomeGenerationSettings.Builder` via `addStructureStart()`

**Our Fork 1.21.1**:
1. `BiomeStructureSettings` parsed from biome config (but **dead on Fabric/NeoForge** per TODO)
2. `StructureSettings` parsed from preset config
3. `BiomeStructureTagConfig` parsed from biome config
4. `StructureTagMapper.getStructureTags()` maps booleans to tag paths
5. `BiomeFactory.createOTGBiome()` builds biome with features/carvers **but NOT structures**
6. Structures must be assigned through **external tag files** (datapacks) that map biomes to `has_structure/*` tags

The `StructureTagMapper` is the bridge, but it is **never called during biome creation in `BiomeFactory`**. The tag injection presumably happens via a mixin or datagen system elsewhere. The biome-to-tag wiring would need to occur at the Minecraft registry level.

## 5. SUMMARY TABLE

| Aspect | PG85 1.20.1 | Our Fork 1.21.1 |
|--------|-------------|-----------------|
| **Structure assignment method** | Programmatic per-biome registration in `ForgeBiome.addVanillaStructures()` | Tag-based via `StructureTagMapper` + MC tags (no programmatic assignment in biome factory) |

| **Shadow chunk structure detection** | String-name-based with hardcoded radius map | Type-instanceof-based with pre-built biome-structure map |

| **StructureCommand** | Forge-only, 78 lines | Shared module, 104 lines, more robust |
| **Platform architecture** | Per-platform (`ForgeBiome`, `FabricBiome`) | Shared (`BiomeFactory`, `SharedBiome`) |
| **StructureCommand** location | `platforms/forge/commands/` | `platforms/shared/commands/` |
| **BiomeStructureTagConfig** | Identical | Identical |
| **StructureSettings** | Identical | Identical |
| **CustomStructureCache** | `FifoMap` based | `ThreadSafeLRUCache` based, extra constructor params |

# Main function for when the file is run directly
from io import TextIOWrapper
import regex
import os
import json

# Read file and return all lines
def readFile(filepath: str) -> list[str]:
    file : TextIOWrapper = open(filepath)
    strings : list[str] = []
    for line in file:
        # Filter out # and empty lines
        if line.startswith("#") or line == "":
            continue;
        strings.append(line.strip())
    return strings;

# A tag or tag group, representing either a standalone entry or a list in the md file
class Tag:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self._members : list[Tag] = []
        self._name : str = name

    def add_member(self, other : "Tag") -> None :
        self._members.append(other)

    def is_group(self) -> bool :
        return len(self._members) > 0

    def get_members(self) -> list["Tag"] :
        return self._members

    def get_name(self) -> str :
        return self._name

def parse_tags(strings) -> list[Tag] :
    tags : list[Tag] = []

    # limit tag names to only a-z and _
    pattern = regex.compile("[^a-z_]+")

    is_list_item : bool = False

    for line in strings:
        # lower case
        tag_str : str = line.lower()
        # list item - part of a tag group
        if line.startswith("-"):
            tag_str = tag_str[1:]
            tag_str = tag_str.strip()
            is_list_item = True
        # not a list item - standalone, or tag group
        else:
            is_list_item = False

        # no spaces
        tag_str.replace(" ", "_")

        # error if name doesn't match the pattern
        if regex.match(pattern, tag_str):
            print("Incorrect formatting of tag: "+tag_str)
            continue

        if len(tag_str) == 0:
            continue

        # make the tag object
        tag : Tag = Tag(tag_str)

        # if part of tag group, add it to it
        if is_list_item:
            group : Tag = tags[-1]
            group.add_member(tag)
        # add to the list of tags/tag groups
        else:
            tags.append(tag)
    return tags

def make_tag_file(folder : str, tag_path : str, tag : Tag) :
    # make sure folder contains separator
    if not folder.endswith(os.sep):
        folder += os.sep

    # make sure tag path includes separator
    if len(tag_path) > 0 and not tag_path.endswith(os.sep):
        tag_path += os.sep

    # replace path separator with / for tag scope
    tag_path_json = tag_path.replace(os.sep, "/")

    # open json file for writing (not appending), and creates if it doesn't exist
    out_file = open(folder + tag_path + tag.get_name() + ".json", "w+")

    # defining the json using a dictionary
    out_json = {
        'values': [
            "#c:"+tag_path_json+tag.get_name()
        ]
    }

    # convert the json dict to a printable string
    out_str = json.dumps(out_json)

    # write the json to file
    out_file.write(out_str)

    # close the file
    out_file.close()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Read file "list_of_tags.md"
    strings : list[str] = readFile("list_of_tags.md")
    tags : list[Tag] = parse_tags(strings)

    folder = "out" + os.sep

    os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)

    for tag in tags:
        if tag.is_group():
            os.makedirs(folder + tag.get_name(), exist_ok=True)
            for child in tag.get_members():
                make_tag_file(folder, tag.get_name(), child)
        else:
            make_tag_file(folder, "", tag)

## 2. What Happened -- The History

### The old implementation (now deleted)

From the conversation log file (`Concise conversation title generation.txt`, lines 29006-29122), the **previous** `WorldPresetTagsMixin` had:

```java
@Inject(method = "updateRegistryTags()V", at = @At("RETURN"))
private void addOurOwnTags(CallbackInfo ci) {
    // ... bind OTG presets to WorldPreset tags ...
    addBiomesToStructureTags(registryAccess);  // <-- THIS WAS THE KEY CALL
}

private void addBiomesToStructureTags(RegistryAccess registryAccess) {
    Map<ResourceKey<Biome>, BiomeStructureTagConfig> structureConfigs =
            SharedDimensionPresetBiomeLoader.getStructureTagConfigs();
    // ... iterate configs, call StructureTagMapper.getStructureTags() ...
    biomeRegistry.bindTags(biomeTagMap);  // <-- THE PERFORMANCE KILLER
}
```

### The performance bug

- **File:** `C:\Users\dylan\Desktop\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\docs\plans\2026-02-16-bindtags-perf-bug.md`
- `biomeRegistry.bindTags()` replaces ALL biome tag bindings, invalidating MC's `HolderSet.Named` instances that cache feature ordering.
- On NeoForge this triggers a ~60 second stall because NeoForge patches `HolderSet.Named.bind()` with invalidation callbacks that force `FeatureSorter.buildFeaturesPerStep()` to rebuild per-chunk.
- The bug doc proposes three possible fixes (Options A, B, C) but **none have been implemented**.

### The current disabled state

- **File:** `C:\Users\dylan\Desktop\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\platforms\shared\src\main\java\com\pg85\otg\shared\mixin\WorldPresetTagsMixin.java` (lines 1-14)

A well-designed pre-computed resolver:

### Layer 4: Biome Provider (`SharedOTGBiomeProvider.java`)
**File:** `C:\Users\dylan\Desktop\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\platforms\shared\src\main\java\com\pg85\otg\shared\biome\SharedOTGBiomeProvider.java` (150 lines, read in full above)

This is where everything comes together. The critical method is `resolveNoiseBiome()` (lines 93-124):

```java
private Holder<Biome> resolveNoiseBiome(int noiseX, int noiseY, int noiseZ) {
    int surfaceBiomeId = this.getLayer().get().sample(noiseX, noiseZ);

    if (undergroundResolver != null && undergroundResolver.hasUndergroundBiomes()) {
        int worldY = noiseY << 2;    // quart pos -> world pos
        int worldX = noiseX << 2;
        int worldZ = noiseZ << 2;

        int estimatedSurfaceY = surfaceHeightEstimator != null
                ? surfaceHeightEstimator.applyAsInt(worldX, worldZ)
                : 64;

        int undergroundBiomeId = undergroundResolver.resolve(
            surfaceBiomeId, worldX, worldY, worldZ, estimatedSurfaceY);
        if (undergroundBiomeId >= 0) {
            // Gate: underground biomes only in cheese cave regions
            DensityFunction cheese = this.cheeseCaveDensity;
            if (cheese != null) {            // <--- ALWAYS NULL (see below)
                double density = cheese.compute(...);
                if (density >= this.cheeseDensityThreshold) {
                    return keyLookup.get(surfaceBiomeId); // too dense, stay surface
                }
            }
            Holder<Biome> underground = keyLookup.get(undergroundBiomeId);
            if (underground != null) {
                return underground;          // <--- UNDERGROUND BIOME RETURNED
            }
        }
    }
    return keyLookup.get(surfaceBiomeId);
}
```

The resolver is created in `collectPossibleBiomes()` (line 63):
```java
this.undergroundResolver = new UndergroundBiomeResolver(iBiomes, this.seed);
```

**STATUS: WIRED.** Both `getNoiseBiome(int, int, int, Climate.Sampler)` and `getNoiseBiome(int, int, int)` delegate to `resolveNoiseBiome()`.

### Layer 5: How getNoiseBiome Gets Called With Y

The 3-argument `getNoiseBiome(noiseX, noiseY, noiseZ)` is the Minecraft `BiomeSource` override. Minecraft's `NoiseChunk` and biome sampling calls this with quart-position Y values (worldY / 4). The `resolveNoiseBiome` method converts back: `worldY = noiseY << 2`.

Key callers found:
- **`SharedOTGChunkGenerator` line 290:** `biomeManager2 = biomeManager.withDifferentSource((i, j, k) -> this.getBiomeSource().getNoiseBiome(i, j, k, randomState.sampler()))` -- used in carver pass
- **`SharedOTGChunkGenerator` line 302:** `this.getBiomeSource().getNoiseBiome(QuartPos.fromBlock(...), 0, QuartPos.fromBlock(...), randomState.sampler())` -- carver biome settings lookup (note: uses Y=0 here)
- **`PreviewWorld` line 47:** preview access

**The Y coordinate IS passed through to the resolver in the main biome source path.**

### Layer 7: Cheese Cave Density Gate (NOT WIRED -- THE ONE INCOMPLETE FEATURE)

- **Implemented** in `SharedOTGBiomeProvider` (line 130)
- **NEVER CALLED** anywhere in the entire codebase.

I searched for `.setCheeseCaveDensity(` across all `.java` files and found **zero callers**.

The `NoiseCaveSettings` config has `UndergroundBiomeCheeseDensityThreshold` (default 0.0), and `OTGNoiseRouterFactory` builds cheese cave density functions internally (line 119-121: `caveCheese = DensityFunctions.noise(...)`), but nobody passes this density function into the biome provider.

**Consequence:** Since `this.cheeseCaveDensity` is always `null`, the `if (cheese != null)` guard at line 109 is always false, and the gate is completely bypassed. Underground biomes appear **everywhere** below the surface offset, not just in cheese cave regions.

**This means underground biomes will replace surface biomes in solid rock too**, not just in actual cave openings. The biome data changes, but blocks are still placed by the 2D terrain generator using the surface biome, so it primarily affects:
- F3 debug screen biome display
- Mob spawning (biome-specific spawns)
- Biome-specific particle effects and music
- Vanilla decoration features tied to biome

### Layer 8: CachedBiomeProvider (2D only -- by design)

**File:** `C:\Users\dylan\Desktop\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\OpenTerrainGenerator-1.21.1\common\common-generator\src\main\java\com\pg85\otg\gen\biome\CachedBiomeProvider.java`

This is the internal OTG terrain generator's biome provider. Its `getNoiseBiome(int noiseX, int noiseZ)` is **2D only** -- no Y parameter. It is used by `OTGChunkGenerator` for noise column generation, surface/ground control, and carving.

**This is by design, not a bug.** The `CachedBiomeProvider` determines which blocks are placed (stone, surface blocks). +package com.pg85.otg.gen.biome;
+
+import com.pg85.otg.interfaces.IBiome;
+import com.pg85.otg.interfaces.ILayerSampler;
+import com.pg85.otg.interfaces.IUndergroundBiomeMap;
+import com.pg85.otg.util.ChunkCoordinate;
+import com.pg85.otg.util.gen.OTGWorldInfo;
+import it.unimi.dsi.fastutil.ints.IntArrayList;
+import it.unimi.dsi.fastutil.ints.IntList;
+
+import java.util.function.ToIntBiFunction;
+
+/**
+ * Pre-computed per-chunk map of underground biome ids at quart resolution
+ * (4x4 columns in XZ, quart steps in Y). Built once via {@link #build}, then read
+ * cheaply per-block by block placement and per-region by decoration.
+ */
+public final class UndergroundBiomeMap implements IUndergroundBiomeMap {
+
+    private final IBiome[] biomesById;
+    private final int originBlockX;
+    private final int originBlockZ;
+    private final int minY;
+    private final int quartsY;
+    private final int[] ids; // index: (qx*4 + qz) * quartsY + qy ; value: ug id or -1
+    private final float[] caveScales; // flat: ((qx*4+qz)*quartsY + qy)*CAVE_SCALE_COUNT + caveType; null = all 1.0
+    private final boolean empty;
+
+    private UndergroundBiomeMap(IBiome[] biomesById, int originBlockX, int originBlockZ,
+                               int minY, int quartsY, int[] ids, float[] caveScales, boolean empty) {
+        this.biomesById = biomesById;
+        this.originBlockX = originBlockX;
+        this.originBlockZ = originBlockZ;
+        this.minY = minY;
+        this.quartsY = quartsY;
+        this.ids = ids;
+        this.caveScales = caveScales;
+        this.empty = empty;
+    }
+
+    private static final UndergroundBiomeMap EMPTY =
+            new UndergroundBiomeMap(new IBiome[0], 0, 0, 0, 0, new int[0], null, true);
+
+    /** Shared empty map (no underground biomes) — used for shadow/height-probe chunks. */
+    public static UndergroundBiomeMap empty() {
+        return EMPTY;
+    }
+
+    public static UndergroundBiomeMap build(UndergroundBiomeResolver resolver, ILayerSampler sampler,
+                                            ToIntBiFunction<Integer, Integer> heightEstimator,
+                                            ChunkCoordinate chunkCoord, OTGWorldInfo worldInfo,
+                                            IBiome[] biomesById) {
+        int originBlockX = chunkCoord.getBlockX();
+        int originBlockZ = chunkCoord.getBlockZ();
+        int minY = worldInfo.minY();
+        int quartsY = (worldInfo.maxY() - minY + 1 + 3) / 4;
+        int[] ids = new int[16 * quartsY];
+        float[] caveScales = null; // lazily allocated (filled with 1.0) on first non-default quart
+        boolean empty = true;
+
+        for (int qx = 0; qx < 4; qx++) {
+            for (int qz = 0; qz < 4; qz++) {
+                int worldX = originBlockX + (qx << 2);
+                int worldZ = originBlockZ + (qz << 2);
+                int surfaceId = sampler.sample(worldX >> 2, worldZ >> 2);
+                int estSurfaceY = heightEstimator != null
+                        ? heightEstimator.applyAsInt(Integer.valueOf(worldX), Integer.valueOf(worldZ))
+                        : 64;
+                int base = (qx * 4 + qz) * quartsY;
+                for (int qy = 0; qy < quartsY; qy++) {
+                    int worldY = minY + (qy << 2);
+                    int id = resolver.resolve(surfaceId, worldX, worldY, worldZ, estSurfaceY);
+                    ids[base + qy] = id;
+                    if (id >= 0) empty = false;
+                    float[] scales = resolver.resolveCaveScales(surfaceId, worldX, worldY, worldZ, estSurfaceY);
+                    if (notAllOnes(scales)) {
+                        if (caveScales == null) {
+                            caveScales = new float[16 * quartsY * CAVE_SCALE_COUNT];
+                            java.util.Arrays.fill(caveScales, 1.0f);
+                        }
+                        System.arraycopy(scales, 0, caveScales, (base + qy) * CAVE_SCALE_COUNT, CAVE_SCALE_COUNT);
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        return new UndergroundBiomeMap(biomesById, originBlockX, originBlockZ, minY, quartsY, ids, caveScales, empty);
+    }
+
+    @Override
+    public int getUndergroundBiomeId(int worldX, int worldY, int worldZ) {
+        if (this.empty) return -1;
+        int qx = (worldX - this.originBlockX) >> 2;
+        int qz = (worldZ - this.originBlockZ) >> 2;
+        if (qx < 0 || qx > 3 || qz < 0 || qz > 3) return -1;
+        int qy = (worldY - this.minY) >> 2;
+        if (qy < 0 || qy >= this.quartsY) return -1;
+        return this.ids[(qx * 4 + qz) * this.quartsY + qy];
+    }
+
+    @Override
+    public float caveScaleAt(int worldX, int worldY, int worldZ, int caveType) {
+        if (this.caveScales == null) return 1.0f;
+        int qx = (worldX - this.originBlockX) >> 2;
+        int qz = (worldZ - this.originBlockZ) >> 2;
+        if (qx < 0 || qx > 3 || qz < 0 || qz > 3) return 1.0f;
+        int qy = (worldY - this.minY) >> 2;
+        if (qy < 0 || qy >= this.quartsY) return 1.0f;
+        return this.caveScales[((qx * 4 + qz) * this.quartsY + qy) * CAVE_SCALE_COUNT + caveType];
+    }
+
+    private static boolean notAllOnes(float[] s) {
+        for (float v : s) {
+            if (v != 1.0f) return true;

# Cave System Comparison: `origin/1.21.5` vs `main`

## 1. Architectural Overview -- Two Fundamentally Different Approaches

The two branches implement the cave system using completely different architectures:

### `origin/1.21.5` -- "Inline carveWithNoise" architecture
- **Cave carving happens directly in `SharedOTGChunkGenerator`** via a `carveWithNoise()` method called from `fillFromNoise()`.
- The `OTGNoiseRouterData` class builds the full vanilla-like noise router (including aquifers, ore veins, climate noise, terrain shape -- everything).
- A separate `caveDensityForCarving()` method produces terrain-independent cave density (no `slopedCheese`, no `rangeChoice`).
- `initCaveComponents()` in `SharedOTGChunkGenerator` builds a cave-only `RandomState` from a custom `NoiseRouter` that wires the individual cave components into the router slots, then extracts the resolved density functions.
- The `carveWithNoise()` loop iterates block-by-block, evaluates `caveDensity.compute()`, and carves air. It has surface suppression and breakthrough logic.
- There is also a `RegionScaleFunction` mechanism for underground biome-aware cave scaling.

### `main` -- "NoiseChunk + OTGNoiseRouterFactory + OTGNoiseCaveFiller" architecture
- **Cave carving happens via Minecraft's `NoiseChunk` system.** The `fillFromNoiseModern()` method creates a `NoiseChunk` using a custom `NoiseGeneratorSettings` with an `OTGNoiseRouterFactory`-built router, then calls `OTGNoiseCaveFiller.fill()` to write blocks.
- `OTGNoiseRouterFactory.create()` builds a lightweight router that only has cave density components (no aquifer noise, no climate, no terrain shape). All aquifer and lava slots are `DensityFunctions.zero()`.
- `OTGNoiseCaveFiller.fill()` walks the NoiseChunk cell-by-cell using `noiseChunk.updateForY/X/Z()` and the vanilla `getInterpolatedState()` to place blocks, including aquifer fluid scheduling.
- The old `caveDensityForCarving()` / `caveDensityComponentsForCarving()` code still exists in `OTGNoiseRouterData` on main but is **not used** by the new pipeline.
- `SharedOTGChunkGenerator` on main has no `carveWithNoise()` method at all.

---

## 2. Commit `993da3541` -- The Aquifer Fix

**File changed:** `platforms/fabric/src/main/java/com/pg85/otg/fabric/gen/noise/OTGNoiseRouterFactory.java`

This commit is on the `origin/1.21.5` branch and modifies a **Fabric-platform-specific** `OTGNoiseRouterFactory.java` (path: `platforms/fabric/...`). It is NOT the same file as the shared `OTGNoiseRouterFactory.java` on `main`.

**What it changed (3 key diffs):**

1. **Aquifer noise slots in the NoiseRouter** -- Changed from `DensityFunctions.zero()` to actual vanilla aquifer noises:
   ```java
   // BEFORE (all zeros -- aquifers disabled):
   DensityFunctions.zero(), // barrierNoise
   DensityFunctions.zero(), // fluidLevelFloodednessNoise
   DensityFunctions.zero(), // fluidLevelSpreadNoise
   DensityFunctions.zero(), // lavaNoise

   // AFTER (vanilla aquifer noises enabled):
   DensityFunctions.noise(noises.getOrThrow(Noises.AQUIFER_BARRIER), 0.5),
   DensityFunctions.noise(noises.getOrThrow(Noises.AQUIFER_FLUID_LEVEL_FLOODEDNESS), 0.67),
   DensityFunctions.noise(noises.getOrThrow(Noises.AQUIFER_FLUID_LEVEL_SPREAD), 0.7142857142857143),
   DensityFunctions.noise(noises.getOrThrow(Noises.AQUIFER_LAVA)),
   ```

2. **`aquifersEnabled` flag** -- Changed from `false` to `true` in the `NoiseGeneratorSettings` constructor.

3. **Updated Javadoc** to explain the rationale: "Without aquifers every cave below the water level floods."

**Impact:** This fix is critical. Without it, `NoiseChunk` uses `Aquifer.createDisabled(fluidPicker)` and every carved block below sea level becomes water, creating one giant flooded underground. With aquifers enabled, only vanilla-style aquifer pockets generate water/lava underground, keeping caves mostly dry.

**Status on `main`:** This fix is NOT needed on `main` because `main`'s `OTGNoiseRouterFactory` uses `NoiseChunk`-based filling. However, `main`'s `OTGNoiseRouterFactory` still has all-zero aquifer slots and `aquifersEnabled=false`, which means **the same flooding bug exists on `main`** when `UseModernCaves=true`.

5. Creates a `NoiseGeneratorSettings` with aquifers **disabled** (`false, false`)
6. Creates `RandomState` from those settings
7. Extracts the resolved density functions from the processed router
8. Creates `SimplexNoise` for breakthrough logic

## 7. What Needs to Be Done for the Most Functional Cave System

### Critical Bug Fix: Aquifer Flooding

**The `main` branch has the same aquifer flooding bug that commit 993da3541 fixed on `origin/1.21.5`.** In `OTGNoiseRouterFactory.create()`:

```java
// Line 49-53 on main -- aquifer slots are ALL ZERO:
NoiseRouter router = new NoiseRouter(
    DensityFunctions.zero(),  // barrierNoise       <-- BUG
    DensityFunctions.zero(),  // fluidLevelFloodednessNoise  <-- BUG
    DensityFunctions.zero(),  // fluidLevelSpreadNoise  <-- BUG
    DensityFunctions.zero(),  // lavaNoise          <-- BUG
    ...
);

// Line 76 on main -- aquifers disabled:
false,  // aquifersEnabled    <-- BUG
```

**Fix needed:** Change these to vanilla aquifer noises and set `aquifersEnabled = true`, exactly as commit 993da3541 did on `origin/1.21.5`. Without this, any modern cave below sea level will be completely flooded.

### Differences in Cheese Constant and Pillar Threshold

On `origin/1.21.5`'s `caveDensityForCarving`:
- Cheese constant: `0.35` (smaller cheese caves than vanilla's `0.27`)
- Pillar threshold: `0.15` (far fewer pillars than vanilla's `0.03`)

On `main`'s `OTGNoiseRouterFactory`, the final density is built from vanilla data functions (`overworld/caves/entrances`, `overworld/caves/noodle`, `overworld/caves/spaghetti_2d`, etc.) which use vanilla's `0.27` and `0.03` values.

### CarveWithNoise Surface Suppression vs OTGNoiseCaveFiller

The `origin/1.21.5` branch's `carveWithNoise()` has sophisticated surface-relative features that `main`'s `OTGNoiseCaveFiller` lacks:
- **Surface suppression range** (configurable, default 30 blocks) -- caves fade out near the surface
- **Breakthrough noise** (simplex noise at configurable scale/chance) -- some columns allow caves to breach the surface
- **Block-by-block evaluation** of the cave density function with per-block control

`main`'s `OTGNoiseCaveFiller.fill()` relies entirely on the NoiseChunk's built-in evaluation, which gives the vanilla aquifer/fluid behavior but less fine-grained surface control.

### Summary of What to Merge/Port

1. **Aquifer fix** (commit 993da3541) -- Adapt the four aquifer noise slots and `true` flag into `main`'s `OTGNoiseRouterFactory.create()`. This is the most critical fix.

2. **Surface suppression + breakthrough** -- The `carveWithNoise()` logic from `origin/1.21.5` could be ported into `main`'s pipeline to add surface-relative cave behavior. The config settings already exist in `NoiseCaveSettings` on both branches.

3. **Cheese/pillar tuning** -- The `0.35` cheese constant and `0.15` pillar threshold from `origin/1.21.5` produce visually different caves. Decide which values to use.

4. **Region scaling** (`RegionScaleFunction`) -- Only on `origin/1.21.5`. Allows underground biome maps to modulate cave density per-region.

5. **API version differences** (1.21.5 vs 1.21.1) -- Method signatures for `applyCarvers`, `createStructures`, `getOrCreateCarvingMask` differ and cannot be directly merged.

    }

    public record OTGNoiseCaveContext(
            NoiseGeneratorSettings runtimeSettings,
            RandomState randomState,
            Aquifer.FluidPicker fluidPicker
    ) {
    }

    public static OTGNoiseCaveContext create(
            OTGChunkGenerator internalGenerator,
            double densityScale,
            double depthGradient,
            NoiseGeneratorSettings registeredSettings,
            RegistryAccess registryAccess,
            long seed
    ) {
        HolderGetter<DensityFunction> functions =
                registryAccess.lookupOrThrow(Registries.DENSITY_FUNCTION);
        HolderGetter<NormalNoise.NoiseParameters> noises =
                registryAccess.lookupOrThrow(Registries.NOISE);

        DensityFunction otgTerrain = new OTGTerrainDensityFunction(internalGenerator, densityScale);
        DensityFunction depthProxy = new OTGDepthProxyFunction(internalGenerator, depthGradient);
        DensityFunction finalDensity = finalDensity(otgTerrain, depthProxy, functions, noises);

        NoiseRouter router = new NoiseRouter(
                DensityFunctions.zero(),
                DensityFunctions.zero(),
                DensityFunctions.zero(),
                DensityFunctions.zero(),
                DensityFunctions.zero(),
                DensityFunctions.zero(),
                DensityFunctions.zero(),
                DensityFunctions.zero(),
                DensityFunctions.zero(),
                DensityFunctions.zero(),
                otgTerrain,
                finalDensity,
                DensityFunctions.zero(),
                DensityFunctions.zero(),
                DensityFunctions.zero()
        );

        NoiseGeneratorSettings runtimeSettings = new NoiseGeneratorSettings(
                registeredSettings.noiseSettings(),
                registeredSettings.defaultBlock(),
                registeredSettings.defaultFluid(),
                router,
                registeredSettings.surfaceRule(),
                registeredSettings.spawnTarget(),
                registeredSettings.seaLevel(),
                registeredSettings.disableMobGeneration(),
                false,
                false,
                registeredSettings.useLegacyRandomSource()
        );

        return new OTGNoiseCaveContext(
                runtimeSettings,
                RandomState.create(runtimeSettings, noises, seed),
                new OTGFluidPicker(internalGenerator)
        );
    }

    private static DensityFunction finalDensity(
            DensityFunction slopedCheese,
            DensityFunction depthProxy,
            HolderGetter<DensityFunction> functions,
            HolderGetter<NormalNoise.NoiseParameters> noises
    ) {
        DensityFunction entrances = getFunction(functions, "overworld/caves/entrances");
        DensityFunction noodle = getFunction(functions, "overworld/caves/noodle");

        DensityFunction entrancesOnly = DensityFunctions.min(
                slopedCheese,
                DensityFunctions.mul(DensityFunctions.constant(5.0), entrances)
        );
        DensityFunction caved = DensityFunctions.rangeChoice(
                depthProxy, -1000000.0, ENTRANCES_THRESHOLD,
                entrancesOnly,
                DensityFunctions.min(slopedCheese, underground(depthProxy, entrances, functions, noises))
        );
        return DensityFunctions.min(postProcess(caved), noodle);
    }

    private static DensityFunction underground(
            DensityFunction depthProxy,
            DensityFunction entrances,
            HolderGetter<DensityFunction> functions,
            HolderGetter<NormalNoise.NoiseParameters> noises
    ) {
        DensityFunction spaghetti2d = getFunction(functions, "overworld/caves/spaghetti_2d");
        DensityFunction spaghettiRoughness = getFunction(functions, "overworld/caves/spaghetti_roughness_function");
        DensityFunction caveLayer = DensityFunctions.noise(noises.getOrThrow(Noises.CAVE_LAYER), 8.0);
        DensityFunction layerBulge = DensityFunctions.mul(DensityFunctions.constant(4.0), caveLayer.square());
        DensityFunction caveCheese = DensityFunctions.noise(noises.getOrThrow(Noises.CAVE_CHEESE), 0.6666666666666666);
        DensityFunction cheese = DensityFunctions.add(
                DensityFunctions.add(DensityFunctions.constant(0.27), caveCheese).clamp(-1.0, 1.0),
                DensityFunctions.add(
                        DensityFunctions.constant(1.5),
                        DensityFunctions.mul(DensityFunctions.constant(-0.64), depthProxy)
                ).clamp(0.0, 0.5)
        );
        DensityFunction caves = DensityFunctions.min(
                DensityFunctions.min(DensityFunctions.add(layerBulge, cheese), entrances),
                DensityFunctions.add(spaghetti2d, spaghettiRoughness)
        );
        DensityFunction pillars = getFunction(functions, "overworld/caves/pillars");
        DensityFunction activePillars = DensityFunctions.rangeChoice(
                pillars, -1000000.0, 0.03, DensityFunctions.constant(-1000000.0), pillars
        );
        return DensityFunctions.max(caves, activePillars);
    }

    private static DensityFunction postProcess(DensityFunction density) {
        DensityFunction blended = DensityFunctions.blendDensity(density);
        return DensityFunctions.mul(DensityFunctions.interpolated(blended), DensityFunctions.constant(0.64)).squeeze();
    }

    private static DensityFunction getFunction(HolderGetter<DensityFunction> functions, String name) {
        Holder<DensityFunction> holder = functions.getOrThrow(
                ResourceKey.create(Registries.DENSITY_FUNCTION, ResourceLocation.parse(name))
        );
        return new DensityFunctions.HolderHolder(holder);
    }
}

        carverSettingsBuilder.useModernCaves(reader.getSetting(USE_MODERN_CAVES));
        carverSettingsBuilder.aquifersEnabled(reader.getSetting(AQUIFERS_ENABLED));
        carverSettingsBuilder.oreVeinsEnabled(reader.getSetting(ORE_VEINS_ENABLED));
        carverSettingsBuilder.legacyCarversEnabled(reader.getSetting(LEGACY_CARVERS_ENABLED));

        carverSettingsBuilder.cavesEnabled(reader.getSetting(CAVES_ENABLED));
        carverSettingsBuilder.caveFrequency(reader.getSetting(CAVE_FREQUENCY));
        carverSettingsBuilder.caveRarity(reader.getSetting(CAVE_RARITY));
        carverSettingsBuilder.evenCaveDistribution(reader.getSetting(EVEN_CAVE_DISTRIBUTION));
        carverSettingsBuilder.caveMinAltitude(reader.getSetting(CAVE_MIN_ALTITUDE));
        carverSettingsBuilder.caveMaxAltitude(reader.getSetting(CAVE_MAX_ALTITUDE));
        carverSettingsBuilder.caveSystemFrequency(reader.getSetting(CAVE_SYSTEM_FREQUENCY));
        carverSettingsBuilder.individualCaveRarity(reader.getSetting(INDIVIDUAL_CAVE_RARITY));
        carverSettingsBuilder.caveSystemPocketChance(reader.getSetting(CAVE_SYSTEM_POCKET_CHANCE));
        carverSettingsBuilder.caveSystemPocketMinSize(reader.getSetting(CAVE_SYSTEM_POCKET_MIN_SIZE));
        carverSettingsBuilder.caveSystemPocketMaxSize(reader.getSetting(CAVE_SYSTEM_POCKET_MAX_SIZE));

        carverSettingsBuilder.ravinesEnabled(reader.getSetting(RAVINES_ENABLED));
        carverSettingsBuilder.ravineRarity(reader.getSetting(RAVINE_RARITY));
        carverSettingsBuilder.ravineMinLength(reader.getSetting(RAVINE_MIN_LENGTH));
        carverSettingsBuilder.ravineMaxLength(reader.getSetting(RAVINE_MAX_LENGTH));
        carverSettingsBuilder.ravineDepth(reader.getSetting(RAVINE_DEPTH));
        carverSettingsBuilder.ravineMinAltitude(reader.getSetting(RAVINE_MIN_ALTITUDE));
        carverSettingsBuilder.ravineMaxAltitude(reader.getSetting(RAVINE_MAX_ALTITUDE));
        return carverSettingsBuilder.fixSettings().build();
    }

    @Override
    public String getSectionName() {
        return "Carver Settings";
    }

    public static class CarverSettingsBuilder {
        public CarverSettingsBuilder fixSettings() {
            checkCaveMaxAltitude();
            checkCaveSystemPocketMaxSize();
            checkRavineMaxAltitude();
            checkRavineMaxLength();
            return this;
        }
        private void checkCaveMaxAltitude() {
            caveMaxAltitude = Math.max(caveMaxAltitude, caveMinAltitude);
        }
        private void checkCaveSystemPocketMaxSize() {
            caveSystemPocketMaxSize = Math.max(caveSystemPocketMaxSize, caveSystemPocketMinSize);
        }
        private void checkRavineMaxAltitude() {
            ravineMaxAltitude = Math.max(ravineMaxAltitude, ravineMinAltitude);
        }
        private void checkRavineMaxLength() {
            ravineMaxLength = Math.max(ravineMaxLength, ravineMinLength);
        }
    }

    public abstract Boolean checkHasVanillaStructureWithoutLoading(ServerLevel level, ChunkCoordinate chunkCoord);

    public abstract int getHighestBlockYInUnloadedChunk(int x, int z, boolean findSolid, boolean findLiquid, boolean ignoreLiquid, boolean ignoreSnow);

    public abstract LocalMaterialData getMaterialInUnloadedChunk(int x, int y, int z);

    // --- Fields ---

    protected final Holder<NoiseGeneratorSettings> settings;
    protected final IOTGBiomeProvider otgBiomeProvider;
    protected final OTGChunkGenerator internalGenerator;
    protected final DimensionPreset preset;

    protected final NoiseBasedChunkGenerator horribleDelegateForCarvers;
    protected Aquifer.FluidPicker globalFluidPicker = null;
    protected final OTGChunkDecorator chunkDecorator;
    protected volatile OTGNoiseRouterFactory.OTGNoiseCaveContext noiseCaveContext = null;
    protected final boolean useModernWorldgen;
    protected CustomStructureCache structureCache = null;
    protected Long seed = 0L;
    protected ServerLevel serverLevel = null;
    protected final OTGWorldInfo otgWorldInfo;

    // --- Timing counters (thread-safe) ---
    private static final int TIMING_LOG_INTERVAL = 50;
    private final AtomicInteger fillNoiseCount = new AtomicInteger();
    private final AtomicLong fillNoiseTotalNs = new AtomicLong();
    private final AtomicLong populateNoiseTotalNs = new AtomicLong();
    private final AtomicInteger carversCount = new AtomicInteger();
    private final AtomicLong carversTotalNs = new AtomicLong();
    private final AtomicInteger structuresCount = new AtomicInteger();
    private final AtomicLong structuresTotalNs = new AtomicLong();
    private final AtomicInteger decorationCount = new AtomicInteger();
    private final AtomicLong decorationTotalNs = new AtomicLong();
    private final AtomicLong superDecorationTotalNs = new AtomicLong();

    // --- Constructor ---

    protected SharedOTGChunkGenerator(
            IOTGBiomeProvider otgBiomeProvider,
            Holder<NoiseGeneratorSettings> settings,
            Registry<Biome> biomeRegistry
    ) {
        super((net.minecraft.world.level.biome.BiomeSource) otgBiomeProvider);
        this.otgBiomeProvider = otgBiomeProvider;
        this.settings = settings;
        int minY = settings.value().noiseSettings().minY();
        int maxY = settings.value().noiseSettings().height() + minY - 1;
        this.otgWorldInfo = new OTGWorldInfo(minY, maxY);
        this.internalGenerator = new OTGChunkGenerator(
                OTG.getEngine().getDimensionPresetLoader().getDimensionPresetByFolderName(otgBiomeProvider.getPresetFolderName()),
                (com.pg85.otg.interfaces.ILayerSource) otgBiomeProvider,
